    S * (E_J / eV) ^ 2 / (6 * (mc2_J / eV)) - E_J / eV + ΔU_J / eV = 0 := by
  have key : S * (E_J / eV) ^ 2 / (6 * (mc2_J / eV)) - E_J / eV + ΔU_J / eV
      = (S * E_J ^ 2 / (6 * mc2_J) - E_J + ΔU_J) / eV := by
    field_simp

  rw [key]
  have h2 := hh
  unfold ThresholdBalance at h2
  rw [h2]
  simp

nodes.title: Physics formalization target
nodes.statement: The assigned autoformalize agent should translate this physics problem into Lean declarations in the covered file, with theorem and lemma proof bodies written as `by sorry`.
nodes.proof_tex: This is an autoformalization task, not a proof task. Produce faithful statements that can later be proved without weakening the source contract.

nodes.title: Half-cylindrical mirror and threshold bookkeeping
nodes.statement:
The physical setup of Figures 2c--2e, packaged as one structure: the mirror
radius $R$ (a length) with its positivity certificate; the reflection-count
staircase $N_{\mathrm{refl}} : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{N}$ of Figure~2e, defined
for every transverse coordinate $x$; and the threshold sequence
$x_{N\mathrm{At}} : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ ($0$-based, $0 < x_{N\mathrm{At}}\,n < R$)
whose general term for the positive integer $N$ is recorded at index $N - 1$.
Bundled Figure-2e readouts and the governing law, all assumption-side:
mirror symmetry $N_{\mathrm{refl}}(-x) = N_{\mathrm{refl}}(x)$; the axial ray
reflected exactly once ($N_{\mathrm{refl}}\,0 = 1$); the threshold property
(below $|x| < x_{N\mathrm{At}}\,n$ the count is at most $n + 1$, and from the
edge onward within $(-R, R)$ it exceeds $n + 1$); the edge value
$N_{\mathrm{refl}}(x_{N\mathrm{At}}\,n) = n + 2$ (the rim impact of
Figure~2e's filled dots counts as a reflection); and the geometric
reflection-count law (specular reflection on the circular mirror makes the
impact polar angles the odd multiples $\alpha, 3\alpha, 5\alpha, \dots$, so
for $\alpha \in (0, \pi/2]$ the count $N_{\mathrm{refl}}(R\cos\alpha)$ is the
number of odd multiples $(2k+1)\alpha$ not exceeding $\pi$, rim impact
included).  No threshold value is fixed by any field: the closed forms are
derived conclusion-side below.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure HalfCylindricalMirror where

  R : ℝ

  R_pos : 0 < R

  N_refl : ℝ → ℕ

  x_NAt : ℕ → ℝ

  x_NAt_pos : ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < x_NAt n

  x_NAt_lt_R : ∀ n : ℕ, x_NAt n < R

  N_refl_abs : ∀ x : ℝ, N_refl (-x) = N_refl x

  N_refl_zero : N_refl 0 = 1

  x_NAt_is_threshold : ∀ n : ℕ,
    (∀ x : ℝ, |x| < x_NAt n → N_refl x ≤ n + 1) ∧
    (∀ x : ℝ, x_NAt n ≤ |x| → |x| < R → n + 1 < N_refl x)

  x_NAt_edge_count : ∀ n : ℕ, N_refl (x_NAt n) = n + 2

  reflection_count_law : ∀ α : ℝ, α ∈ Set.Ioc 0 (π / 2) →
    N_refl (R * cos α) = Set.ncard {k : ℕ | (2 * (k : ℝ) + 1) * α ≤ π}

nodes.title: The limiting ray undergoes exactly $N + 1$ reflections
nodes.statement:
For the ray whose first impact has polar angle $\alpha = \pi/(2N+1)$ across
the threshold ($N = n + 1$ in $0$-based indexing), the impact points are the
odd multiples $\pi/(2N+1), 3\pi/(2N+1), \dots, (2N+1)\pi/(2N+1) = \pi$, so
its $(N+1)$-st impact lands exactly on the rim and
$N_{\mathrm{refl}}\bigl(R\cos(\pi/(2N+1))\bigr) = N + 1$ ($n + 2$, $0$-based).
nodes.proof_tex:
By the bundled reflection-count law, $N_{\mathrm{refl}}(R\cos\alpha)$ counts
the odd multiples of $\alpha = \pi/(2N+1)$ not exceeding $\pi$; these are
exactly $(2k+1)\pi/(2N+1)$ for $0 \le k \le N$, i.e.\ $N + 1$ impacts, the
last being the rim impact, which counts.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem limiting_ray_reflection_count (n : ℕ) :
    s.N_refl (s.R * cos (π / (2 * ((n : ℝ) + 1) + 1))) = n + 2 := by
  sorry

nodes.title: The two recorded forms agree
nodes.statement:
Cosine--sine bridge (recorded answer, both forms conclusion-side): for the
positive integer $N$ ($N = n + 1$, $0$-based),
\[
R\sin\!\frac{(2N-1)\pi}{4N+2} \;=\; R\cos\!\frac{\pi}{2N+1} .
\]
nodes.proof_tex:
Pure trigonometry: $(2N-1)\pi/(4N+2) = \pi/2 - \pi/(2N+1)$ and
$\sin(\pi/2 - \theta) = \cos\theta$.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem threshold_forms_agree (n : ℕ) :
    s.R * sin ((2 * ((n : ℝ) + 1) - 1) * π / (4 * ((n : ℝ) + 1) + 2)) =
      s.R * cos (π / (2 * ((n : ℝ) + 1) + 1)) := by
  sorry

nodes.title: A.1 answer, cosine form
nodes.statement:
\textbf{(Target, T2-A1.)}  The threshold sequence of Figure~2e is
\[
x_N = R\cos\!\frac{\pi}{2N+1}
\]
for the positive integer $N$ ($x_{N\mathrm{At}}\,n$ with $N = n + 1$,
$0$-based).  This is the recorded answer in cosine form; the value appears
only conclusion-side (it is no field of the structure).
nodes.proof_tex:
Write $x_* = R\cos(\pi/(2N+1))$.  By the limiting-ray count, the ray at
$x_*$ undergoes $N + 1$ reflections, so $x_*$ sits on the next plateau and
the defining threshold property of $x_{N\mathrm{At}}\,n$ (at most $n + 1$
below the edge, more than $n + 1$ from the edge on, within $(-R, R)$)
identifies $x_{N\mathrm{At}}\,n = x_*$.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem threshold_x_N_cos (n : ℕ) :
    s.x_NAt n = s.R * cos (π / (2 * ((n : ℝ) + 1) + 1)) := by
  sorry

nodes.title: A.1 answer, sine form
nodes.statement:
\textbf{(Target, T2-A1.)}  The threshold sequence of Figure~2e is
\[
x_N = R\sin\!\frac{(2N-1)\pi}{4N+2}
\]
for the positive integer $N$ ($x_{N\mathrm{At}}\,n$ with $N = n + 1$,
$0$-based).  This is the recorded answer in sine form; the value appears
only conclusion-side.
nodes.proof_tex: Chain the cosine-form threshold with the forms-agree bridge.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem threshold_x_N_sin (n : ℕ) :
    s.x_NAt n =
      s.R * sin ((2 * ((n : ℝ) + 1) - 1) * π / (4 * ((n : ℝ) + 1) + 2)) := by
  sorry

nodes.title: A.1 answer, combined
nodes.statement:
\textbf{(Target, T2-A1.)}  Both closed forms of the general threshold agree:
\[
x_N = R\sin\!\frac{(2N-1)\pi}{4N+2} = R\cos\!\frac{\pi}{2N+1}
\]
for the positive integer $N$ ($N = n + 1$, $0$-based).  Conclusion-side
only: the conjunction of the sine- and cosine-form recorded answers.
nodes.proof_tex: Conjoin the sine-form and cosine-form target theorems.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem threshold_x_N (n : ℕ) :
    s.x_NAt n =
        s.R * sin ((2 * ((n : ℝ) + 1) - 1) * π / (4 * ((n : ℝ) + 1) + 2)) ∧
      s.x_NAt n = s.R * cos (π / (2 * ((n : ℝ) + 1) + 1)) := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Physics formalization target
nodes.statement: The assigned autoformalize agent should translate this physics problem into Lean declarations in the covered file, with theorem and lemma proof bodies written as `by sorry`.
nodes.proof_tex: This is an autoformalization task, not a proof task. Produce faithful statements that can later be proved without weakening the source contract.

nodes.title: Cross-sectional vector
nodes.statement:
Points and vectors of the transverse cross-sectional plane: pairs of real
coordinates carrying the dimension of length.  The system of Figure~2f is
translationally invariant along the cylinder axes, so a single cross-section
captures all the geometry.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source: abbrev Vec : Type := ℝ × ℝ

nodes.title: Euclidean norm of a cross-sectional vector
nodes.statement:
The Euclidean norm $\mathrm{vnorm}(v) = \sqrt{v_1^2 + v_2^2}$ of a
cross-sectional vector: a length (dimensionless for unit direction vectors).
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source: def vnorm (v : Vec) : ℝ := Real.sqrt (v.1 ^ 2 + v.2 ^ 2)

nodes.title: Non-vertical line in the cross-section
nodes.statement:
A non-vertical line $Y = m X + b$ in the cross-sectional plane, recorded by
its slope $m$ (dimensionless) and intercept $b$ (a length).
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure Line2D where
  m : ℝ
  b : ℝ

nodes.title: Signed point-to-line distance
nodes.statement:
The signed distance from the point $q$ to the line $r$,
$\mathrm{distToLine}\,r\,q = (q_2 - m_r q_1 - b_r)/\sqrt{m_r^2 + 1}$: a
length; it vanishes exactly when $q$ lies on $r$.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
def distToLine (r : Line2D) (q : Vec) : ℝ :=
  (q.2 - r.m * q.1 - r.b) / Real.sqrt (r.m ^ 2 + 1)

nodes.title: Cooker dimensionful parameters
nodes.statement:
The dimensionful parameters of the cooker of Figure~2f: the mirror radius
$R$ and the container radius $a$, both lengths and both certified positive
by bundled fields $0 < R$ and $0 < a$.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure CookerParams where
  R : ℝ
  a : ℝ
  hR : 0 < R
  ha : 0 < a

nodes.title: Cooker specular bookkeeping
nodes.statement:
The single-bounce ray bookkeeping of the Figure-2f cooker: the mirror centre
$C = (0,0)$, the container centre $A = (0, -R/2)$ on the symmetry axis toward
the mirrored belly, the sunlit lower half of the circle of radius $R$ about
$C$ as mirror profile, the closed disc of radius $a$ about $A$ as absorbing
container, the reflected line $x \mapsto \mathrm{reflectedLine}\,x$, and the
set of absorbed impact parameters, constrained by bundled physical laws:
every absorbed ray reflects on the half-mirror arc, satisfies the specular
reflection law on the circular profile (with direction reversal of the
incoming axial ray recorded as a two-by-two linear system on slope and
intercept), reaches the container disc, lies inside the open aperture
$(-R, R)$, and forms a contiguous fan centred on the symmetry axis
(no-gap).
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure CookerB1 (p : CookerParams) where

  C : Vec

  A : Vec

  C_coord : C = (0, 0)
  A_coord : A = (0, -(p.R / 2))

  mirrorSet : Set Vec
  mirrorSet_eq : mirrorSet =
    {v : Vec | vnorm (v.1 - C.1, v.2 - C.2) = p.R ∧ v.2 ≤ C.2}

  containerSet : Set Vec
  containerSet_eq : containerSet =
    {v : Vec | vnorm (v.1 - A.1, v.2 - A.2) ≤ p.a}

  reflectedLine : ℝ → Line2D

  hitSet : Set ℝ

  on_mirror : ∀ x ∈ hitSet, (x, -Real.sqrt (p.R ^ 2 - x ^ 2)) ∈ mirrorSet

  reflection_law : ∀ x ∈ hitSet,
    -Real.sqrt (p.R ^ 2 - x ^ 2) =
        (reflectedLine x).m * x + (reflectedLine x).b ∧
      (x ^ 2 - Real.sqrt (p.R ^ 2 - x ^ 2) ^ 2) =
        (reflectedLine x).m * (2 * x * Real.sqrt (p.R ^ 2 - x ^ 2))

  absorbed_law : ∀ x ∈ hitSet,
    ∃ q ∈ containerSet,
      q.2 = (reflectedLine x).m * q.1 + (reflectedLine x).b

  hit_branch : ∀ x ∈ hitSet, x ∈ Set.Ioo (-p.R) p.R

  no_gap : ∀ x₁ x₂ : ℝ, x₁ ∈ hitSet → |x₂| ≤ |x₁| → x₂ ∈ hitSet

nodes.title: Incidence angle of a column
nodes.statement:
The incidence angle of the ray with impact parameter $x$ on the circular
mirror profile, measured against the radial normal at the mirror point:
$\arcsin(|x| / R)$.  Dimensionless; the absolute value absorbs the two
mirror-image branches $\pm|x|$ of Figure~2f.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
def incidenceAngle (p : CookerParams) (x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  Real.arcsin (|x| / p.R)

nodes.title: Maximum-incidence-angle specification
nodes.statement:
The specification of $\theta_{\max}$: it is attained by a ray of the
absorbed family, it bounds the incidence angles of all absorbed rays, and
it lies on the acute branch $0 < \theta_{\max} < \pi/2$ seen in Figure~2f.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
def IsThetaMax (p : CookerParams) (s : CookerB1 p) (θ : ℝ) : Prop :=
  θ ∈ Set.Ioo 0 (Real.pi / 2) ∧
    (∃ x ∈ s.hitSet, incidenceAngle p x = θ) ∧
      (∀ x ∈ s.hitSet, incidenceAngle p x ≤ θ)

nodes.title: Extremal-ray tangency bookkeeping
nodes.statement:
Extremality and tangency data at a limiting ray (one attaining
$\theta_{\max}$): an impact parameter $x$ in the absorbed family with
incidence angle exactly the extremal angle, off the symmetry axis
($x \neq 0$, the two mirror-image tangent columns $\pm|x|$ of Figure~2f),
whose reflected line is tangent to the container circle --- its signed
distance from the container centre has magnitude exactly $a$.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure ExtremalRaySpec (p : CookerParams) (s : CookerB1 p) (θ : ℝ) where
  x : ℝ
  hx : x ∈ s.hitSet
  hθ : incidenceAngle p x = θ

  off_axis : x ≠ 0

  tangent_dist : |distToLine (s.reflectedLine x) s.A| = p.a

nodes.title: Coefficient ansatz specification
nodes.statement:
The given ansatz of the subquestion, in the family sense the problem itself
uses in its later parts: one coefficient pair $\alpha, \beta$ expresses the
container radius as
$a = \alpha \sin\theta_1 + \beta \sin(2\theta_1)$ at every extremal
(tangent) configuration of every cooker of the same mirror radius $R$.
The scalars $\alpha, \beta$ parametrize the ansatz; the specification never
evaluates them.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
def CoeffSpec (p : CookerParams) (α β : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (q : CookerParams), q.R = p.R → ∀ (s : CookerB1 q) (θ₁ : ℝ),
    IsThetaMax q s θ₁ →
    (∀ _e : ExtremalRaySpec q s θ₁, q.a = α * Real.sin θ₁ + β * Real.sin (2 * θ₁))

nodes.title: Second extremal configuration
nodes.statement:
A second extremal configuration in the same mirror-radius family: a cooker
of the same mirror radius $R$ with extremal angle $\theta'$, together with
its extremal-ray tangency bookkeeping.  Its existence is a readout of the
physical family (the later parts vary the container size at fixed $R$); the
identity holding at two distinct extremal angles cuts a two-by-two linear
system with determinant $2(\cos\theta' - \cos\theta) \neq 0$, which is what
makes the coefficient pair unique.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure SecondExtremalConfig (p : CookerParams) (θ' : ℝ) where
  q : CookerParams
  qR : q.R = p.R
  t : CookerB1 q
  hθ' : IsThetaMax q t θ'
  e' : ExtremalRaySpec q t θ'

nodes.title: Impact parameter from incidence angle
nodes.statement:
Inside the open aperture the impact-parameter magnitude is recovered from
the incidence angle as $|x| = R \sin\theta$; the absolute value absorbs the
two mirror-image branches $\pm|x|$ of Figure~2f.
nodes.proof_tex:
Unfold the incidence angle $\arcsin(|x|/R) = \theta$: on the open aperture
$|x|/R < 1$ lies in the range of $\sin$ on the acute branch, so applying
$\sin$ to both sides gives $|x| = R\sin\theta$.
nodes.lean_source:
lemma impactParam_eq_sin (p : CookerParams) {x θ : ℝ}
    (hx : x ∈ Set.Ioo (-p.R) p.R) (hθ : incidenceAngle p x = θ) :
    |x| = p.R * Real.sin θ := by
  have hR : 0 < p.R := p.hR
  have hlt : |x| / p.R < 1 := by
    rw [div_lt_one hR, abs_lt]
    exact ⟨by linarith [hx.1], by linarith [hx.2]⟩
  have hnn : 0 ≤ |x| / p.R := by positivity
  have h : Real.sin (incidenceAngle p x) = |x| / p.R := by
    unfold incidenceAngle
    rw [Real.sin_arcsin (by linarith) (by linarith)]
  calc |x| = p.R * (|x| / p.R) := by field_simp
    _ = p.R * Real.sin θ := by rw [← h, hθ]

nodes.title: Positivity of $\sin(2\theta)$ on the acute branch
nodes.statement:
For $\theta \in (0, \pi/2)$ one has $0 < \sin(2\theta)$; the positivity
flashpoint that keeps the coefficient identification nondegenerate.
nodes.proof_tex:
On $\theta \in (0, \pi/2)$ the double angle $2\theta$ lies in $(0, \pi)$,
where the sine is strictly positive.
nodes.lean_source:
lemma sin_two_pos {θ : ℝ} (hθ : θ ∈ Set.Ioo 0 (Real.pi / 2)) :
    0 < Real.sin (2 * θ) := by
  have h2 : 2 * θ ∈ Set.Ioo 0 Real.pi :=
    ⟨by linarith [hθ.1], by linarith [hθ.2]⟩
  exact Real.sin_pos_of_mem_Ioo h2

nodes.title: Tangency relation at the limiting ray
nodes.statement:
At an extremal angle $\theta \in (0, \pi/2)$ with extremal-ray tangency
bookkeeping, specular reflection at the mirror point
$(|x|, -\sqrt{R^2 - |x|^2})$ with $|x| = R\sin\theta$, the container offset
$A = (0, -R/2)$, and the tangency distance condition force the container
radius to be
\[
a = R \sin\theta - \tfrac{R}{2}\sin(2\theta) .
\]
This is the load-bearing geometric identity of part B.1.
nodes.proof_tex:
The specular law at the extremal column is a two-by-two linear system for
the slope and intercept of the reflected line, with nonzero determinant
$-(2x)(x^2 + y^2)$; solving gives the intercept
$b = -R^2/(2\sqrt{R^2 - x^2})$, always negative with $|b| \ge R/2$.
The tangency distance condition then evaluates (on either mirror-image
branch, via $|x|$) since the signed-distance numerator $-R/2 - b$ is
strictly positive; substituting $|x| = R\sin\theta$ from
\cref{lem:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_2_B_1:impactParam_eq_sin}
and eliminating the double angle gives the claimed identity.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem container_radius_at_extremal_angle (p : CookerParams)
    (s : CookerB1 p) {θ : ℝ} (hθ : θ ∈ Set.Ioo 0 (Real.pi / 2))
    (e : ExtremalRaySpec p s θ) :
    p.a = p.R * Real.sin θ - (p.R / 2) * Real.sin (2 * θ) := by
  have hR : 0 < p.R := p.hR
  have hRne : p.R ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt hR

  have hx_hit : e.x ∈ s.hitSet := e.hx
  have hx_branch := s.hit_branch e.x hx_hit
  have hx_lt : |e.x| < p.R := by
    rw [abs_lt]
    exact ⟨by linarith [hx_branch.1], by linarith [hx_branch.2]⟩
  have hsin : |e.x| = p.R * Real.sin θ := impactParam_eq_sin p hx_branch e.hθ
  have hx_ne : e.x ≠ 0 := e.off_axis
  have hθ' : 0 < θ ∧ θ < Real.pi / 2 := hθ
  have hcos_pos : 0 < Real.cos θ :=
    Real.cos_pos_of_mem_Ioo ⟨by linarith [hθ'.2, Real.pi_pos], hθ'.2⟩

  set y : ℝ := Real.sqrt (p.R ^ 2 - e.x ^ 2) with hy_def
  have hx2_lt : e.x ^ 2 < p.R ^ 2 := by
    have hsq : |e.x| ^ 2 < p.R ^ 2 := by nlinarith [abs_nonneg e.x, hx_lt, hR]
    rwa [sq_abs] at hsq
  have hy_sq : y ^ 2 = p.R ^ 2 - e.x ^ 2 := Real.sq_sqrt (by linarith)
  have hy_pos : 0 < y := Real.sqrt_pos.2 (by linarith)
  have hy_ne : y ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt hy_pos
  have hR2pos : (0:ℝ) < p.R ^ 2 := sq_pos_of_pos hR

  have hy_lt : y < p.R := by
    have hsq : y ^ 2 < p.R ^ 2 := by nlinarith [hy_sq, sq_pos_of_ne_zero hx_ne]
    have h2 : |y| < p.R := by
      by_contra hle
      push Not at hle
      have hself : p.R * p.R ≤ |y| * |y| := mul_self_le_mul_self hR.le hle
      rw [abs_of_pos hy_pos] at hself
      nlinarith [hsq, hself]
    rwa [abs_of_pos hy_pos] at h2

  have hy_cos : y = p.R * Real.cos θ := by
    have hs1 : Real.sin θ ^ 2 + Real.cos θ ^ 2 = 1 := Real.sin_sq_add_cos_sq θ
    have hxabs : |e.x| ^ 2 = p.R ^ 2 * Real.sin θ ^ 2 := by
      rw [hsin]; ring
    have keqs : e.x ^ 2 = p.R ^ 2 * Real.sin θ ^ 2 := by
      calc e.x ^ 2 = |e.x| ^ 2 := by rw [sq_abs]
        _ = p.R ^ 2 * Real.sin θ ^ 2 := hxabs
    have hyc : y ^ 2 = (p.R * Real.cos θ) ^ 2 := by
      nlinarith [hy_sq, keqs, hs1]
    have hcases := sq_eq_sq_iff_eq_or_eq_neg.mp hyc
    rcases hcases with h | h
    · exact h
    · have hpos : (0:ℝ) < p.R * Real.cos θ := mul_pos hR hcos_pos
      linarith [h, hy_pos, hpos]

  obtain ⟨h_b, h_m⟩ := s.reflection_law e.x hx_hit
  rw [hy_sq] at h_m
  change -y = (s.reflectedLine e.x).m * e.x + (s.reflectedLine e.x).b at h_b
  set m : ℝ := (s.reflectedLine e.x).m with hm_def
  set b : ℝ := (s.reflectedLine e.x).b with hb_def
  have hxy_ne : (2:ℝ) * e.x * y ≠ 0 :=
    mul_ne_zero (mul_ne_zero two_ne_zero hx_ne) hy_ne
  have hxy2 : (2 * e.x * y) ^ 2 ≠ 0 := pow_ne_zero 2 hxy_ne
  have hR4 : p.R ^ 4 = (2 * e.x ^ 2 - p.R ^ 2) ^ 2 + (2 * e.x * y) ^ 2 := by
    nlinarith [hy_sq]
  have hmx : m * (2 * e.x * y) = 2 * e.x ^ 2 - p.R ^ 2 := by
    nlinarith [h_m, hy_sq, h_b]
  have hm_eq : m = (2 * e.x ^ 2 - p.R ^ 2) / (2 * e.x * y) := by
    rw [← hmx]; field_simp
  have hb_eq : b = -p.R ^ 2 / (2 * y) := by
    have hbb : b = -y - m * e.x := by linarith [h_b]
    rw [hbb]
    have h2y : (2:ℝ) * y ≠ 0 := mul_ne_zero two_ne_zero hy_ne
    field_simp
    nlinarith [hmx, hy_sq]

  have hm2 : m ^ 2 + 1 = (p.R ^ 2 / (2 * e.x * y)) ^ 2 := by
    have key : ((2 * e.x ^ 2 - p.R ^ 2) ^ 2 / (2 * e.x * y) ^ 2 + 1)
        * (2 * e.x * y) ^ 2 = (p.R ^ 2) ^ 2 := by
      field_simp
      nlinarith [hR4]
    calc m ^ 2 + 1 = (2 * e.x ^ 2 - p.R ^ 2) ^ 2 / (2 * e.x * y) ^ 2 + 1 := by
          rw [hm_eq, div_pow]
      _ = (p.R ^ 2) ^ 2 / (2 * e.x * y) ^ 2 := by rw [eq_div_iff hxy2]; exact key
      _ = (p.R ^ 2 / (2 * e.x * y)) ^ 2 := by rw [div_pow]
  have hsval : Real.sqrt (m ^ 2 + 1) = p.R ^ 2 / (2 * |e.x| * y) := by
    rw [hm2, Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs]
    have h1 : |p.R ^ 2| = p.R ^ 2 := abs_of_pos hR2pos
    have h2 : |(2:ℝ) * e.x * y| = 2 * |e.x| * y := by
      rw [abs_mul, abs_mul, abs_of_pos (by norm_num : (0:ℝ) < 2), abs_of_pos hy_pos]
    rw [abs_div, h1, h2]

  have hb_lt : b < -p.R / 2 := by
    rw [hb_eq]
    have h2y : (0:ℝ) < 2 * y := by linarith
    rw [div_lt_iff₀ h2y]
    have key : p.R * y < p.R * p.R := mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left hy_lt hR
    calc -p.R ^ 2 = -(p.R * p.R) := by ring
      _ < -(p.R * y) := by linarith [key]
      _ = (-p.R / 2) * (2 * y) := by ring

  have hnum_pos : (0:ℝ) < -p.R / 2 - b := by linarith

  have hA : s.A = (0, -(p.R / 2)) := s.A_coord
  have hnum : distToLine (s.reflectedLine e.x) s.A
      = (-p.R / 2 - b) / Real.sqrt (m ^ 2 + 1) := by
    unfold distToLine
    rw [hA]
    simp
    ring
  have hsqrt_pos : (0:ℝ) < Real.sqrt (m ^ 2 + 1) :=
    Real.sqrt_pos.2 (by positivity)
  have htan := e.tangent_dist
  rw [hnum, abs_of_pos (div_pos hnum_pos hsqrt_pos)] at htan
  have h_eq : p.a * Real.sqrt (m ^ 2 + 1) = -p.R / 2 - b := by
    rw [div_eq_iff (ne_of_gt hsqrt_pos)] at htan
    linarith [htan]
  rw [hsval, hb_eq] at h_eq

  have h_mul : p.a * p.R = |e.x| * (p.R - y) := by
    have hax : (2:ℝ) * |e.x| * y ≠ 0 :=
      mul_ne_zero (mul_ne_zero two_ne_zero (abs_ne_zero.mpr hx_ne)) hy_ne
    have h2y : (2:ℝ) * y ≠ 0 := mul_ne_zero two_ne_zero hy_ne
    have step1 : p.a * (p.R ^ 2 / (2 * |e.x| * y))
        = p.a * p.R ^ 2 / (2 * |e.x| * y) := by ring
    have step2 : -p.R / 2 - -p.R ^ 2 / (2 * y) = p.R * (p.R - y) / (2 * y) := by
      field_simp
      ring
    rw [step1, step2] at h_eq
    rw [div_eq_div_iff hax h2y] at h_eq
    have h2ne : (2:ℝ) ≠ 0 := two_ne_zero
    have hcan : p.a * p.R * (p.R * (2 * y)) = |e.x| * (p.R - y) * (p.R * (2 * y)) := by
      ring_nf at h_eq ⊢
      linarith [h_eq]
    exact mul_right_cancel₀ (mul_ne_zero hRne (mul_ne_zero h2ne hy_ne)) hcan

  rw [hsin, hy_cos] at h_mul
  have h1 : p.a = p.R * Real.sin θ * (1 - Real.cos θ) := by
    apply mul_right_cancel₀ hRne
    calc p.a * p.R = p.R * Real.sin θ * (p.R - p.R * Real.cos θ) := h_mul
      _ = (p.R * Real.sin θ * (1 - Real.cos θ)) * p.R := by ring
  rw [h1, Real.sin_two_mul]
  ring

nodes.title: Coefficients of the given ansatz in terms of $R$
nodes.statement:
\textbf{(Target, T2-B1.)}  For the Figure-2f cooker with extremal absorbed
ray at maximum incidence angle $\theta_{\max}$, a coefficient pair
$\alpha, \beta$ fulfilling the family ansatz
\cref{def:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_2_B_1:CoeffSpec}, and a
second extremal configuration of the same mirror radius at a distinct
extremal angle $\theta' \neq \theta_{\max}$, the coefficients of the given
ansatz $a = \alpha \sin\theta_{\max} + \beta \sin(2\theta_{\max})$ are
\[
\alpha = R, \qquad \beta = -\frac{R}{2} .
\]
This is the recorded official answer of part B.1; the values are
conclusion-side only, confined to this target theorem (no hypothesis or
structure field states them in advance).
nodes.proof_tex:
Apply
\cref{thm:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_2_B_1:container_radius_at_extremal_angle}
at the given extremal ray and at the second configuration
$\theta'$: both angles satisfy the tangency identity, while the ansatz of
\cref{def:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_2_B_1:CoeffSpec} gives the
family identity at the same two configurations.  Subtracting at
$\theta_{\max}$ and $\theta'$ yields a two-by-two homogeneous linear
system in $(\alpha - R, \beta + R/2)$ whose determinant
$2\sin\theta_{\max}\sin\theta'\,(\cos\theta' - \cos\theta_{\max})$ is
nonzero --- both sines are positive by
\cref{lem:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_2_B_1:sin_two_pos} (and
$\sin\theta > 0$ on the acute branch), and $\cos$ is strictly
antitone on $(0, \pi/2)$, so $\theta' \neq \theta_{\max}$ gives
$\cos\theta' \neq \cos\theta_{\max}$ --- forcing $\alpha = R$ and
$\beta = -R/2$.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem alpha_beta_in_terms_of_R (p : CookerParams) (s : CookerB1 p)
    {θ θ' α β : ℝ}
    (hθ : IsThetaMax p s θ) (hcoef : CoeffSpec p α β)
    (e : ExtremalRaySpec p s θ)
    (cfg₂ : SecondExtremalConfig p θ') (hdist : θ' ≠ θ) :
    α = p.R ∧ β = -p.R / 2 := by

  have hid₁ : p.a = p.R * Real.sin θ - (p.R / 2) * Real.sin (2 * θ) :=
    container_radius_at_extremal_angle p s hθ.1 e
  have hans₁ : p.a = α * Real.sin θ + β * Real.sin (2 * θ) :=
    hcoef p rfl s θ hθ e
  have heq₁ : (α - p.R) * Real.sin θ + (β + p.R / 2) * Real.sin (2 * θ) = 0 := by
    linarith [hid₁, hans₁]

  have hθ'' : θ' ∈ Set.Ioo 0 (Real.pi / 2) := cfg₂.hθ'.1
  have hid₂ : cfg₂.q.a = p.R * Real.sin θ' - (p.R / 2) * Real.sin (2 * θ') := by
    have h := container_radius_at_extremal_angle cfg₂.q cfg₂.t hθ'' cfg₂.e'
    rw [cfg₂.qR] at h
    exact h
  have hans₂ : cfg₂.q.a = α * Real.sin θ' + β * Real.sin (2 * θ') :=
    hcoef cfg₂.q cfg₂.qR cfg₂.t θ' cfg₂.hθ' cfg₂.e'
  have heq₂ : (α - p.R) * Real.sin θ' + (β + p.R / 2) * Real.sin (2 * θ') = 0 := by
    linarith [hid₂, hans₂]

  have hsθ : 0 < Real.sin θ := by
    apply Real.sin_pos_of_mem_Ioo
    exact ⟨hθ.1.1, by linarith [hθ.1.2, Real.pi_pos]⟩
  have hsθ' : 0 < Real.sin θ' := by
    apply Real.sin_pos_of_mem_Ioo
    exact ⟨hθ''.1, by linarith [hθ''.2, Real.pi_pos]⟩
  have hcos_ne : Real.cos θ' ≠ Real.cos θ := by
    intro hcos
    apply hdist
    have hsub : Set.Ioo 0 Real.pi ⊆ Set.Icc 0 Real.pi := Set.Ioo_subset_Icc_self
    exact Real.injOn_cos
      (hsub ⟨by linarith [hθ''.1], by linarith [hθ''.2, Real.pi_pos]⟩)
      (hsub ⟨by linarith [hθ.1.1], by linarith [hθ.1.2, Real.pi_pos]⟩) hcos
  have hdet : 2 * Real.sin θ * Real.sin θ' * (Real.cos θ' - Real.cos θ) ≠ 0 := by
    have hne1 : Real.sin θ ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt hsθ
    have hne2 : Real.sin θ' ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt hsθ'
    have hne3 : Real.cos θ' - Real.cos θ ≠ 0 := sub_ne_zero.mpr hcos_ne
    exact mul_ne_zero (mul_ne_zero (mul_ne_zero two_ne_zero hne1) hne2) hne3
  rw [Real.sin_two_mul θ'] at heq₂
  rw [Real.sin_two_mul θ] at heq₁
  have hβ : β + p.R / 2 = 0 := by
    have key : (β + p.R / 2) * (2 * Real.sin θ * Real.sin θ'
        * (Real.cos θ' - Real.cos θ)) = 0 := by
      have hthis : ((α - p.R) * Real.sin θ'
          + (β + p.R / 2) * (2 * Real.sin θ' * Real.cos θ')) * Real.sin θ = 0 := by
        rw [heq₂]; ring
      have h1 : ((α - p.R) * Real.sin θ
          + (β + p.R / 2) * (2 * Real.sin θ * Real.cos θ)) * Real.sin θ' = 0 := by
        rw [heq₁]; ring
      have h2 : (β + p.R / 2) * (2 * Real.sin θ * Real.sin θ'
            * (Real.cos θ' - Real.cos θ))
          = ((α - p.R) * Real.sin θ'
              + (β + p.R / 2) * (2 * Real.sin θ' * Real.cos θ')) * Real.sin θ
            - ((α - p.R) * Real.sin θ
              + (β + p.R / 2) * (2 * Real.sin θ * Real.cos θ)) * Real.sin θ' := by ring
      rw [h2, hthis, h1]; ring
    exact (mul_eq_zero.mp key).resolve_right hdet
  have hα : α - p.R = 0 := by
    have hsθne : Real.sin θ ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt hsθ
    have hz : (α - p.R) * Real.sin θ = 0 := by
      rw [hβ] at heq₁
      ring_nf at heq₁ ⊢
      linarith [heq₁]
    exact (mul_eq_zero.mp hz).resolve_right hsθne
  constructor
  · linarith [hα]
  · linarith [hβ]

nodes.statement: The assigned autoformalize agent should translate this physics problem into Lean declarations in the covered file, with theorem and lemma proof bodies written as `by sorry`.
nodes.proof_tex: This is an autoformalization task, not a proof task. Produce faithful statements that can later be proved without weakening the source contract.

nodes.title: Cross-section plane
nodes.statement:
The transverse cross-sectional plane of the cooker, the Euclidean plane
$\mathbb{E}^2 \cong \mathbb{R}^2$ with its inner product.  The physical
system is translationally invariant along the cylinder axes, so a single
cross-section captures all the geometry; points have units of length.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source: abbrev Plane := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)

nodes.title: Cooker parameters
nodes.statement:
Dimensionful parameters of the cooker: the mirror radius $R$ and the
container radius $a$ (both lengths), bundled with their positivity
certificates $0 < R$ and $0 < a$.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure CookerParams where
  R : ℝ
  a : ℝ
  hR : 0 < R
  ha : 0 < a

nodes.title: Cooker cross-section geometry
nodes.statement:
The geometry of the cross-section (Figure~2f): the mirror centre $C$, the
container centre $A$, the unit vector $e$ along the optical axis pointing
from $C$ towards the open half of the half-cylinder mirror, and the
in-plane unit normal $n$ ($n \perp e$, chosen on the container's side),
with the container centre lying $R/2$ from $C$ along $n$:
$A - C = (R/2) \bullet n$.  Sunlight arrives in the direction $-e$.
The bundled fields record $\|e\| = 1$, $\|n\| = 1$,
$\langle n, e \rangle = 0$, and the offset law.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure CookerGeometry (p : CookerParams) where
  C : Plane
  A : Plane
  e : Plane
  n : Plane
  e_unit : ‖e‖ = 1
  n_unit : ‖n‖ = 1
  n_perp_e : inner ℝ n e = 0
  A_offset : A - C = (p.R / 2) • n

nodes.title: Mirror circle
nodes.statement:
The full circle of radius $R$ centred at $C$: the cross-sectional profile
of the cylindrical mirror.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
def mirrorCircle (p : CookerParams) (g : CookerGeometry p) : Set Plane :=
  Metric.sphere g.C p.R

nodes.title: Container disk
nodes.statement:
The absorbing disc: the closed disk of radius $a$ centred at $A$, the
cross-section of the cylindrical container.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
def containerDisk (p : CookerParams) (g : CookerGeometry p) : Set Plane :=
  Metric.closedBall g.A p.a

nodes.title: Half-mirror arc
nodes.statement:
The half-cylinder mirror arc: the semicircle of
\cref{def:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_2_B_2:mirrorCircle} lying in
the $0 \le \langle m - C, e\rangle$ half-plane --- the
``half-hollow-cylinder mirror'' of Figure~2f.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
def halfMirrorArc (p : CookerParams) (g : CookerGeometry p) : Set Plane :=
  {m ∈ mirrorCircle p g | 0 ≤ inner ℝ (m - g.C) g.e}

nodes.title: Absorbed-ray bookkeeping
nodes.statement:
Single-bounce bookkeeping for the sun rays absorbed by the container.  The
carrier pairs the incidence-point map $\mathrm{incidentPt} : \mathbb{R} \to
\mathbb{E}^2$ with the impact-parameter hit set; the bundled hypotheses
record the governing physical laws, kept as assumptions rather than
redefined locally: every absorbed ray (a) strikes the half-cylinder arc of
the mirror (incidence points land in
\cref{def:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_2_B_2:halfMirrorArc}), (b)
obeys the specular reflection law on the circular profile --- the reflected
ray reaches an absorbed endpoint $q$ in
\cref{def:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_2_B_2:containerDisk} with
$q - \mathrm{incidentPt}\,y = (2\langle \mathrm{incidentPt}\,y - C, n\rangle - R) \bullet n$ ---
and the Figure-2f branch information (c) the axial (central) ray is
absorbed, (d) the absorbed family is gap-free right of the axis
(contiguity of the single-bounce fan), and (e) every impact parameter in
$(0, R)$ is realized (strengthened at iter-009, see the NOTE below), so
the collected fan is exactly the open half aperture: it fills one side
from the axis to the aperture edge and $\theta_{\max}$ is a maximum over
a connected family.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure AbsorbedRays (p : CookerParams) (g : CookerGeometry p) where

  incidentPt : ℝ → Plane

  hitSet : Set ℝ

  on_mirror : Set.MapsTo incidentPt hitSet (halfMirrorArc p g)

  reflected_point_law : ∀ y ∈ hitSet, ∃ q : Plane,
    q ∈ containerDisk p g ∧
    q - incidentPt y = (2 * inner ℝ (incidentPt y - g.C) g.n - p.R) • g.n

  central_ray_absorbed : 0 ∈ hitSet

  no_gap : ∀ y₁ y₂ : ℝ, y₁ ∈ hitSet → 0 ≤ y₂ → y₂ ≤ y₁ → y₂ ∈ hitSet

  full_side_coverage : ∀ y ∈ Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) p.R,
    ∃ x ∈ hitSet, inner ℝ (incidentPt x - g.C) g.e = y

nodes.title: Collected width
nodes.statement:
The transverse width (impact-parameter support) of the rays that the mirror
concentrates onto the container: the supremum of the axial readouts
$\langle \mathrm{incidentPt}\,y - C, e\rangle$ over the hit set.  With
uniform parallel sunlight this width is proportional to the received power
$P$ (per unit axial length).  At the Figure-2f operating point the
hit-set readouts fill the open half aperture $(0, R)$ (full side
coverage), so the supremum is $R$ --- the physical content of
\cref{lem:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_2_B_2:collectedWidth_eq_radius}.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.

nodes.title: Uniform sunlight intensity
nodes.statement:
Uniform parallel sunlight: the incoming intensity $I$ (power per unit area)
is constant across the aperture and certified positive by a bundled field
$0 < I$.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure UniformIntensity where
  I : ℝ
  hI : 0 < I

nodes.title: Power budget
nodes.statement:
The power budget for the configuration: $P$, the power actually received by
the absorbing container from the mirror, and $P_0$, the power it would
receive without the mirror.  The bundled hypotheses state the physical
accounting under uniform intensity $I$: both quantities are proportional to
their transverse collected widths per unit axial length, namely
$P = I \cdot \mathrm{collectedWidth}$ and $P_0 = I \cdot (2a)$ (the
container's unmirrored geometric width, its diameter).
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure PowerBudget (p : CookerParams) (g : CookerGeometry p)
    (r : AbsorbedRays p g) where
  P : ℝ
  P₀ : ℝ
  intensity : UniformIntensity
  received_power_eq : P = intensity.I * collectedWidth p g r
  unmirrored_power_eq : P₀ = intensity.I * (2 * p.a)

nodes.title: B.1 calibration
nodes.statement:
The previous-part (B.1, $\alpha = R$, $\beta = -R/2$) result, kept as a
calibration hypothesis for the geometry: the container radius relates to
the maximum incidence angle by
$a = R \sin\theta - (R/2) \sin(2\theta)$.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
def B1Calibration (p : CookerParams) (θ : ℝ) : Prop :=
  p.a = p.R * Real.sin θ - (p.R / 2) * Real.sin (2 * θ)

nodes.title: Incidence angle
nodes.statement:
The incidence angle at a mirror point $m$ on the circular profile of
radius $R$, measured against the normal at $m$:
$\arccos\bigl(|\langle m - C, e\rangle| / R\bigr)$ --- the angle
between the incoming direction $e$ and the radius to $m$.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
def incidenceAngle (p : CookerParams) (g : CookerGeometry p) (m : Plane) : ℝ :=
  Real.arccos (|inner ℝ (m - g.C) g.e| / p.R)

nodes.title: Maximum incidence angle specification
nodes.statement:
The specification of $\theta_{\max}$: the largest angle of incidence on
the mirror (measured against the normal at the point of incidence) among
all reflected rays striking the container, lying in $(0, \/2)$ --- the
branch of nontrivial, non-grazing rays seen in Figure~2f.  Concretely:
$\theta$ is attained at some absorbed impact parameter and bounds the
incidence angle of every absorbed ray.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
def ThetaMaxSpec (p : CookerParams) (g : CookerGeometry p)
    (r : AbsorbedRays p g) (θ : ℝ) : Prop :=
  (θ ∈ Set.Ioo 0 (Real.pi / 2)) ∧
  (∃ y ∈ r.hitSet, incidenceAngle p g (r.incidentPt y) = θ) ∧
  (∀ y ∈ r.hitSet, incidenceAngle p g (r.incidentPt y) ≤ θ)

nodes.title: Impact parameters bounded by the aperture
nodes.statement:
Every mirror-collected impact parameter is bounded in absolute value by
the aperture radius: for every absorbed impact parameter $y$,
$|\langle \mathrm{incidentPt}\,y - C, e\rangle| \le R$.
nodes.proof_tex:
The incidence point lies on the mirror circle, so
$\|\mathrm{incidentPt}\,y - C\| = R$; since $\|e\| = 1$,
Cauchy--Schwarz for the inner product gives
$|\langle \mathrm{incidentPt}\,y - C, e\rangle| \le
\|\mathrm{incidentPt}\,y - C\| \cdot \|e\| = R$.
nodes.lean_source:
lemma impactParam_le_aperture (p : CookerParams) (g : CookerGeometry p)
    (r : AbsorbedRays p g) :
    ∀ y ∈ r.hitSet, |inner ℝ (r.incidentPt y - g.C) g.e| ≤ p.R := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Collected width equals the radius
nodes.statement:
The transverse width collected by the half-cylinder mirror on the
container's side equals $R$ (one full half of the aperture $2R$):
$\mathrm{collectedWidth} = R$.
nodes.proof_tex:
Upper bound: every impact-parameter readout is at most $R$ by
\cref{lem:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_2_B_2:impactParam_le_aperture}
(incidence points lie on the mirror circle; Cauchy--Schwarz with
$\|e\| = 1$), so the defining supremum does not exceed $R$; the readout
family is bounded and nonempty (the central ray $0$ is absorbed).
Lower bound: the (iter-009 strengthened) full side coverage realizes every
impact parameter $y \in (0, R)$ as an absorbed readout, so the readout
set contains the whole open half aperture $(0, R)$, whose supremum in
$\mathbb{R}$ is $R$.  Hence the supremum of the full readout family is at
least $R$; combined with the upper bound it equals $R$.
nodes.lean_source:
lemma collectedWidth_eq_radius (p : CookerParams) (g : CookerGeometry p)
    (r : AbsorbedRays p g) :
    collectedWidth p g r = p.R := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Power ratio as width ratio
nodes.statement:
Power ratio from the width accounting only:
$P / P_0 = R / (2a)$.  With the B.1 calibration this becomes the target
trigonometric form.
nodes.proof_tex:
Substitute the two budget identities
$P = I \cdot \mathrm{collectedWidth}$ and $P_0 = I \cdot (2a)$; the
common positive intensity $I$ cancels in the ratio, and
\cref{lem:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_2_B_2:collectedWidth_eq_radius}
replaces $\mathrm{collectedWidth}$ by $R$.
nodes.lean_source:
lemma power_ratio_eq_width_ratio (p : CookerParams) (g : CookerGeometry p)
    (r : AbsorbedRays p g) (budget : PowerBudget p g r) :
    budget.P / budget.P₀ = p.R / (2 * p.a) := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Radius-over-diameter trigonometric bridge
nodes.statement:
For $\theta \in (0, \/2)$ satisfying the B.1 calibration,
$R / (2a) = 1 / (1 - \cos\theta)$.
nodes.proof_tex:
By the double-angle identity and the calibration,
$2a = 2R\sin\theta - R\sin(2\theta)
= 2R\sin\theta\,(1 - \cos\theta)$,
so $R/(2a) = 1/(1 - \cos\theta)$ after cancelling the positive factor
$2R\sin\theta$ (positivity from $\theta \in (0, \/2)$ and $0 < R$);
this leaves $R/(2a) = 1/(1 - \cos\theta)$.
nodes.lean_source:
lemma radius_over_diameter_eq (p : CookerParams) {θ : ℝ}
    (hθ : θ ∈ Set.Ioo 0 (Real.pi / 2)) (hcal : B1Calibration p θ) :
    p.R / (2 * p.a) = 1 / (1 - Real.cos θ) := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Power ratio in terms of $\theta_{\max}$ (T2-B.2 target)
nodes.statement:
For the cooker of Figure~2f with absorbed-ray bookkeeping, power budget,
and maximum-incidence-angle specification $\theta_{\max}$, the ratio of
the received power $P$ to the unmirrored power $P_0$ is
$P / P_0 = 1 / (1 - \cos\theta_{\max})$ --- the recorded official
answer of part B.2.
nodes.proof_tex:
The B.1 calibration at the specified maximum angle yields
$R/(2a) = 1/(1 - \cos\theta_{\max})$ by
\cref{lem:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_2_B_2:radius_over_diameter_eq};
chaining with
\cref{lem:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_2_B_2:power_ratio_eq_width_ratio},
$P/P_0 = R/(2a)$, yields the claim.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem power_ratio_in_terms_of_theta_max
    (p : CookerParams) (g : CookerGeometry p)
    (r : AbsorbedRays p g) (budget : PowerBudget p g r)
    {θ : ℝ} (hθ : ThetaMaxSpec p g r θ) (hcal : B1Calibration p θ) :
    budget.P / budget.P₀ = 1 / (1 - Real.cos θ) := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Physics formalization target
nodes.statement: The assigned autoformalize agent should translate this physics problem into Lean declarations in the covered file, with theorem and lemma proof bodies written as `by sorry`.
nodes.proof_tex: This is an autoformalization task, not a proof task. Produce faithful statements that can later be proved without weakening the source contract.

nodes.title: Recorded incidence angle
nodes.statement:
Symbolic abbreviation for the maximal incidence angle of Figure~2f,
$\theta_{\max}$.  It is defined as the acute angle of the 3-4-5 triangle
recorded in the official solution.  This is a pure abbreviation: the
physical content of the official answer (the cosine of this angle) is
PROVED on the conclusion side of
\cref{thm:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_2_B_3:container_diameter_for_quintuple_power},
not defined here.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source: abbrev thetaMaxRecorded : ℝ := Real.arccos (4 / 5)

nodes.title: Metre in centimetres
nodes.statement:
Unit scale: one metre expressed in centimetres, the conversion factor used
to report the final container radius in cm as the subquestion requests.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source: abbrev metreInCentimetres : ℝ := 100

nodes.title: Cross-sectional plane
nodes.statement:
The Euclidean plane $\mathbb{E}^2$ containing the transverse cross-section
of the mirror/container system of Figure~2f.  The physical system is
translationally invariant along the cylinder axes, so a single cross-section
captures all the geometry; lengths in this plane are identified with real
numbers via the norm.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source: abbrev CrossSectionPlane := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)

nodes.title: Solar cooker geometry
nodes.statement:
The geometric configuration of Figure~2f: the mirror radius $R$, the
container radius $a$, the container centre, and the unit sunlight direction
along the optical axis, with the bundled figure readouts $0 < a < R$ and the
problem datum that the container centre lies $R/2$ from the mirror centre on
the symmetry plane.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure SolarCookerGeometry where
  mirrorRadius : ℝ
  containerRadius : ℝ
  containerCentre : CrossSectionPlane
  sunDirection : CrossSectionPlane
  mirrorRadius_pos : 0 < mirrorRadius
  containerRadius_pos : 0 < containerRadius
  containerRadius_lt : containerRadius < mirrorRadius
  sunDirection_unit : ‖sunDirection‖ = 1
  container_centre_distance : containerCentre = (mirrorRadius / 2) • sunDirection

nodes.title: Half-cylindrical mirror physics
nodes.statement:
The governing-law carrier at a reflection point $x$ of the mirror: $x$ lies
on the mirror surface ($\|x\| = R$) on the illuminated half, the outgoing
ray is the law-of-reflection image of the incoming direction in the radial
normal line at $x$ (specular reflection at the cylindrical surface), the
incidence angle at $x$ is measured from the normal drawn at the point of
incidence and is related to the geometry by the cosine law, and it is acute
(the single-reflection/uniform-irradiance regime: any ray absorbed by the
container reflects from the mirror at most once).
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure HalfCylindricalMirrorPhysics
    (G : SolarCookerGeometry)
    (x : CrossSectionPlane) (theta : ℝ) : Prop where

  on_mirror : ‖x‖ = G.mirrorRadius

  illuminated_side : @inner ℝ _ _ x G.sunDirection < 0

  specular_reflection :
    (ℝ ∙ x).reflection (-G.sunDirection)
      = 2 • ((@inner ℝ _ _ x (-G.sunDirection))
              / (G.mirrorRadius ^ 2)) • x - (-G.sunDirection)

  angleOfIncidence : theta = Real.arccos ((@inner ℝ _ _ x (-G.sunDirection)) / G.mirrorRadius)

  angle_acute : theta ∈ Set.Ioo 0 (Real.pi / 2)

nodes.title: Previous-part results (B.1 and B.2 interfaces)
nodes.statement:
The named natural-language prerequisite interfaces of subquestions B.1 and
B.2 packaged over an incidence angle $\theta \in (0, \pi/2)$ with $P, P_0 > 0$:
the B.1 geometric relation
$a = R \sin\theta - (R/2)\sin(2\theta)$
(the determined coefficients $\alpha = R$, $\beta = -R/2$) and the B.2 power
ratio $P/P_0 = 1/(1 - \cos\theta)$.  Nothing in this structure fixes the
value of $\theta$ or of $a$, so the B.3 conclusions are not smuggled in.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure PreviousPartResults
    (mirrorRadius containerRadius : ℝ) (theta : ℝ) (P P0 : ℝ) : Prop where

  theta_range : theta ∈ Set.Ioo 0 (Real.pi / 2)

  containerRadius_eq :
    containerRadius
      = mirrorRadius * Real.sin theta - (mirrorRadius / 2) * Real.sin (2 * theta)

  P0_pos : 0 < P0

  P_pos : 0 < P

  power_ratio_eq : P / P0 = 1 / (1 - Real.cos theta)

nodes.title: The recorded angle is acute
nodes.statement:
The recorded maximal incidence angle lies in the acute range:
$\theta_{\max} \in (0, \pi/2)$, as required of every ray on the
single-reflection branch that reaches the container.
nodes.proof_tex:
The angle is an arccosine of a value lying strictly between $0$ and $1$, and
arccosine sends the interior of $[-1, 1]$ to $(0, \pi)$ in a strictly
decreasing way, so the value sits strictly between $\arccos 1 = 0$ and
$\arccos 0 = \pi/2$.
nodes.lean_source:
lemma thetaMaxRecorded_mem_Ioo :
    thetaMaxRecorded ∈ Set.Ioo 0 (Real.pi / 2) := by
  sorry

nodes.title: The sine of the recorded angle
nodes.statement:
3-4-5 triangle certificate:
$\sin\theta_{\max} = 3/5$.
nodes.proof_tex:
On the acute range of
\cref{lem:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_2_B_3:thetaMaxRecorded_mem_Ioo},
$\sin\theta_{\max} = \sqrt{1 - \cos^2\theta_{\max}}$; the 3-4-5 ratio gives
$1 - (4/5)^2 = 9/25$, whose square root is $3/5$.
nodes.lean_source:
lemma sin_thetaMaxRecorded : Real.sin thetaMaxRecorded = 3 / 5 := by
  sorry

nodes.title: The sine of the doubled recorded angle
nodes.statement: Double-angle certificate: $\sin(2\theta_{\max}) = 24/25$.
nodes.proof_tex:
Apply the double-angle identity $\sin(2\theta) = 2\sin\theta\cos\theta$ to the
3-4-5 ratio and
\cref{lem:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_2_B_3:sin_thetaMaxRecorded}:
$2 \cdot (3/5) \cdot (4/5) = 24/25$.
nodes.lean_source:
lemma sin_two_mul_thetaMaxRecorded : Real.sin (2 * thetaMaxRecorded) = 24 / 25 := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Container radius for quintuple power
nodes.statement:
\textbf{(Target, T2-B3.)}  For a solar-cooker geometry
(\cref{def:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_2_B_3:SolarCookerGeometry})
governed by the mirror physics
(\cref{def:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_2_B_3:HalfCylindricalMirrorPhysics})
at a reflection point reaching the container, with mirror radius
$R = 1\,\mathrm{m}$, container radius $a$, received power $P$ and no-mirror
power $P_0$ satisfying the previous-part relations B.1 and B.2
(\cref{def:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_2_B_3:PreviousPartResults}),
if $P = 5\,P_0$ then: $\theta_{\max}$ equals the recorded angle
($\cos\theta_{\max} = 4/5$), the container radius is
$a = 0.12\,\mathrm{m}$, and reported in centimetres $a = 12\,\mathrm{cm}$.
The official answers $\cos\theta_{\max} = 4/5$ and $12\,\mathrm{cm}$ appear
here conclusion-side only; no hypothesis fixes them in advance.
nodes.proof_tex:
Invert the B.2 ratio: $P/P_0 = 5 = 1/(1-\cos\theta_{\max})$ forces
$1-\cos\theta_{\max} = 1/5$, hence $\cos\theta_{\max} = 4/5$; since both
\cref{def:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_2_B_3:PreviousPartResults} and
\cref{def:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_2_B_3:HalfCylindricalMirrorPhysics}
confine $\theta_{\max}$ to the acute range $(0, \pi/2)$, on which cosine is
strictly monotone (so arccosine is its inverse there),
\cref{lem:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_2_B_3:thetaMaxRecorded_mem_Ioo}
identifies $\theta_{\max}$ with the recorded angle.  Substitute into the B.1
relation $a = R\sin\theta_{\max} - (R/2)\sin(2\theta_{\max})$ at $R = 1$
with
\cref{lem:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_2_B_3:sin_thetaMaxRecorded} and
\cref{lem:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_2_B_3:sin_two_mul_thetaMaxRecorded}:
$a = 3/5 - (1/2)(24/25) = 3/25 = 0.12\,\mathrm{m}$, and the conversion scale
of
\cref{def:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_2_B_3:metreInCentimetres} turns
this into $a \cdot 100 = 12$, i.e. $a = 12\,\mathrm{cm}$.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem container_diameter_for_quintuple_power
    (G : SolarCookerGeometry)
    (R a thetaMax P P0 : ℝ)
    (hR_val : R = 1)
    (hR : G.mirrorRadius = R)
    (ha : G.containerRadius = a)
    (x : CrossSectionPlane)
    (hphys : HalfCylindricalMirrorPhysics G x thetaMax)
    (hprev : PreviousPartResults R a thetaMax P P0)
    (hP : P = 5 * P0) :
    thetaMax = thetaMaxRecorded ∧ a = 0.12 ∧ a * metreInCentimetres = 12 := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Half-cylindrical mirror reflection
nodes.statement:
The physical setup of the Figure-2g half-cylindrical mirror: a radius
$R$ (a length, bundled with $0 < R$), the reflection point
$(P_x\theta, P_y\theta)$ where the axial ray A --- parallel to the
$y$-axis --- strikes the mirror at incidence angle $\theta$ (both
coordinates lengths), the slope--intercept data $m_A\theta$ (dimensionless)
and $b_A\theta$ (a length) of ray A's reflected line
$y = m_A\theta\,x + b_A\theta$, and the analogous slope--intercept data
$m_B\theta\,\Delta\theta$, $b_B\theta\,\Delta\theta$ of the neighboring
parallel ray B incident at $\theta + \Delta\theta$ (ray-B data is setup
context for parts C.2--C.4).  Bundled governing laws: $\theta$ is confined
to the acute branch $(0, \pi/2)$ of Figure~2g; the Figure-2g coordinate
readout $(P_x\theta, P_y\theta) = (R\sin\theta, R\cos\theta)$; the
specular reflection law at $P\theta$ (the reflected line passes through
the reflection point, $P_y\theta / R = \cos\theta$ fixes the incidence
angle against the outward radial normal, the outgoing ray makes the same
angle $\theta$ with that normal, and its tangential component is the
specular reversal of the incoming one); and the same law applied to ray B
at $\theta+\Delta\theta$ for $0 < \Delta\theta < \theta$.  No field or
law states the values of $m_A$ or $b_A$ in advance; extracting them is
the content of the subquestion.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure HalfCylindricalMirrorReflection where

  R : ℝ

  R_pos : 0 < R

  P_x : ℝ → ℝ

  P_y : ℝ → ℝ

  m_A : ℝ → ℝ

  b_A : ℝ → ℝ

  m_B : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ

  b_B : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ

  θ_branch : ∀ θ : ℝ, θ ∈ Set.Ioo 0 (π / 2)

  P_eq : ∀ θ : ℝ, P_x θ = R * sin θ ∧ P_y θ = R * cos θ

  reflection_law :
    ∀ θ : ℝ,
      P_y θ = m_A θ * P_x θ + b_A θ ∧
      P_y θ / R = cos θ ∧
      (P_x θ + m_A θ * P_y θ) /
          (R * Real.sqrt (m_A θ ^ 2 + 1)) = P_y θ / R ∧
      (P_y θ - m_A θ * P_x θ) /
          (R * Real.sqrt (m_A θ ^ 2 + 1)) = P_x θ / R ∧
      0 < P_x θ + m_A θ * P_y θ

  ray_B_reflection_law :
    ∀ θ Δθ : ℝ, 0 < Δθ → Δθ < θ →
      P_y (θ + Δθ) = m_B θ Δθ * P_x (θ + Δθ) + b_B θ Δθ ∧
      P_y (θ + Δθ) / R = cos (θ + Δθ) ∧
      (P_x (θ + Δθ) + m_B θ Δθ * P_y (θ + Δθ)) /
          (R * Real.sqrt (m_B θ Δθ ^ 2 + 1)) = P_y (θ + Δθ) / R ∧
      (P_y (θ + Δθ) - m_B θ Δθ * P_x (θ + Δθ)) /
          (R * Real.sqrt (m_B θ Δθ ^ 2 + 1)) = P_x (θ + Δθ) / R

nodes.title: The reflected intercept is a length
nodes.statement:
The dimensions of the subquestion's answer: for every incidence angle
$\theta$ there exists a real number $L$ equal to the scaled mirror radius
$R/(2\cos\theta)$ such that the reflected-ray intercept satisfies
$b_A\theta = L$; the intercept is a length scaling linearly with $R$,
while the slope $m_A\theta$ is dimensionless.
nodes.proof_tex:
Exhibiting $L := b_A\theta$ proves the existential directly; the recorded
equality to the scaled radius is the conclusion-side C.1 intercept value
of \cref{thm:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_2_C_1:reflected_ray_A_intercept}.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem intercept_is_length (θ : ℝ) :
    ∃ L : ℝ, L = s.R / (2 * cos θ) ∧ s.b_A θ = L := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Slope of the reflected ray A
nodes.statement:
\textbf{(C.1 answer, slope.)}  For the half-cylindrical mirror of
radius $R$ in the Figure-2g coordinate convention, the slope of the line
reflected from ray A at incidence angle $\theta$ is
$m_A\theta = \cot(2\theta)$, a dimensionless quantity.  This is a
conclusion-side target of the subquestion, not an assumption: no clause
of the governing-law structure states it in advance.
nodes.proof_tex:
The specular law at the reflection point
$(R\sin\theta, R\cos\theta)$ constrains the reflected direction
$(1, m_A\theta)$: the angle-equality and tangential-reversal conditions
form a two-by-two linear system in the direction components whose
solution is the line inclined at $2\theta$ from the vertical, whence
$m_A\theta = \cot(2\theta)$.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem reflected_ray_A_slope (θ : ℝ) :
    s.m_A θ = cot (2 * θ) := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Intercept of the reflected ray A
nodes.statement:
\textbf{(C.1 answer, intercept.)}  The intercept of the line reflected
from ray A at incidence angle $\theta$ is
$b_A\theta = R/(2\cos\theta)$, a length.  Conclusion-side only; the
value does not appear in any hypothesis or field of the governing-law
structure.
nodes.proof_tex:
The reflected line passes through the reflection point
$(R\sin\theta, R\cos\theta)$, so
$b_A\theta = P_y\theta - m_A\theta\,P_x\theta$; substituting the
Figure-2g readout of $P$ and the slope
\cref{thm:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_2_C_1:reflected_ray_A_slope}
and simplifying the trigonometric expression yields
$R/(2\cos\theta)$.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem reflected_ray_A_intercept (θ : ℝ) :
    s.b_A θ = s.R / (2 * cos θ) := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Slope and intercept of the reflected ray A
nodes.statement:
\textbf{(Target, T2-C1.)}  For the half-cylindrical mirror of radius
$R$, the line $y = m_A\theta\,x + b_A\theta$ reflected from the axial
ray A incident at angle $\theta$ (Figure-2g convention) satisfies
\[
m_A\theta = \cot(2\theta), \qquad b_A\theta = \frac{R}{2\cos\theta} .
\]
This is the recorded official answer of part C.1; both values are
conclusion-side, confined to the target theorems of this chapter.
nodes.proof_tex:
Conjoin the slope bridge
\cref{thm:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_2_C_1:reflected_ray_A_slope}
with the intercept bridge
\cref{thm:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_2_C_1:reflected_ray_A_intercept}.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem reflected_ray_A_slope_and_intercept (θ : ℝ) :
    s.m_A θ = cot (2 * θ) ∧ s.b_A θ = s.R / (2 * cos θ) := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Neighboring-ray expansion package
nodes.statement:
The Figure-2g C.2 package: the half-cylindrical mirror of radius $R > 0$;
the one-parameter reflected slope--intercept family
$\varphi \mapsto (M\,\varphi, B\,\varphi)$ generated by specular reflection
of the axial (parallel-to-$y$) rays, with ray A the member at
$\varphi = \theta$ and the neighboring parallel ray B the member at
$\varphi = \theta + \Delta\theta$; the acute branch datum
$0 < \theta < \pi/2$ keeping the mirror hit on the upper right quarter; the
C.1 recorded values of $m_A(\theta)$ and $b_A(\theta)$ as natural-language
prerequisite hypotheses; and the smooth-governing-law regularity interface,
certifying that $M$ and $B$ each admit a first-order expansion about
$\theta$ with remainder little-$o$ of $\Delta\theta$ (a Mathlib
\texttt{Asymptotics.IsLittleO} contract over the neighborhood filter of
$0$).  All coordinate readouts live in the Figure-2g plane: $R$ and the
intercepts carry the dimension of length, the slopes and angles are
dimensionless.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure NeighboringRayExpansion where

  R : ℝ

  R_pos : 0 < R

  M : ℝ → ℝ

  B : ℝ → ℝ

  m_A : ℝ → ℝ

  b_A : ℝ → ℝ

  m_B : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ

  b_B : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ

  θ : ℝ

  θ_branch : θ ∈ Set.Ioo 0 (π / 2)

  m_A_eq : m_A θ = M θ

  b_A_eq : b_A θ = B θ

  m_B_eq : ∀ Δθ : ℝ, m_B θ Δθ = M (θ + Δθ)

  b_B_eq : ∀ Δθ : ℝ, b_B θ Δθ = B (θ + Δθ)

  m_A_formula : m_A θ = cot (2 * θ)

  b_A_formula : b_A θ = R / (2 * cos θ)

  M_first_order :
    ∃ dm : ℝ, (fun Δθ : ℝ ↦ M (θ + Δθ) - M θ - dm * Δθ) =o[𝓝 0]
      fun Δθ : ℝ ↦ Δθ

  B_first_order :
    ∃ db : ℝ, (fun Δθ : ℝ ↦ B (θ + Δθ) - B θ - db * Δθ) =o[𝓝 0]
      fun Δθ : ℝ ↦ Δθ

nodes.title: Branch denominators are nonzero
nodes.statement:
On the acute Figure-2g branch of the expansion package, the denominators
appearing in the C.1/C.2 formulas do not vanish:
$\sin (2\theta) \neq 0$ and $\cos \theta \neq 0$, so $\cot(2\theta)$,
$\csc(2\theta)$, $\tan\theta$ and the C.1 intercept are all well-formed
quantities of the subquestion.  Bridge lemma only; not a target conclusion.
nodes.proof_tex:
The branch datum gives $0 < \theta < \pi/2$, hence $0 < 2\theta < \pi$;
there $\sin(2\theta) > 0$ and $\cos\theta > 0$, so both are nonzero.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem branch_denominators_ne_zero :
    sin (2 * s.θ) ≠ 0 ∧ cos s.θ ≠ 0 := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Neighboring-ray slope to first order
nodes.statement:
\textbf{(Target, T2-C.2, slope half; coefficients conclusion-side.)}  As
$\Delta\theta \to 0$,
\[
m_B(\theta, \Delta\theta)
= \cot (2\theta) - 2\,\csc(2\theta)^{2}\,\Delta\theta + o(\Delta\theta) ,
\]
stated formally as an \texttt{IsLittleO} contract of the defect
$\Delta\theta \mapsto m_B(\theta,\Delta\theta) -
(\cot(2\theta) - 2\,\csc(2\theta)^2\,\Delta\theta)$ against
$\Delta\theta \mapsto \Delta\theta$ in the neighborhood filter of $0$.
nodes.proof_tex:
Family membership rewrites $m_B(\theta,\Delta\theta) = M(\theta+\Delta\theta)$
and the smooth-governing-law interface expands
$M(\theta+\Delta\theta) = M(\theta) + (\partial_\theta M)\,\Delta\theta
+ o(\Delta\theta)$.  The C.1 value $M(\theta) = \cot(2\theta)$ fixes the
zeroth order; the derivative identity
$(d/d\theta)\cot(2\theta) = -2\csc(2\theta)^2$ of the specular family,
nonsingular on the branch by
\cref{lem:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_2_C_2:branch_denominators_ne_zero},
fixes the first-order coefficient.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem ray_B_slope_first_order :
    (fun Δθ : ℝ ↦
        s.m_B s.θ Δθ - (cot (2 * s.θ) - 2 * (sin (2 * s.θ))⁻¹ ^ 2 * Δθ))
      =o[𝓝 0] fun Δθ : ℝ ↦ Δθ := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Neighboring-ray intercept to first order
nodes.statement:
\textbf{(Target, T2-C.2, intercept half; coefficients conclusion-side.)}
As $\Delta\theta \to 0$,
\[
b_B(\theta, \Delta\theta)
= \frac{R}{2\cos\theta}\,\bigl(1 + \tan\theta\,\Delta\theta\bigr)
+ o(\Delta\theta) ,
\]
stated formally as an \texttt{IsLittleO} contract of the defect against
$\Delta\theta \mapsto \Delta\theta$ in the neighborhood filter of $0$.
nodes.proof_tex:
Family membership rewrites $b_B(\theta,\Delta\theta) = B(\theta+\Delta\theta)$
and the interface expands $B$ to first order with little-$o$ remainder.
The C.1 value $B(\theta) = R/(2\cos\theta)$ fixes the zeroth order; the
derivative identity
$(d/d\theta)\bigl(R/(2\cos\theta)\bigr)
= \bigl(R/(2\cos\theta)\bigr)\tan\theta$ of the specular family fixes the
first-order coefficient.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem ray_B_intercept_first_order :
    (fun Δθ : ℝ ↦
        s.b_B s.θ Δθ -
          (s.R / (2 * cos s.θ)) * (1 + tan s.θ * Δθ))
      =o[𝓝 0] fun Δθ : ℝ ↦ Δθ := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Neighboring-ray first-order expansion (C.2 main target)
nodes.statement:
\textbf{(Target, T2-C.2.)}  The two recorded C.2 expansions hold jointly:
the reflected slope and intercept of the neighboring ray B expand to first
order in $\Delta\theta$ with remainders little-$o$ of $\Delta\theta$ ---
the faithful first-order content of the official $+\,O(\Delta\theta^{2})$
phrasing.  The expansion coefficients appear only here and in the two halves
above, never hypothesis-side.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem ray_B_first_order_expansion :
    ((fun Δθ : ℝ ↦
          s.m_B s.θ Δθ - (cot (2 * s.θ) - 2 * (sin (2 * s.θ))⁻¹ ^ 2 * Δθ))
        =o[𝓝 0] fun Δθ : ℝ ↦ Δθ) ∧
      ((fun Δθ : ℝ ↦
          s.b_B s.θ Δθ -
            (s.R / (2 * cos s.θ)) * (1 + tan s.θ * Δθ))
        =o[𝓝 0] fun Δθ : ℝ ↦ Δθ) := by
  exact ⟨s.ray_B_slope_first_order, s.ray_B_intercept_first_order⟩

nodes.title: Physical length
nodes.statement:
A physical length as a dimensionful quantity of the Physlib units API
(a value of the length dimension over $\mathbb{R}$): one value packages
its numerical readouts in every unit system, related by the dimensional
scaling law, rather than a bare real number in an implicit unit.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
abbrev PhysicalLength :=
  Dimensionful (WithDim Dimension.L𝓭 ℝ)

nodes.title: Figure-2g length projection
nodes.statement:
The fixed length-unit choice \texttt{unitChoice : UnitChoices} for all
Figure-2g coordinate readouts, together with the named scalar projection
sending a physical length to its real coordinate readout
$(\textit{length}\ \textit{unitChoice}).\textit{val} : \mathbb{R}$ in that
unit.  \emph{Modeling choice (typed readout):} every Figure-2g coordinate
appearing below is read through this \emph{single} projection and this one
fixed unit, so physical lengths are never silently identified with bare
real numbers and no equation mixes two unit systems.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure Figure2gLengthProjection where
  unitChoice : UnitChoices

def Figure2gLengthProjection.readout
    (projection : Figure2gLengthProjection) (length : PhysicalLength) : ℝ :=
  (length projection.unitChoice).val

nodes.title: Half-cylindrical mirror of Figure 2g
nodes.statement:
The half-cylindrical mirror: a physical-length \texttt{radius} $R$ with a
positivity certificate at every unit choice.  Its reflecting upper
semicircle is the predicate $x^2 + y^2 = R^2 \wedge 0 \le y$ on Figure-2g
points, expressed through the fixed unit readout.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure Figure2gMirror where
  radius : PhysicalLength
  radius_pos : ∀ unitChoice : UnitChoices, 0 < (radius unitChoice).val

def Figure2gMirror.OnReflectingSurface
    (projection : Figure2gLengthProjection)
    (mirror : Figure2gMirror) (point : Figure2gPoint) : Prop :=
  projection.readout point.xCoordinate ^ 2 +
        projection.readout point.yCoordinate ^ 2 =
      projection.readout mirror.radius ^ 2 ∧
    0 ≤ projection.readout point.yCoordinate

nodes.title: Point of Figure 2g
nodes.statement:
A point of the Figure-2g coordinate plane: two physical-length
coordinates \texttt{xCoordinate}, \texttt{yCoordinate} (not bare reals).
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure Figure2gPoint where
  xCoordinate : PhysicalLength
  yCoordinate : PhysicalLength

nodes.title: Supporting line of a reflected ray
nodes.statement:
The supporting affine line $y = m x + b$ of a reflected optical ray in
Figure 2g: a dimensionless \texttt{slopeRatio} $m$ and a physical-length
\texttt{yIntercept} $b$; a point lies on the line when
$y_{\mathrm{rd}} = m\,x_{\mathrm{rd}} + b_{\mathrm{rd}}$ under the fixed
unit readout.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure ReflectedRayLine where
  slopeRatio : ℝ
  yIntercept : PhysicalLength

def ReflectedRayLine.Contains
    (projection : Figure2gLengthProjection)
    (ray : ReflectedRayLine) (point : Figure2gPoint) : Prop :=
  projection.readout point.yCoordinate =
    ray.slopeRatio * projection.readout point.xCoordinate +
      projection.readout ray.yIntercept

nodes.title: Intersection of neighboring reflected rays
nodes.statement:
Simultaneous membership of a Figure-2g point in the reflected line at
incidence angle $\theta$ (ray A) and in the reflected line at the
neighboring incidence angle $\theta + \Delta\theta$ (ray B): both line
equations hold at once.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
def IsNeighboringReflectedIntersection
    (projection : Figure2gLengthProjection)
    (reflectedRayAtIncidenceAngle : ℝ → ReflectedRayLine)
    (θ Δθ : ℝ) (point : Figure2gPoint) : Prop :=
  (reflectedRayAtIncidenceAngle θ).Contains projection point ∧
    (reflectedRayAtIncidenceAngle (θ + Δθ)).Contains projection point

nodes.title: Limiting intersection of neighboring reflected rays
nodes.statement:
For the half-cylindrical mirror of radius $R$ in the coordinate system of
Figure~2g, the intersection of the reflected ray A (incidence angle $\theta$)
with the reflected neighboring ray B (incidence angle $\theta+\Delta\theta$)
tends, as $\Delta\theta\to 0$, to the caustic point
\[
X_c = R\sin^3\theta, \qquad Y_c = \frac{R}{2}\cos\theta\,\bigl(2-\cos 2\theta\bigr).
\]
Here the exact line of part C.1 ($m_A = \cot 2\theta$,
$b_A = R/(2\cos\theta)$), the first-order $O(\Delta\theta^2)$ expansions of
$m_B, b_B$ of part C.2, and the existence of the intersection for all
sufficiently small nonzero $\Delta\theta$ enter as natural-language
hypotheses recorded in the theorem's hypothesis structures; only the two
limit coordinate statements are conclusion-side.
nodes.proof_tex:
Subtracting the two line equations at the intersection point gives
$b_B - b_A = -(m_B - m_A)\cdot X$.  By the C.1 values and the C.2
expansions, $m_B - m_A = -\bigl(2/\sin^2 2\theta + O(\Delta\theta)\bigr)
\,\Delta\theta$ and
$b_B - b_A = \bigl(\partial b/\partial\theta + O(\Delta\theta)\bigr)
\,\Delta\theta$ with
$\partial b/\partial\theta = R\sin\theta/(2\cos^2\theta)$; substituting and
dividing through by $\Delta\theta \to 0$ yields
$X_c = R\sin^3\theta$, and then $Y_c = \frac{R}{2}\cos\theta\,(2-\cos 2\theta)$
follows from the ray-A line $Y_c = \cot 2\theta\cdot X_c + R/(2\cos\theta)$
via the trig identity
$\frac{R}{2}\cos\theta\,(2-\cos 2\theta)
= \cot 2\theta\cdot R\sin^3\theta + R/(2\cos\theta)$.
All trigonometric manipulations and the limit passage are at the informal
level here; the formal counterpart is the prover stage's (currently
sorried) proof body in Lean.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem limitingIntersectionCoordinates
    (lengthProjection : Figure2gLengthProjection)
    (mirror : Figure2gMirror)
    (θ : ℝ)
    (reflectedRayAtIncidenceAngle : ℝ → ReflectedRayLine)
    (neighboringIntersection : ℝ → Figure2gPoint)
    (hθ_pos : 0 < θ)
    (hθ_acute : θ < Real.pi / 2)
    (hRayA_slope :
      (reflectedRayAtIncidenceAngle θ).slopeRatio =
        Real.cot (2 * θ))
    (hRayA_intercept :
      lengthProjection.readout
          (reflectedRayAtIncidenceAngle θ).yIntercept =
        lengthProjection.readout mirror.radius / (2 * Real.cos θ))
    (hRayB_slope_firstOrder :
      (fun Δθ : ℝ ↦
          (reflectedRayAtIncidenceAngle (θ + Δθ)).slopeRatio -
            (Real.cot (2 * θ) -
              2 * (Real.sin (2 * θ))⁻¹ ^ 2 * Δθ))
        =O[𝓝 0] (fun Δθ : ℝ ↦ Δθ ^ 2))
    (hRayB_intercept_firstOrder :
      (fun Δθ : ℝ ↦
          lengthProjection.readout
              (reflectedRayAtIncidenceAngle (θ + Δθ)).yIntercept -
            ((lengthProjection.readout mirror.radius /
                (2 * Real.cos θ)) *
              (1 + Real.tan θ * Δθ)))
        =O[𝓝 0] (fun Δθ : ℝ ↦ Δθ ^ 2))
    (hNeighboringIntersection :
      ∀ᶠ Δθ in 𝓝[≠] (0 : ℝ),
        IsNeighboringReflectedIntersection
          lengthProjection reflectedRayAtIncidenceAngle
          θ Δθ (neighboringIntersection Δθ)) :
    Tendsto
        (fun Δθ ↦
          lengthProjection.readout
            (neighboringIntersection Δθ).xCoordinate)
        (𝓝[≠] (0 : ℝ))
        (𝓝
          (lengthProjection.readout mirror.radius *
            Real.sin θ ^ 3)) ∧
      Tendsto
        (fun Δθ ↦
          lengthProjection.readout
            (neighboringIntersection Δθ).yCoordinate)
        (𝓝[≠] (0 : ℝ))
        (𝓝
          ((lengthProjection.readout mirror.radius / 2) * Real.cos θ *
            (2 - Real.cos (2 * θ)))) := by
  constructor <;> sorry

nodes.title: Half-cylindrical mirror caustic data
nodes.statement:
The physical setup of the C-parts of IPhO 2026 Problem 2: the
half-cylindrical mirror of Figure~2g recorded by its radius $R$ with a
positivity certificate, the slopes and intercepts
$y = m_A\,x + b_A$, $y = m_B\,x + b_B$ of the lines reflected from ray A
(incidence angle $\theta$) and from the neighboring parallel ray B
(incidence angle $\theta + \Delta\theta$), and the limiting intersection
coordinates $(X_c\,\theta, Y_c\,\theta)$ of the two reflected lines as
$\Delta\theta \to 0$.  All coordinates are Cartesian reals in the plane of
Figure~2g; $R$, $X_c$, $Y_c$ carry the dimension of length.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure HalfCylindricalMirrorCaustic where

  R : ℝ

  R_pos : 0 < R

  m_A : ℝ → ℝ

  b_A : ℝ → ℝ

  m_B : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ

  b_B : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ

  X_c : ℝ → ℝ

  Y_c : ℝ → ℝ

  envelope_law :
    ∀ θ : ℝ, ∀ᶠ Δθ in nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0),
      ∃! p : ℝ × ℝ,
        p.2 = m_A θ * p.1 + b_A θ ∧
        p.2 = m_B θ Δθ * p.1 + b_B θ Δθ

  X_c_formula : ∀ θ : ℝ, X_c θ = R * sin θ ^ 3

  Y_c_formula : ∀ θ : ℝ, Y_c θ = R / 2 * cos θ * (2 - cos (2 * θ))

nodes.title: Small-angle filter
nodes.statement:
The small-$\theta$ regime $\theta \ll 1$ stipulated in the subquestion,
carried by the filter of neighborhoods of $0$ within the positive
incidence angles.  Taking the positive side is the branch/orientation data:
it makes the absolute value $|X_c|$ of the source statement harmless ($X_c$
is positive for small positive $\theta$) and selects the physical branch of
the power law.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source: noncomputable def smallAngleFilter : Filter ℝ := nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0)

nodes.title: Small-angle regime predicate
nodes.statement:
The plain-English reading of $\theta \ll 1$ as a predicate on an incidence
angle: $\theta$ is positive and strictly smaller than one radian.  The
neighborhoods of the small-angle filter carry the operative asymptotic
notion; this predicate only names the regime.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
def InSmallAngleRegime (θ : ℝ) : Prop :=
  0 < θ ∧ θ < 1

nodes.title: Caustic power-law form
nodes.statement:
The $\theta \ll 1$ power-law form of a parametric plane curve
$\theta \mapsto (X\,\theta, Y\,\theta)$: the exponent $p/q$ is a positive
rational, the coordinate functions have a well-defined positive
leading-order balance as $\theta \to 0^{+}$ along the small-angle filter ---
$Y$ agrees to leading order with $v\,X^{p/q} + u$ and $X$ with a positive
scale times $\theta^{q}$, in the sense of asymptotic equivalence.  Here $u$
and $v$ carry the dimension of length and $p/q$ is dimensionless.  This is
the genuine asymptotic content of the subquestion: the two sides agree to
leading order without being required to coincide exactly (they do not for
the mirror caustic).  All quantities are parameters of the definition, so
nothing here is specialized to the recorded answer.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
def CausticPowerLawForm (X Y : ℝ → ℝ) (u v : ℝ) (p q : ℕ) : Prop :=
  0 < p ∧ 0 < q ∧
  (fun θ : ℝ => Y θ) ~[smallAngleFilter]
    (fun θ => v * X θ ^ ((p : ℝ) / (q : ℝ)) + u) ∧
  ∃ w : ℝ, 0 < w ∧
    (fun θ : ℝ => X θ) ~[smallAngleFilter] (fun θ => w * θ ^ q)

nodes.title: Caustic power law with the C.4 constants
nodes.statement:
The power-law form with the recorded constants of subquestion C.4 made
explicit: the vertical shift $u$ and the prefactor $v$ are the ones
determined from the mirror geometry, and the exponent is $p/q = 2/3$.
Packaging predicate over the generic power-law form; it asserts no value by
itself.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
def SatisfiesCausticPowerLaw (X Y : ℝ → ℝ) (R u v : ℝ) : Prop :=
  u = R / 2 ∧
  v = (3 / 4) * R ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 3) ∧
  CausticPowerLawForm X Y u v 2 3

nodes.title: Small-angle regime is a filter neighborhood
nodes.statement:
The set of incidence angles satisfying the small-angle regime predicate is a
neighborhood of $0$ within the positive angles, so statements eventually
true along the small-angle filter apply to the whole regime.
nodes.proof_tex:
The open half-line below one radian is an open set containing $0$, and
inside it membership in the regime predicate is exactly positivity; hence
the predicate set agrees with the positive half-line on a neighborhood of
$0$.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem smallAngleRegime_mem_filter :
    {θ : ℝ | InSmallAngleRegime θ} ∈ smallAngleFilter := by
  rw [smallAngleFilter, mem_nhdsWithin]
  exact ⟨Set.Iio 1, isOpen_Iio, by simp, fun θ hθ => ⟨hθ.2, hθ.1⟩⟩

nodes.title: C.4 target: small-angle caustic power law
nodes.statement:
\textbf{(Target, T2-C.4.)}  In the small-angle regime $\theta \ll 1$, the
caustic of the half-cylindrical mirror of radius $R$ has the power-law form
\[
Y_c = v\,|X_c|^{p/q} + u
\quad\text{with}\quad
u = \frac{R}{2},\qquad
v = \frac{3}{4}\,R^{1/3},\qquad
p = 2,\qquad q = 3,
\]
read as asymptotic agreement to leading order as $\theta \to 0^{+}$.  The
$|X_c|$ of the source statement is subsumed by the positive-angle branch of
the small-angle filter, where $X_c\,\theta$ is positive.  This is the
recorded official answer of part C.4; the values are conclusion-side only,
confined to this target theorem (no hypothesis or structure field states
them in advance).
nodes.proof_tex:
Insert the previous-part coordinates of the caustic (part C.3, recorded as
hypotheses on the caustic data) into both sides and expand about
$\theta = 0$: $Y_c\,\theta$ is $R/2$ plus its leading quadratic term, while
$|X_c\,\theta|^{2/3}$ carries the matching leading quadratic term with
prefactor fixed by the geometry, and $X_c$ itself matches a positive
multiple of $\theta^{3}$; the recorded constants are exactly the ones making
the leading terms coincide, so the two sides are asymptotically equivalent
along the small-angle filter.  An exact identity at every small $\theta$ is
false for this caustic --- the residual is higher order --- which is why the
agreement is stated to leading order.  All expansions are at the informal
level here; the formal counterpart is the prover stage's (currently
sorried) proof body in Lean.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem caustic_small_angle_power_law :
    SatisfiesCausticPowerLaw c.X_c c.Y_c c.R (c.R / 2)
      ((3 / 4) * c.R ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 3)) := by
  sorry
