nodes.title: Free space and instantaneous current
nodes.statement:
The permeability of free space $\mu_0$ packaged as a named positive record,
and the instantaneous current in the wire as an amount-with-readout wrapper
(its scalar readout in amperes); the extensionality theorem identifies two
currents with equal readouts.
nodes.lean_source:
structure FreeSpace where

  μ₀ : ℝ

  μ₀_pos : 0 < μ₀

structure InstantaneousCurrent where

  readout : ℝ

theorem InstantaneousCurrent.ext {i j : InstantaneousCurrent}
    (h : i.readout = j.readout) : i = j := by
  cases i; cases j; simp_all

nodes.title: Radial profile and H-field readouts
nodes.statement:
Function-space habitats: a radial profile is a real-valued function of the
radial coordinate, and an H-field readout on a turn-index type is a
per-turn real magnitude readout (A/m).
nodes.lean_source:
abbrev RadialProfile := ℝ → ℝ

abbrev HFieldReadouts (Turn : Type*) := Turn → ℝ

nodes.title: Amperian filament
nodes.statement:
A single turn of the winding treated as an amperian filament: an indexed
turn carrying an instantaneous current certified free and nonnegative;
the consequence theorems re-export freeness and nonnegativity of the
readout.
nodes.lean_source:
structure AmperianFilament (Turn : Type*) where

  turn : Turn

  i : InstantaneousCurrent

  i_nonneg : 0 ≤ i.readout

  isFreeCurrent : Prop

  freeHolds : isFreeCurrent

theorem is_free (f : AmperianFilament Turn) : f.isFreeCurrent := f.freeHolds

theorem current_nonneg (f : AmperianFilament Turn) : 0 ≤ f.i.readout :=
  f.i_nonneg

nodes.title: Ampère circulation law
nodes.statement:
Ampère's law on a finite index of loops: the circulation of the field
magnitude along each loop equals the enclosed free current; the
\texttt{circulation} theorem extracts the per-loop equation and
\texttt{circulation\_constant} its constant-magnitude specialization.
nodes.lean_source:
structure AmpereLaw (α : Type*) [Fintype α] where

  HasRadialProfile : RadialProfile

  turnCurrent : α → InstantaneousCurrent

  circulation_eq :
    ∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ →
      (2 * Real.pi * ρ) * HasRadialProfile ρ
        = ∑ t : α, (turnCurrent t).readout

theorem circulation {α : Type*} [Fintype α]
    (law : AmpereLaw α) (ρ : ℝ) (hρ : 0 < ρ) :
    (2 * Real.pi * ρ) * law.HasRadialProfile ρ =
      ∑ t : α, (law.turnCurrent t).readout :=
  law.circulation_eq ρ hρ

theorem circulation_constant {α : Type*} [Fintype α]
    (law : AmpereLaw α) {ρ ρ' : ℝ} (hρ : 0 < ρ) (hρ' : 0 < ρ') :
    (2 * Real.pi * ρ) * law.HasRadialProfile ρ
      = (2 * Real.pi * ρ') * law.HasRadialProfile ρ' := by
  rw [law.circulation_eq ρ hρ, law.circulation_eq ρ' hρ']

nodes.title: Finite winding
nodes.statement:
A dense winding of $N$ turns: a finite turn-index type with its equivalence
to $\mathrm{Fin}\,N$; \texttt{card} certifies the turn count is exactly $N$.
nodes.lean_source:
structure FiniteWinding (N : ℕ) where

  Turn : Type*

  turnFintype : Fintype Turn

  turnEquiv : Turn ≃ Fin N

attribute [instance] FiniteWinding.turnFintype

theorem card {N : ℕ} (w : FiniteWinding N) :
    @Fintype.card w.Turn w.turnFintype = N :=
  (@Fintype.card_congr _ _ w.turnFintype _ w.turnEquiv).trans (Fintype.card_fin N)

nodes.title: Ampère law on the thin mean path
nodes.statement:
The thin-torus ($r \ll R$) specialization of Ampère's law: the mean path of
length $2\pi R$ encloses all $N$ turns, each carrying its
current, with per-turn magnitude readout; carries the geometry parameters
$R, r, A, V$ (positive, $V = 2\pi R A$). Consequences: the sum form
$\sum_t 2\pi R\, H_t = \sum_t I_t$, the mean-circumference identities, and
positivity of $2\pi R$.
nodes.lean_source:
structure AmpereLawThinMeanPath (N : ℕ) (w : FiniteWinding N) where

  R : ℝ

  r : ℝ

  A : ℝ

  V : ℝ

  R_pos : 0 < R

  r_pos : 0 < r

  thin : r < R

  A_pos : 0 < A

  V_pos : 0 < V

  V_eq : V = 2 * Real.pi * R * A

  turnCurrent : w.Turn → InstantaneousCurrent

  HOf : HFieldReadouts w.Turn

  ampere_sum :
    ∑ t : w.Turn, (2 * Real.pi * R) * HOf t
      = ∑ t : w.Turn, (turnCurrent t).readout

theorem ampere_sum_const (law : AmpereLawThinMeanPath N w) {H : ℝ}
    (h : ∀ t : w.Turn, law.HOf t = H) :
    ∑ t : w.Turn, (2 * Real.pi * law.R) * law.HOf t
      = (N : ℝ) * ((2 * Real.pi * law.R) * H) := by
  have hc : ∀ t : w.Turn,
      (2 * Real.pi * law.R) * law.HOf t = (2 * Real.pi * law.R) * H :=
    fun t => by rw [h t]
  rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun t _ => hc t), Finset.sum_const]
  have hcard : (Finset.univ : Finset w.Turn).card = N := by
    rw [Finset.card_univ]
    exact w.card
  rw [hcard, nsmul_eq_mul]

theorem mean_circumference_eq (law : AmpereLawThinMeanPath N w) :
    2 * Real.pi * law.R = law.V / law.A := by
  have hA : law.A ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt law.A_pos
  rw [law.V_eq]
  field_simp

theorem mean_circumference_mul_eq (law : AmpereLawThinMeanPath N w) :
    2 * Real.pi * law.R * law.A = law.V := by
  have hA : law.A ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt law.A_pos
  calc 2 * Real.pi * law.R * law.A = law.V / law.A * law.A := by
        rw [law.mean_circumference_eq]
    _ = law.V := div_mul_cancel₀ law.V hA

theorem mean_circumference_pos (law : AmpereLawThinMeanPath N w) :
    0 < 2 * Real.pi * law.R :=
  mul_pos (mul_pos two_pos Real.pi_pos) law.R_pos

nodes.title: Uniform field magnitude interface
nodes.statement:
The uniformity interface for an approximately uniform field inside the
torus: a constant magnitude $H$ agreeing with every per-turn readout, so
the piecewise readout equals $H$ and any two turns read the same value.
nodes.lean_source:
structure UniformFieldMag (Turn : Type*) where

  H : ℝ

  H_nonneg : 0 ≤ H

  HField : HFieldReadouts Turn

  piecewise : HFieldReadouts Turn

  piecewise_eq : ∀ t : Turn, piecewise t = HField t

  uniform : ∀ t : Turn, HField t = H

theorem piecewise_eq_H (u : UniformFieldMag Turn) (t : Turn) :
    u.piecewise t = u.H := by
  rw [u.piecewise_eq t, u.uniform t]

theorem uniform_across (u : UniformFieldMag Turn) (t s : Turn) :
    u.HField t = u.HField s := by
  rw [u.uniform t, u.uniform s]

nodes.title: Uniform-material winding law
nodes.statement:
Along the mean path each turn behaves as an amperian filament carrying the
winding current, and the circulation of the per-turn magnitude equals the
total filament (free) current — the official hint's reading of $I_C$ in
$\oint \vec{H}\cdot d\vec{\ell} = I_C$; the two named theorems are its
elimination and freeness re-export.
nodes.lean_source:
structure AmperianFilamentLaw (N : ℕ) (w : FiniteWinding N) where

  base : AmpereLawThinMeanPath N w

  filament : w.Turn → AmperianFilament w.Turn

  filament_turn : ∀ t : w.Turn, (filament t).turn = t

  filament_current : ∀ t : w.Turn, (filament t).i = base.turnCurrent t

  uniform : ∃ u : UniformFieldMag w.Turn, ∀ t : w.Turn, u.HField t = base.HOf t

theorem circulation_eq_filament_current (law : AmperianFilamentLaw N w) :
    ∑ t : w.Turn, (2 * Real.pi * law.base.R) * law.base.HOf t
      = ∑ t : w.Turn, ((law.filament t).i).readout := by
  rw [law.base.ampere_sum]
  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun t _ =>
    congrArg InstantaneousCurrent.readout (law.filament_current t).symm

theorem filament_is_free (law : AmperianFilamentLaw N w) (t : w.Turn) :
    (law.filament t).isFreeCurrent := (law.filament t).is_free

nodes.title: Vacuum-core constitutive identity
nodes.statement:
The electromagnetic material law recorded for downstream parts (not needed
for A.1 itself): pointwise $B = \mu_0 H + \mu_0 M$ with $H$ and $M$
constant-magnitude in the region and $M$ parallel to $H$ (paramagnetic
branch, $M = \chi H$, $\chi \ge 0$); consequences rewrite $B$ as the scaled
field and certify uniformity.
nodes.lean_source:
structure VacuumCoreIdentity (Space : Type*) where

  freeSpace : FreeSpace

  hField : Space → ℝ

  mField : Space → ℝ

  bField : Space → ℝ

  b_eq :
    ∀ x : Space,
      bField x = freeSpace.μ₀ * hField x + freeSpace.μ₀ * mField x

  h_const : ∃ H : ℝ, ∀ x : Space, hField x = H

  m_const : ∃ M : ℝ, ∀ x : Space, mField x = M

  m_parallel : ∃ χ : ℝ, 0 ≤ χ ∧ ∀ x : Space, mField x = χ * hField x

theorem b_eq_scaled (v : VacuumCoreIdentity Space) (x : Space) :
    ∃ χ : ℝ, 0 ≤ χ ∧
      v.bField x = v.freeSpace.μ₀ * (1 + χ) * v.hField x := by
  obtain ⟨χ, hχ, hm⟩ := v.m_parallel
  exact ⟨χ, hχ, by rw [v.b_eq x, hm x]; ring⟩

theorem b_uniform (v : VacuumCoreIdentity Space) :
    ∃ B : ℝ, ∀ x : Space, v.bField x = B := by
  obtain ⟨H, hH⟩ := v.h_const
  obtain ⟨M, hM⟩ := v.m_const
  exact ⟨v.freeSpace.μ₀ * H + v.freeSpace.μ₀ * M,
    fun x => by rw [v.b_eq x, hH x, hM x]⟩

nodes.title: Paramagnetic torus of Part A.1
nodes.statement:
The full problem-parameter package: $N \ge 1$ turns of dense winding, mean
radius $R > 0$, tube radius $r$ with $0 < r < R$ (thin-torus regime),
cross-section $A > 0$, volume $V = 2\pi R A > 0$, series wire current $I$
(same through every turn), the interior field magnitude $H \ge 0$ under
measurement (never fixed by fiat), and the embedding equations tying the
thin-mean-path Ampère law to these parameters with uniform per-turn
readout $H$. No field states the target $H = NIA/V$.
nodes.lean_source:
structure ParamagneticTorusA1 where

  numTurns : ℕ

  numTurns_pos : 0 < numTurns

  winding : FiniteWinding numTurns

  meanRadius : ℝ

  innerRadius : ℝ

  thin : innerRadius < meanRadius

  meanRadius_pos : 0 < meanRadius

  innerRadius_pos : 0 < innerRadius

  crossSectionArea : ℝ

  crossSectionArea_pos : 0 < crossSectionArea

  volume : ℝ

  volume_pos : 0 < volume

  volume_eq : volume = 2 * Real.pi * meanRadius * crossSectionArea

  wireCurrent : InstantaneousCurrent

  wireCurrent_nonneg : 0 ≤ wireCurrent.readout

  fieldMagnitude : ℝ

  fieldMagnitude_nonneg : 0 ≤ fieldMagnitude

  ampere : AmpereLawThinMeanPath numTurns winding

  ampere_R : ampere.R = meanRadius

  ampere_r : ampere.r = innerRadius

  ampere_A : ampere.A = crossSectionArea

  ampere_V : ampere.V = volume

  ampere_current : ∀ t : winding.Turn, ampere.turnCurrent t = wireCurrent

  ampere_uniform : ∀ t : winding.Turn, ampere.HOf t = fieldMagnitude

theorem winding_card (T : ParamagneticTorusA1) :
    @Fintype.card T.winding.Turn T.winding.turnFintype = T.numTurns :=
  T.winding.card

nodes.title: Bridge 1 — Ampère in the uniform regime
nodes.statement:
The circulation of the uniform magnitude along the mean path equals the
total threading free current: $2\pi R \cdot (N H) = N I$.
nodes.proof_tex:
Sum the per-turn magnitudes (all equal to $H$ by uniformity) against the
per-turn currents (all equal to $I$ by the series winding) in the embedded
thin-mean-path Ampère equation; left to the prover stage.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem ampere_uniform_eq (T : ParamagneticTorusA1) :
    2 * Real.pi * T.meanRadius * ((T.numTurns : ℝ) * T.fieldMagnitude)
      = (T.numTurns : ℝ) * T.wireCurrent.readout := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Bridge 2 — solve for $H$ along the mean path
nodes.statement: $H = N I / (2\pi R)$.
nodes.proof_tex:
Divide Bridge 1 by $N \cdot 2\pi R \neq 0$ (uses $N \ge 1$, $R > 0$,
$\pi > 0$).
nodes.lean_source:
theorem fieldMagnitude_eq_meanRadius_form (T : ParamagneticTorusA1) :
    T.fieldMagnitude
      = (T.numTurns : ℝ) * T.wireCurrent.readout
          / (2 * Real.pi * T.meanRadius) := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Bridge 3 — geometry rewrite of the mean circumference
nodes.statement: $2\pi R = V / A$.
nodes.proof_tex: Field-simplify the thin-torus volume law $V = 2\pi R A$ using $A > 0$.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem mean_circumference_eq (T : ParamagneticTorusA1) :
    2 * Real.pi * T.meanRadius = T.volume / T.crossSectionArea := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Bridge 4 — figure parametrization of the answer
nodes.statement: $N I / (2\pi R) = N I A / V$.
nodes.proof_tex:
Substitute Bridge 3 into the denominator
(uses $2\pi R > 0$, $V > 0$).
nodes.lean_source:
theorem meanRadius_form_eq_volume_form (T : ParamagneticTorusA1) :
    (T.numTurns : ℝ) * T.wireCurrent.readout / (2 * Real.pi * T.meanRadius)
      = (T.numTurns : ℝ) * T.wireCurrent.readout * T.crossSectionArea
          / T.volume := by
  sorry

nodes.title: A.1 main target: $H = NIA/V$
nodes.statement:
The magnitude of $\vec{H}$ inside the paramagnetic torus, in terms of
$N$, $A$, $V$ and the instantaneous current $I$, is
$H = N I A / V$.
nodes.proof_tex:
Chain Bridge 2 ($H = NI/(2\pi R)$) with Bridge 4
($NI/(2\pi R) = NIA/V$).
nodes.lean_source:
theorem paramagneticTorus_H_eq (T : ParamagneticTorusA1) :
    T.fieldMagnitude
      = (T.numTurns : ℝ) * T.wireCurrent.readout * T.crossSectionArea
          / T.volume := by
  sorry

nodes.title: A.1 answer in mean-radius form
nodes.statement:
Equivalent form obtained directly from Ampère's law before the geometry
substitution: $H = N I / (2\pi R)$.
nodes.proof_tex: Restatement of Bridge 2.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem paramagneticTorus_H_eq_meanRadius (T : ParamagneticTorusA1) :
    T.fieldMagnitude
      = (T.numTurns : ℝ) * T.wireCurrent.readout
          / (2 * Real.pi * T.meanRadius) := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Physics formalization target
nodes.statement: The assigned autoformalize agent should translate this physics problem into Lean declarations in the covered file, with theorem and lemma proof bodies written as `by sorry`.
nodes.proof_tex: This is an autoformalization task, not a proof task. Produce faithful statements that can later be proved without weakening the source contract.

nodes.title: Strictly positive scalar
nodes.statement:
A local positive-real constraint, $\mathtt{IsPositive}\ x \leftrightarrow 0 < x$,
carrying the physical role ``this scalar is a strictly positive amount''
(length, area, volume, turn count, elapsed time).  Local stand-in for the
PhysLean constraint of the same intent; no governing-law content.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
inductive IsPositive (x : ℝ) : Prop
  | intro : 0 < x → IsPositive x

nodes.title: Toroid geometry and winding data
nodes.statement:
The geometry of the torus and its winding: mean radius $R$, inner radius $r$
with $r < R$ (thin-ring regime), cross-sectional area $A$, volume $V$ of the
paramagnetic material, and the number $N$ of densely wound turns, all bundled
with positivity certificates.  Carries geometric-law content: the ring-volume
identity $V = 2\pi R\,A$ used implicitly in Part A.1, recorded as a bundled
field (an assumed geometric input, not derived).
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure ToroidData where

  R : ℝ

  r : ℝ

  V : ℝ

  A : ℝ

  N : ℝ

  R_pos : IsPositive R

  r_pos : IsPositive r

  thin_ring : r < R

  A_pos : IsPositive A

  V_pos : IsPositive V

  N_pos : IsPositive N

  volume_eq : V = 2 * Real.pi * R * A

nodes.title: Uniform operating point of the magnetized torus
nodes.statement:
The operating state at one instant: the instantaneous current $I$ in the
winding and the uniform fields $H$, $B$, $M$ inside the torus, over a PhysLean
$\mathtt{FreeSpace}$ record.  Carries governing-law content as bundled
hypothesis fields (assumed, not conclusions): the constitutive relation
$B = \mu_0 H + \mu_0 M$ and Ampère's law along the mean circumference,
$H = N I/(2\pi R)$.  The A.2 work identity is not among the fields.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure UniformToroidOperatingPoint (fs : FreeSpace) (t : ToroidData) where

  I : ℝ

  H : ℝ

  B : ℝ

  M : ℝ

  constitutive : B = fs.μ₀ * H + fs.μ₀ * M

  ampere : H = t.N * I / (2 * Real.pi * t.R)

nodes.title: Quasistatic change with induced EMF (Faraday's law)
nodes.statement:
A small quasistatic change: the EMF $\varepsilon$ induced in the $N$-turn
winding over the elapsed time $dt > 0$ while the flux density changes by $dB$.
Carries governing-law content: Faraday's law of induction integrated over the
change, $\varepsilon\,dt = N A\,dB$ (each of the $N$ turns sees the flux
change $A\,dB$), bundled as an equation field.  The Part A.2 answer does not
appear here.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure InducedEMFChange (t : ToroidData) where

  emf : ℝ

  dt : ℝ

  dB : ℝ

  dt_pos : IsPositive dt

  faraday : emf * dt = t.N * t.A * dB

nodes.title: Work delivered by the source, as a typed readout
nodes.statement:
The energy delivered by the external voltage source to the torus circuit as a
typed scalar quantity: $\mathtt{val}$ is positive when work enters the
paramagnetic torus (the IPhO T3 sign convention); withdrawal of energy
($\mathtt{val} < 0$, as when $B$ decreases) is physical, so no nonnegativity
invariant is bundled.  Packaging wrapper only; no governing-law content.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure WorkOnSource where

  val : ℝ

nodes.title: Source work over an induced-EMF change
nodes.statement:
The work performed by the external voltage source over an induced-EMF change at
a given operating point: the electrical power $\varepsilon\,I$ integrated over
the elapsed time, read out as the scalar $\varepsilon\,I\,dt$.  Carries
governing-law content: the energy-balance law of a voltage source
($P = \varepsilon I$); by itself it does not state the Part A.2 answer.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
noncomputable def sourceWork (fs : FreeSpace) (t : ToroidData)
    (op : UniformToroidOperatingPoint fs t) (e : InducedEMFChange t) :
    WorkOnSource :=
  ⟨e.emf * op.I * e.dt⟩

nodes.title: A.1 bridge: field strength in $A/V$ parameters
nodes.statement:
The field magnitude written in the Part-A.1 recorded form,
$H = N I A / V$.  A derivable bridge from the present file's data, not an
assumption: Ampère's law restated through the ring-volume identity.
nodes.proof_tex:
Substitute $1/(2\pi R) = A/V$ — the volume law $V = 2\pi R A$ cleared by
$A > 0$, $V > 0$ — into the bundled Ampère equation $H = N I/(2\pi R)$.
nodes.lean_source:
lemma fieldStrength_eq_N_mul_I_mul_A_div_V
    (fs : FreeSpace) (t : ToroidData) (op : UniformToroidOperatingPoint fs t) :
    op.H = t.N * op.I * t.A / t.V := by
  sorry

nodes.title: A.2 target: source work $dW_{\mathrm{emf}} = V H\,dB$
nodes.statement:
When the magnetic flux density changes by $dB$, the work performed by the
external voltage source is $dW_{\mathrm{emf}} = V H\,dB$ — the recorded
official answer of Part A.2, conclusion-side only: the hypotheses are the
governing laws (Faraday's law, Ampère's law via the A.1 bridge, the
ring-volume law, the source power law), and the conclusion is not among them.
nodes.proof_tex:
Expand the source work as $\varepsilon\,I\,dt = (\varepsilon\,dt)\,I$ and
replace $\varepsilon\,dt$ by $N A\,dB$ from Faraday's law, obtaining
$N A I\,dB$; then rewrite $N A I = V H$ using the A.1 bridge
$H = N I A / V$ (cleared by $V > 0$), concluding $dW_{\mathrm{emf}} = V H\,dB$.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem work_emf_eq_V_mul_H_mul_dB
    (fs : FreeSpace) (t : ToroidData) (op : UniformToroidOperatingPoint fs t)
    (e : InducedEMFChange t) :
    sourceWork fs t op e = ⟨t.V * op.H * e.dB⟩ := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Physics formalization target
nodes.statement: The assigned autoformalize agent should translate this physics problem into Lean declarations in the covered file, with theorem and lemma proof bodies written as `by sorry`.
nodes.proof_tex: This is an autoformalization task, not a proof task. Produce faithful statements that can later be proved without weakening the source contract.

nodes.title: Thin paramagnetic torus
nodes.statement:
Geometry of the thin paramagnetic torus: mean radius $R$, winding radius
$r \ll R$, cross-sectional area $A$, volume $V$, with positivity
certificates $0 < r$, $r < R$, $A > 0$, $V > 0$ and the thin-torus volume
identity $V = 2\pi R\,A$ (an assumed geometric input, not derived).
nodes.proof_tex: Packaging/definition; nothing derived.
nodes.lean_source:
structure PmTTorus where

  R : ℝ

  r : ℝ

  A : ℝ

  V : ℝ

  r_pos : 0 < r

  r_lt_R : r < R

  A_pos : 0 < A

  V_pos : 0 < V

  V_eq : V = 2 * Real.pi * R * A

nodes.title: Dense winding
nodes.statement:
The insulated wire wound densely around the torus: $N$ turns with $N \ge 1$,
carrying an instantaneous signed current $I$ (A); the sign of $I$ fixes the
orientation of the drive relative to the chosen positive $H$ direction.
nodes.proof_tex: Packaging/definition; nothing derived.
nodes.lean_source:
structure PmTWinding where

  N : ℕ

  I : ℝ

  N_pos : 0 < N

nodes.title: Ampère's-law predicate for the torus
nodes.statement:
Ampère's law $\oint \vec{H}\cdot d\vec{\ell} = I_C$ specialized to the
densely wound thin torus: $H = N\,I\,A / V$, with the enclosed free current
$I_C = N I$ through the mean circle. Assumed governing-law input.
nodes.proof_tex: Packaging/definition; nothing derived.
nodes.lean_source:
def AmpereLawTorus (t : PmTTorus) (w : PmTWinding) (H : ℝ) : Prop :=
  H = (w.N : ℝ) * w.I * t.A / t.V

nodes.title: Mean circumference in $V/A$ form
nodes.statement:
The mean circumference of the thin torus is $2\pi R = V/A$ — the geometric
bridge from the loop form of Ampère's law to the $V/A$ form.
nodes.proof_tex: Divide the thin-torus identity $V = 2\pi R\,A$ by $A > 0$ and rearrange.
nodes.lean_source:
lemma meanCircumference_eq (t : PmTTorus) : 2 * Real.pi * t.R = t.V / t.A := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Uniform core field state
nodes.statement:
The instantaneous, approximately uniform electromagnetic state of the core:
field intensity $H$ (A/m), flux density $B$ (T), magnetization $M$ (A/m).
nodes.proof_tex: Packaging/definition; nothing derived.
nodes.lean_source:
structure PmTFieldState where

  H : ℝ

  B : ℝ

  M : ℝ

nodes.title: Constitutive law $B = \mu_0(H+M)$
nodes.statement:
The material's constitutive relation $B = \mu_0 H + \mu_0 M$, an assumed
governing-law input, with $\mu_0$ the free-space permeability supplied by
the PhysLean \texttt{FreeSpace} record $\mathcal{F}$.
nodes.proof_tex: Packaging/definition; nothing derived.
nodes.lean_source:
def ConstitutiveBH (𝓕 : FreeSpace) (s : PmTFieldState) : Prop :=
  s.B = 𝓕.μ₀ * s.H + 𝓕.μ₀ * s.M

nodes.title: Admissible infinitesimal process
nodes.statement:
A current core state together with increments $dB$, $dH$, $dM$ (T, A/m,
A/m) produced by a slight change of the source current. Hypothesis fields
(all assumed governing-law inputs, not conclusions): Ampère's law holds for
the state $H$, the constitutive law holds for the state, and the linearized
constitutive law $dB = \mu_0\,dH + \mu_0\,dM$ holds for the increments.
The increments are formal differentials packaged as reals — a named scalar
projection of the one-form language; this is the documented modeling choice
of this file.
nodes.proof_tex: Packaging/definition; nothing derived.
nodes.lean_source:
structure PmTVariation (t : PmTTorus) (w : PmTWinding) (𝓕 : FreeSpace) where

  s : PmTFieldState

  H_ampere : AmpereLawTorus t w s.H

  BH : ConstitutiveBH 𝓕 s

  dB : ℝ

  dH : ℝ

  dM : ℝ

  dBH : dB = 𝓕.μ₀ * dH + 𝓕.μ₀ * dM

nodes.title: Vacuum-core $B$-increment
nodes.statement:
For a vacuum core ($M = 0$, hence $dM = 0$) the linearized constitutive law
reduces to $dB = \mu_0\,dH$: from $dB = \mu_0\,dH + \mu_0\cdot 0$ conclude
$dB = \mu_0\,dH$. This justifies the vacuum-core contribution in the work
budget below.
nodes.proof_tex: Simplify the additive term $\mu_0\cdot 0$ to zero and cancel.

nodes.title: Infinitesimal work budget of the Pm-T
nodes.statement:
The three licensed inputs of subquestion A.3 (all work entries in joules,
with the sign convention that work entering the paramagnetic torus is
positive): the part-A.2 source-work law $dW_{\mathrm{emf}} = V\,H\,dB$;
the problem statement's split
$dW_{\mathrm{emf}} = dW_{\mathrm{vac}} + dW$ into a vacuum-core part and
the work done on the material itself; and the vacuum-core contribution
$dW_{\mathrm{vac}} = \mu_0\,V\,H\,dH$ (the A.2 law applied to a core with
$M = 0$, with $H$ unchanged because Ampère's law sees only the free
current). The A.3 answer $dW = \mu_0 V H dM$ is \emph{not} among these
fields.
nodes.proof_tex: Packaging/definition; nothing derived.
nodes.lean_source:
structure PmTWorkBudget (t : PmTTorus) (w : PmTWinding) (𝓕 : FreeSpace)
    (v : PmTVariation t w 𝓕) where

  dW_emf : ℝ

  dW_vac : ℝ

  dW : ℝ

  emf_source : dW_emf = t.V * v.s.H * v.dB

  split : dW_emf = dW_vac + dW

  vacuum_part : dW_vac = 𝓕.μ₀ * t.V * v.s.H * v.dH

nodes.title: Material work as the source-minus-vacuum difference
nodes.statement:
Subtracting the vacuum-core contribution isolates the work done on the
material: $dW = dW_{\mathrm{emf}} - dW_{\mathrm{vac}}$.
nodes.proof_tex:
Rearrange the split identity
$dW_{\mathrm{emf}} = dW_{\mathrm{vac}} + dW$ by subtracting
$dW_{\mathrm{vac}}$ from both sides.
nodes.lean_source:
lemma dW_eq_sub_vac (t : PmTTorus) (w : PmTWinding) (𝓕 : FreeSpace)
    (v : PmTVariation t w 𝓕) (b : PmTWorkBudget t w 𝓕 v) :
    b.dW = b.dW_emf - b.dW_vac := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Material work through the increments of $H$ and $B$
nodes.statement:
Substituting the licensed inputs expresses the material work as
$dW = V\,H\,(dB - \mu_0\,dH)$.
nodes.proof_tex:
Replace $dW_{\mathrm{emf}}$ by $V\,H\,dB$ (part A.2) and
$dW_{\mathrm{vac}}$ by $\mu_0\,V\,H\,dH$ in the difference
$dW = dW_{\mathrm{emf}} - dW_{\mathrm{vac}}$, then factor out $V\,H$.
nodes.lean_source:
lemma dW_eq_VH_dB_sub_mu0_dH (t : PmTTorus) (w : PmTWinding) (𝓕 : FreeSpace)
    (v : PmTVariation t w 𝓕) (b : PmTWorkBudget t w 𝓕 v) :
    b.dW = t.V * v.s.H * (v.dB - 𝓕.μ₀ * v.dH) := by
  sorry

nodes.title: A.3 target: work done on the paramagnetic material
nodes.statement:
The work done on the paramagnetic material itself when the magnetization
changes by $dM$ is
\[ dW = \mu_0\,V\,H\,dM, \]
the recorded official answer $dW = \alpha\,V\,\mu_0\,H\,dM$ at $\alpha = 1$.
This is the conclusion of the derivation; it never appears as a hypothesis.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem dW_eq_mu0_V_H_dM (t : PmTTorus) (w : PmTWinding) (𝓕 : FreeSpace)
    (v : PmTVariation t w 𝓕) (b : PmTWorkBudget t w 𝓕 v) :
    b.dW = 𝓕.μ₀ * t.V * v.s.H * v.dM := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Physics formalization target
nodes.statement: The assigned autoformalize agent should translate this physics problem into Lean declarations in the covered file, with theorem and lemma proof bodies written as `by sorry`.
nodes.proof_tex: This is an autoformalization task, not a proof task. Produce faithful statements that can later be proved without weakening the source contract.

nodes.title: Torus parameters
nodes.statement:
The constant parameters of the paramagnetic torus experiment: the
permeability of free space $\mu_0$, the fixed torus volume $V$, the amount
of paramagnetic material $n$ (moles), the material constant $K$ appearing
in the equation of state $T M V = n K H$, and the heat-capacity coefficient
$\lambda$ of $C_M = n\lambda/T^2$.  All fields are physical scalars;
positivity and regularity constraints enter separately as hypotheses where
they are needed.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure TorusParams where

  mu0 : ℝ

  V : ℝ

  n : ℝ

  K : ℝ

  lambda : ℝ

nodes.title: Torus state
nodes.statement:
The variables that vary along a quasistatic process of the torus: the
temperature $T$, the magnetization $M$ (magnetic moment per unit volume),
and the applied magnetic field strength $H$.  The volume is fixed, so it
lives in the parameters record rather than here.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure TorusState where

  T : ℝ

  M : ℝ

  H : ℝ

nodes.title: Heat capacity at constant magnetization
nodes.statement:
The heat capacity at constant magnetization as given in the problem
statement, $C_M(T) = n\lambda/T^2$, as a real-valued readout of the torus
parameters at temperature $T$.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
noncomputable def heatCapacityConstM (p : TorusParams) (T : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  p.n * p.lambda / T ^ 2

nodes.title: Equation of state of the paramagnet
nodes.statement:
The magnetic equation of state of the torus material as a predicate on a
parameter record and a state: $T\,M\,V = n\,K\,H$.  This is a governing law
recorded from the problem statement, not a target.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
def SatisfiesEOS (p : TorusParams) (s : TorusState) : Prop :=
  s.T * s.M * p.V = p.n * p.K * s.H

nodes.title: Heat-capacity law for the internal energy
nodes.statement:
The characterization of the material's internal energy $U$: at constant
magnetization $dU = C_M\,dT$; that is, $U$ is a function of temperature
alone, differentiable at every nonzero $T$ with derivative
$C_M(T) = n\lambda/T^2$.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
def HasHeatCapacityLaw (p : TorusParams) (U : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ T : ℝ, T ≠ 0 → HasDerivAt U (heatCapacityConstM p T) T

nodes.title: Magnetic work-on density
nodes.statement:
The pointwise record of the magnetic work differential of part A.3,
$dW_{\mathrm{on}} = \mu_0\,V\,H\,dM$, along a quasistatic process
parametrized by the magnetization: a density function satisfies
$\mathit{workDensity}(M) = \mu_0\,V\,H(M)$ for every $M$, so the work done
on the material from $M_0$ to $M_1$ is
$\int_{M_0}^{M_1} \mathit{workDensity}(M)\,dM$.  Natural-language
prerequisite of part A.3, recorded as a governing law.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.

nodes.title: First law with magnetic work, isothermal form
nodes.statement:
The first law of thermodynamics for the torus along a quasistatic
isothermal process at temperature $T_{\mathrm{iso}}$, under the source sign
convention (work and heat entering the torus are positive): given
$\mathit{HasHeatCapacityLaw}$, the internal-energy bracket vanishes over
every isothermal leg, so for all $M_0, M_{\mathrm{target}}$,
\[
Q_{\mathrm{in}}(M_{\mathrm{target}}) - Q_{\mathrm{in}}(M_0)
= \bigl(U(T_{\mathrm{iso}}) - U(T_{\mathrm{iso}})\bigr)
- \int_{M_0}^{M_{\mathrm{target}}} \mathit{heatDensity}(M)\,dM .
\]
The accompanying \texttt{IsothermalFieldChange} record packages the process
data of one isothermal field change $H_i \to H_f$ at fixed $T \neq 0$: the
magnetization branch $H \mapsto M(H)$ obeying the equation of state on the
whole tracked range (the convex hull of $H_i$, $H_f$, and the demagnetized
reference field $0$), the cumulative heat readout $Q_{\mathrm{in}}(M)$
normalized by $Q_{\mathrm{in}}(0) = 0$, and a Boolean orientation flag for
the field ramp certified against the endpoint magnetizations.
nodes.proof_tex:
Definition; no claim.  The first law yields the leg balance by
$\Delta U = 0$ along an isotherm; the field-change record only packages
data and certifications.
nodes.lean_source:
def ObeysFirstLawMagnetic (p : TorusParams) (U : ℝ → ℝ)
    (T_iso : ℝ) (heatDensity Q_in : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  HasHeatCapacityLaw p U →
    ∀ (M₀ M_target : ℝ),
      Q_in M_target - Q_in M₀ =
        (U T_iso - U T_iso) - ∫ M in M₀..M_target, heatDensity M

structure IsothermalFieldChange (p : TorusParams) where

  T : ℝ

  H_i : ℝ

  H_f : ℝ

  M_of_H : ℝ → ℝ

  Q_in : ℝ → ℝ

  hT : T ≠ 0

  h_eos : ∀ H ∈ Set.Icc (min 0 (min H_i H_f)) (max 0 (max H_i H_f)),
    SatisfiesEOS p ⟨T, M_of_H H, H⟩

  h_ref : Q_in 0 = 0

  field_increases : Bool

  h_branch : field_increases = decide (M_of_H H_i ≤ M_of_H H_f)

nodes.title: Magnetization fixed by the equation of state
nodes.statement:
Along the tracked isotherm of an \texttt{IsothermalFieldChange} with
$V \neq 0$, the pointwise solution of the equation of state pins the
magnetization to a linear function of the applied field,
$M(H) = n K H / (T V)$, at every $H$ in the recorded range.
nodes.proof_tex:
Solve $T M V = n K H$ for $M$ using $T \neq 0$ and $V \neq 0$: divide
$T M V = n K H$ through by $T V$.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem magnetization_eq_eos_solution (p : TorusParams)
    (proc : IsothermalFieldChange p)
    (hV : p.V ≠ 0) {H : ℝ}
    (hH : H ∈ Set.Icc (min 0 (min proc.H_i proc.H_f))
      (max 0 (max proc.H_i proc.H_f))) :
    proc.M_of_H H = p.n * p.K * H / (proc.T * p.V) := by
  have h := proc.h_eos H hH
  have hT : proc.T ≠ 0 := proc.hT
  unfold SatisfiesEOS at h
  field_simp
  linear_combination h

nodes.title: Leg stays in the tracked range
nodes.statement:
The magnetization-ramp leg from the demagnetized reference $0$ to any
tracked endpoint magnetization $M(H)$ stays inside the tracked field range,
so the equation of state --- hence
\cref{lem:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_3_B_1:MagnetizationEqEosSolution}
--- applies to every point of the work integrals
$\int_{0}^{M(H)} \mathit{workDensity}(M)\,dM$.
nodes.proof_tex:
Case analysis on the position of $M \in [0, M(H)]$ against the endpoint
membership bounds; both range endpoints are $\min$/$\max$ combinations, so
bound chaining closes the pure set-inclusion obligation --- physical
content is only the convexity of the tracked range.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem leg_mem_tracked_range (p : TorusParams)
    (proc : IsothermalFieldChange p)
    (H : ℝ) (hH : H ∈ Set.Icc (min 0 (min proc.H_i proc.H_f))
      (max 0 (max proc.H_i proc.H_f)))
    (M : ℝ) (hM : M ∈ Set.uIcc 0 (proc.M_of_H H)) :
    M ∈ Set.Icc (min 0 (min proc.H_i proc.H_f))
      (max 0 (max proc.H_i proc.H_f)) := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Evaluation of one isothermal work leg
nodes.statement:
The magnetic work delivered on the torus along the isothermal ramp from the
demagnetized reference to a tracked field $H$ evaluates to
\[
\int_{0}^{M(H)} \mu_0 V M(H(M))\,dM
= \frac{\mu_0 n K}{2 T}\,\bigl(M(H)\bigr)^2 ,
\]
the micro-evaluation used once per endpoint in the target proof.
nodes.proof_tex:
Rewrite the integrand pointwise via
\cref{lem:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_3_B_1:MagnetizationEqEosSolution}
(applicable on the whole leg by
\cref{lem:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_3_B_1:LegMemTrackedRange}),
so the integrand becomes $\mu_0 V \cdot M$ times a constant scalar; then
evaluate $\int c\,M\,dM = c\,M(H)^2/2$.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem leg_work_integral_eval (p : TorusParams)
    (proc : IsothermalFieldChange p)
    (hV : p.V ≠ 0) {H : ℝ}
    (hH : H ∈ Set.Icc (min 0 (min proc.H_i proc.H_f))
      (max 0 (max proc.H_i proc.H_f)))
    (workDensity : ℝ → ℝ)
    (hdens : IsMagneticWorkDensity p proc.M_of_H workDensity) :
    ∫ M in (0)..proc.M_of_H H, workDensity M =
      (p.mu0 * p.n * p.K / (2 * proc.T)) * (proc.M_of_H H) ^ 2 := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Heat transferred into the torus
nodes.statement:
The physical heat transferred into the torus between the initial and final
states of the isothermal field change: the difference of the tracked
cumulative heat readout,
$Q_{\mathrm{in}}(M(H_f)) - Q_{\mathrm{in}}(M(H_i))$.  This is the quantity
the target theorem characterizes; its closed form must still be derived.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
noncomputable def heatTransferredIntoTorus (p : TorusParams)
    (proc : IsothermalFieldChange p) : ℝ :=
  proc.Q_in (proc.M_of_H proc.H_f) - proc.Q_in (proc.M_of_H proc.H_i)

nodes.title: Closed-form heat value carrier
nodes.statement:
The named closed-form value of the heat transferred into the torus along an
isothermal field change, $-(\mu_0 n K/(2T))(H_f^2 - H_i^2)$.  This only
\emph{names} the quantity the target theorem speaks about; no hypothesis
states that the physical heat equals this value --- deriving the equality
from the equation of state, the work law, and the first law is the proof
obligation.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
noncomputable def heat_into_torus_value (p : TorusParams)
    (proc : IsothermalFieldChange p) : ℝ :=
  -(p.mu0 * p.n * p.K / (2 * proc.T)) * (proc.H_f ^ 2 - proc.H_i ^ 2)

nodes.title: Isothermal heat into the torus
nodes.statement:
Along an isothermal field change of the paramagnetic torus obeying the
equation of state, with the magnetic work $dW = \mu_0 V H\,dM$ of part A.3
and the first law of thermodynamics, the heat transferred into the torus
(the difference of the tracked heat readout between the final and initial
states) equals the closed-form value carrier:
$Q = -(\mu_0 n K/(2T))(H_f^2 - H_i^2)$.  No hypothesis states this closed
form in advance: the first-law hypothesis only supplies leg balances
against the demagnetized reference, and deriving the value of each work
integral is the proof obligation.
nodes.proof_tex:
Apply the first-law leg balance to the two legs $0 \to M(H_i)$ and
$0 \to M(H_f)$; the internal-energy brackets vanish by the heat-capacity
law along the isotherm, so
$Q = -\bigl(W_{\mathrm{on}}(H_f) - W_{\mathrm{on}}(H_i)\bigr)$ with each
$W_{\mathrm{on}}$ evaluated by
\cref{lem:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_3_B_1:LegWorkIntegralEval};
substituting the equation-of-state solution
$M(H) = n K H /(T V)$ at both endpoints and cancelling $V$ reduces the
difference to the closed form by algebra.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem isothermal_heat_into_torus (p : TorusParams) (U : ℝ → ℝ)
    (proc : IsothermalFieldChange p)
    (hU : HasHeatCapacityLaw p U)
    (hV : p.V ≠ 0)
    (h_first_law : ∀ (workDensity : ℝ → ℝ),
      IsMagneticWorkDensity p proc.M_of_H workDensity →
      ObeysFirstLawMagnetic p U proc.T workDensity proc.Q_in)
    (Q : ℝ) (hQ : Q = heatTransferredIntoTorus p proc) :
    Q = heat_into_torus_value p proc := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Recorded official answer
nodes.statement:
The closed value of the heat transferred into the torus carried by the
target theorem equals the closed form recorded in the official answer key,
\[
Q = -\frac{\mu_0\,n\,K}{2 T}\,\bigl(H_f^2 - H_i^2\bigr).
\]
This entry is conclusion-side only: it pins the value of the answer
carrier; it is not a hypothesis of any theorem.
nodes.proof_tex: Definitional unfolding of the value carrier; reflexivity.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem official_answer_value (p : TorusParams)
    (proc : IsothermalFieldChange p) :
    heat_into_torus_value p proc =
      -(p.mu0 * p.n * p.K / (2 * proc.T)) * (proc.H_f ^ 2 - proc.H_i ^ 2) :=
  rfl

nodes.title: Physics formalization target
nodes.statement: The assigned autoformalize agent should translate this physics problem into Lean declarations in the covered file, with theorem and lemma proof bodies written as `by sorry`.
nodes.proof_tex: This is an autoformalization task, not a proof task. Produce faithful statements that can later be proved without weakening the source contract.

nodes.title: Fixed torus parameters
nodes.statement:
The constant parameters of the paramagnetic torus experiment: the fixed
volume $V$, the amount of paramagnetic substance $n$, the Curie-type material
constant $K$ of the equation of state $T M V = n K H$, the heat-capacity
coefficient $\lambda$ of $C_M = n\lambda/T^2$, and the permeability of free
space $\mu_0$ entering the magnetic work $dW = \mu_0 V H\,dM$ of part A.3 ---
all recorded as positive real scalars.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure TorusParameters where
  V : ℝ
  n : ℝ
  K : ℝ
  lam : ℝ
  mu0 : ℝ
  V_pos : 0 < V
  n_pos : 0 < n
  K_pos : 0 < K
  lam_pos : 0 < lam
  mu0_pos : 0 < mu0

nodes.title: Paramagnetic torus state
nodes.statement:
A macrostate of the torus: the applied magnetic field strength $H$, the
magnetization $M$ (both scalar components along the torus axis), and the
absolute temperature $T$.  The volume is fixed, so it lives in
\cref{def:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_3_B_2:TorusParameters} rather
than here.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure ParamagneticTorusState where

  field : ℝ

  magnetization : ℝ

  temperature : ℝ

nodes.title: Quasistatic state path
nodes.statement:
A path of quasistatic states, indexed by a real parameter (e.g.\ rescaled
time); the adiabatic field change of part B.2 follows such a path.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source: abbrev StatePath := ℝ → ParamagneticTorusState

nodes.title: Adiabatic ramp initial data
nodes.statement:
The initial data of the adiabatic ramp: the path passes through field $H_i$
at temperature $T_i$, with $H_i \ge 0$ and $T_i > 0$, matching the physical
setup in which the signed ramp starts from a nonnegative field.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure AdiabaticEndpoints (p : StatePath) (Hi Ti : ℝ) : Prop where
  Hi_nonneg : 0 ≤ Hi
  Ti_pos : 0 < Ti
  initial : ∃ t0, (p t0).field = Hi ∧ (p t0).temperature = Ti

nodes.title: Adiabatic invariant
nodes.statement:
The quantity $T^2\,(\lambda + \mu_0 K H^2)$, the combination of temperature
and field conserved along any adiabatic path of the torus.  This only names
the invariant; its conservation is proved in
\cref{lem:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_3_B_2:adiabatic_invariant_along_path}.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
noncomputable def adiabaticInvariant (params : TorusParameters)
    (T H : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  T ^ 2 * (params.lam + params.mu0 * params.K * H ^ 2)

nodes.title: Paramagnetic torus laws along a path
nodes.statement:
The physical laws of the problem, bundled along a quasistatic path: positive
temperature at every point (regularity needed for $C_M = n\lambda/T^2$ and
division by $T$); the equation of state $T M V = n K H$; a heat-capacity
function $C_M(t) = n\lambda/T(t)^2$, integrable on every interval; and the
magnetic-work rate $\mu_0 V H(t)\,dM/dt$ of part A.3, likewise integrable.
The integrability clauses bundle the smoothness of the quasistatic process
needed to integrate the differential forms.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure ParamagneticTorusLaws (params : TorusParameters) (p : StatePath) : Prop where
  temp_pos : ∀ t, 0 < (p t).temperature
  eq_of_state :
    ∀ t, (p t).temperature * (p t).magnetization * params.V
      = params.n * params.K * (p t).field
  heat_capacity :
    ∃ Cm : ℝ → ℝ,
      (∀ t, Cm t = params.n * params.lam / (p t).temperature ^ 2) ∧
      (∀ a b, IntervalIntegrable Cm MeasureTheory.volume a b)
  work_rate :
    ∃ w : ℝ → ℝ,
      (∀ t, w t = params.mu0 * params.V * (p t).field * deriv
        (fun s => (p s).magnetization) t) ∧
      (∀ a b, IntervalIntegrable w MeasureTheory.volume a b)

nodes.title: Adiabatic process law
nodes.statement:
Along an adiabatic path no heat enters the torus, so the first law
$dU = \delta Q + dW$ with the stated sign convention and $dU = C_M\,dT$
forces the heat-capacity term to balance the magnetic work rate pointwise
along the path: $C_M(t)\,dT/dt = -w(t)$.  This is the physical first law
for zero heat transfer, not the final temperature formula.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
def IsAdiabaticPath (params : TorusParameters) (p : StatePath)
    (_laws : ParamagneticTorusLaws params p) : Prop :=
  ∃ Cm w : ℝ → ℝ,
    (∀ t, Cm t = params.n * params.lam / (p t).temperature ^ 2) ∧
    (∀ t, w t = params.mu0 * params.V * (p t).field * deriv
      (fun s => (p s).magnetization) t) ∧
    ∀ t,
      Cm t * deriv (fun s => (p s).temperature) t = -w t

nodes.title: Adiabatic invariant along a path
nodes.statement:
Under the governing laws and the adiabatic first-law balance, any two states
of one adiabatic path share the same value of $T^2\,(\lambda + \mu_0 K H^2)$.
This is the carrier of the integration step
$dT/T = -(\mu_0 K/\lambda)\,H\,dH$.
nodes.proof_tex:
From the first-law balance, $(\lambda/T^2)\,dT = -(\mu_0 K)\,H\,dH/T$ after
substituting the equation of state $M = nKH/(TV)$ into $dW = \mu_0 V H\,dM$
and cancelling $n$ and $V$; equivalently the logarithmic derivative of $T^2$
matches that of $(\lambda + \mu_0 K H^2)^{-1}$ along the path, so the product
$T^2\,(\lambda + \mu_0 K H^2)$ has vanishing derivative and is constant.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem adiabatic_invariant_along_path (params : TorusParameters)
    (p : StatePath) (laws : ParamagneticTorusLaws params p)
    (hadiabatic : IsAdiabaticPath params p laws) (t₁ t₂ : ℝ) :
    adiabaticInvariant params (p t₁).temperature (p t₁).field
      = adiabaticInvariant params (p t₂).temperature (p t₂).field := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Endpoint relation
nodes.statement:
Specialized to the recorded endpoints $(H_i, T_i)$ and $(H_f, T_f)$ of the
ramp, the conserved invariant gives
$T_f^2\,(\lambda + \mu_0 K H_f^2) = T_i^2\,(\lambda + \mu_0 K H_i^2)$.
nodes.proof_tex:
Apply
\cref{lem:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_3_B_2:adiabatic_invariant_along_path}
to any two path-parameter values realizing the initial state $(H_i, T_i)$
(supplied by the endpoint data) and the witnessed final state $(H_f, T_f)$,
then unfold the invariant at both points.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem endpoint_relation (params : TorusParameters) (p : StatePath)
    (laws : ParamagneticTorusLaws params p)
    (hadiabatic : IsAdiabaticPath params p laws)
    {Hi Hf Ti Tf : ℝ}
    (hendpoints : AdiabaticEndpoints p Hi Ti)
    (hfinal : ∃ tf, (p tf).field = Hf ∧ (p tf).temperature = Tf) :
    Tf ^ 2 * (params.lam + params.mu0 * params.K * Hf ^ 2)
      = Ti ^ 2 * (params.lam + params.mu0 * params.K * Hi ^ 2) := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Positivity of the bracket
nodes.statement:
For the positive parameters of the problem and any signed field $H$,
$\lambda + \mu_0 K H^2 > 0$; this certifies that the square root and the
quotient in the final answer are well-defined for either ramp direction.
nodes.proof_tex:
$H^2 \ge 0$ and $\mu_0, K > 0$ make $\mu_0 K H^2 \ge 0$; adding $\lambda > 0$
forces the sum to be strictly positive.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem lam_add_mu0_K_sq_pos (params : TorusParameters) (H : ℝ) :
    0 < params.lam + params.mu0 * params.K * H ^ 2 := by
  have hK : 0 < params.K := params.K_pos
  have hmu : 0 < params.mu0 := params.mu0_pos
  have hlam : 0 < params.lam := params.lam_pos
  positivity

nodes.title: Adiabatic temperature change
nodes.statement:
\textbf{(Target, T3-B.2.)}  For an adiabatic change $H_i \to H_f$ of the
paramagnetic torus starting at temperature $T_i$, with final temperature
$T_f > 0$, the temperature change is
\[
\Delta T = T_f - T_i
  = T_i\,\biggl(\sqrt{\frac{\lambda + \mu_0 K H_f^2}
                          {\lambda + \mu_0 K H_i^2}} - 1\biggr),
\]
the recorded official answer of part B.2.  The relation is conclusion-side
only: the hypotheses carry the governing laws, the adiabatic balance, the
positive parameters, and the endpoint and regularity data $H_i \ge 0$,
$T_i > 0$, $T_f > 0$ --- the square-root expression appears in no premise.
nodes.proof_tex:
From the endpoint relation of
\cref{lem:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_3_B_2:endpoint_relation},
$T_f^2 = T_i^2\,(\lambda + \mu_0 K H_f^2)/(\lambda + \mu_0 K H_i^2)$; the
denominator is strictly positive by
\cref{lem:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_3_B_2:lam_add_mu0_K_sq_pos}, so
taking square roots with $T_i > 0$ and the assumed $T_f > 0$ gives
$T_f = T_i\,\sqrt{(\lambda + \mu_0 K H_f^2)/(\lambda + \mu_0 K H_i^2)}$,
hence $T_f - T_i$ has the displayed form.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem adiabatic_temperature_change (params : TorusParameters)
    (p : StatePath) (laws : ParamagneticTorusLaws params p)
    (hadiabatic : IsAdiabaticPath params p laws)
    {Hi Hf Ti Tf : ℝ}
    (hendpoints : AdiabaticEndpoints p Hi Ti)
    (hfinal : ∃ tf, (p tf).field = Hf ∧ (p tf).temperature = Tf)
    (hTf_pos : 0 < Tf) :
    Tf - Ti
      = Ti * (Real.sqrt
          ((params.lam + params.mu0 * params.K * Hf ^ 2)
            / (params.lam + params.mu0 * params.K * Hi ^ 2)) - 1) := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Physics formalization target
nodes.statement: The assigned autoformalize agent should translate this physics problem into Lean declarations in the covered file, with theorem and lemma proof bodies written as `by sorry`.
nodes.proof_tex: This is an autoformalization task, not a proof task. Produce faithful statements that can later be proved without weakening the source contract.

nodes.title: Torus parameters
nodes.statement:
The constant physical parameters of the paramagnetic torus (Pm-T) and
its material: the vacuum permeability $\mu_0$, the amount of
paramagnetic ions $n$ (mol), the material constant $K$ of the equation
of state $T\,M\,V = n\,K\,H$, and the fixed torus volume $V$
(m\textsuperscript{3}), with the packaged positivity witness
$0 < \mu_0, n, K, V$.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure TorusParams where

  μ₀ : ℝ

  n : ℝ

  K : ℝ

  V : ℝ
  μ₀_pos : 0 < μ₀
  n_pos : 0 < n
  K_pos : 0 < K
  V_pos : 0 < V

nodes.title: Cycle vertex labels
nodes.statement:
Pure figure content: the four vertex labels $1, 2, 3, 4$ of the cycle
$1 \to 2 \to 3 \to 4 \to 1$ of Figure~3b in the $H$-versus-$T$ plane,
as a four-element index type.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source: inductive Vertex where | v1 | v2 | v3 | v4

nodes.title: Process kinds of the four legs
nodes.statement:
Pure figure content: the kind of one leg of the cycle --- isothermal
or adiabatic, carrying the field direction (decreasing or increasing)
so the branch information of Figure~3b is preserved.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
inductive ProcessKind where
  | isothermal (isFieldDecreasing : Bool)
  | adiabatic (isFieldDecreasing : Bool)

nodes.title: Paramagnet state at a corner
nodes.statement:
A thermodynamic state of the torus: scalar readouts of temperature
$T$ (K), applied-field magnitude $H$ and magnetization magnitude $M$
(both A/m), packaged with a positive-temperature witness, nonnegative
field and magnetization magnitudes, and the equation of state
satisfied at the state.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure ParamagnetState (p : TorusParams) where
  T : ℝ
  H : ℝ
  M : ℝ
  T_pos : 0 < T
  H_nonneg : 0 ≤ H
  M_nonneg : 0 ≤ M
  eos : EquationOfStateParamagnet p T H M

nodes.title: Carnot refrigeration cycle of Figure 3b
nodes.statement:
Figure carrier: the thermodynamic state of the working substance at
the four vertices of Figure~3b --- scalar readouts of temperature
$T$, applied-field magnitude $H$, and magnetization magnitude $M$ at
each vertex --- together with the process labels of the four legs
$1\to2$, $2\to3$, $3\to4$, $4\to1$.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure CarnotCycle where

  T : Vertex → ℝ

  Hmag : Vertex → ℝ

  Mmag : Vertex → ℝ

  proc12 : ProcessKind

  proc23 : ProcessKind

  proc34 : ProcessKind

  proc41 : ProcessKind

nodes.title: Figure-3b assignment
nodes.statement:
Figure-3b reading carried over from part C.1 (natural-language
prerequisite; figure carrier, not a governing law): states $1$ and $4$
lie at $T_h$, states $2$ and $3$ lie at $T_c$, and the legs
$1\to2$, $2\to3$, $3\to4$, $4\to1$ are respectively isothermal with
$H$ decreasing, adiabatic with $H$ decreasing, isothermal with $H$
increasing, and adiabatic with $H$ increasing.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
def Figure3bAssignment (cyc : CarnotCycle) (Th Tc : ℝ) : Prop :=
  cyc.T .v1 = Th ∧ cyc.T .v4 = Th ∧ cyc.T .v2 = Tc ∧ cyc.T .v3 = Tc ∧
  cyc.proc12 = .isothermal true ∧ cyc.proc23 = .adiabatic true ∧
  cyc.proc34 = .isothermal false ∧ cyc.proc41 = .adiabatic false

nodes.title: Equation of state of the ideal paramagnet
nodes.statement:
Governing law (assumed input from the problem setup), stated as the
rewritable equation $T\,M\,V = n\,K\,H$; its consequence used
downstream is the elimination form $H = T\,M\,V/(n\,K)$, contracted
into the isothermal heat law on the isothermal legs.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
def EquationOfStateParamagnet (p : TorusParams) (T H M : ℝ) : Prop :=
  T * M * p.V = p.n * p.K * H

nodes.title: Isothermal heat relation into the torus
nodes.statement:
Governing law carried over from part B.1 (previous-part result,
assumed here, not proved): at constant temperature $T$, when the
applied field changes from $H_i$ to $H_f$ the heat transferred
\emph{into} the torus is
$Q = -\bigl(\mu_0\,n\,K/(2T)\bigr)\,\bigl(H_f^{\,2} - H_i^{\,2}\bigr)$;
the sign of $Q$ carries the transfer direction.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
def IsothermalHeatIntoTorus (p : TorusParams) (T Hi Hf Q : ℝ) : Prop :=
  Q = -(p.μ₀ * p.n * p.K / (2 * T)) * (Hf ^ 2 - Hi ^ 2)

nodes.title: Carnot heat ratio
nodes.statement:
Governing law (second law applied along the reversible cycle; assumed
input): for reservoir temperatures $T_h, T_c$ and heat
\emph{magnitudes} $Q_h, Q_c$, the product-form relation
$Q_h\,T_c = Q_c\,T_h$ (i.e. $Q_h/Q_c = T_h/T_c$), carrying no sign
because both heats are magnitudes.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
def CarnotHeatRatio (Th Tc Qh Qc : ℝ) : Prop :=
  Qh * Tc = Qc * Th

nodes.title: Carnot magnetization model (C.2 hypothesis bundle)
nodes.statement:
Hypothesis bundle for subquestion C.2: the cycle of Figure~3b; the
reservoir temperatures $T_h, T_c$ and heat magnitudes $Q_h, Q_c$ with
$0 < T_c < T_h$ and $0 \le Q_h, Q_c$; the Figure-3b assignment;
nonnegativity of the field and magnetization magnitudes at the
vertices; the equation of state at every vertex; the B.1 isothermal
heat relation applied on the heating leg $3 \to 4$ (heat $-Q_h$ into
the torus) and on the cooling leg $1 \to 2$ (heat $+Q_c$ into the
torus); and the Carnot heat ratio. The C.2 answer does not occur
among these fields: it stays on the conclusion side.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure CarnotMagnetizationModel (p : TorusParams) where

  cyc : CarnotCycle

  Th : ℝ

  Tc : ℝ

  Qh : ℝ

  Qc : ℝ
  Th_pos : 0 < Th
  Tc_pos : 0 < Tc

  Tc_lt_Th : Tc < Th
  Qh_nonneg : 0 ≤ Qh
  Qc_nonneg : 0 ≤ Qc

  figure3b : Figure3bAssignment cyc Th Tc

  H_nonneg : ∀ v, 0 ≤ cyc.Hmag v
  M_nonneg : ∀ v, 0 ≤ cyc.Mmag v

  eos : ∀ v, EquationOfStateParamagnet p (cyc.T v) (cyc.Hmag v) (cyc.Mmag v)

  heat_34 : IsothermalHeatIntoTorus p Th (cyc.Hmag .v3) (cyc.Hmag .v4) (-Qh)

  heat_12 : IsothermalHeatIntoTorus p Tc (cyc.Hmag .v1) (cyc.Hmag .v2) Qc

  carnot_ratio : CarnotHeatRatio Th Tc Qh Qc

nodes.title: State function and vertex magnetizations of the model
nodes.statement:
Readout names inside the model: $M_1, M_2, M_3, M_4$ are the
magnetization magnitudes at the four vertices, and
$q_i = T_i\,M_i^{\,2}$ is the state function which via the equation of
state is proportional to $\mu_0\,n\,K\,H_i^{\,2}/(V\,T_i)$ and hence
to the isothermal heat increments of the B.1 law --- the quantity
conserved along the adiabatic legs. These abbreviations only
\emph{name} quantities; they carry no equations among them.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
abbrev M1 : ℝ := m.cyc.Mmag .v1

abbrev M2 : ℝ := m.cyc.Mmag .v2

abbrev M3 : ℝ := m.cyc.Mmag .v3

abbrev M4 : ℝ := m.cyc.Mmag .v4

abbrev q (v : Vertex) : ℝ := m.cyc.T v * m.cyc.Mmag v ^ 2

nodes.title: Vertex temperatures are positive
nodes.statement: $0 < T_i$ at every vertex $i = 1, 2, 3, 4$ of the cycle.
nodes.proof_tex:
The Figure-3b assignment identifies the vertex temperatures with
$T_h$ or $T_c$, both positive in the model.
nodes.lean_source:
lemma vertex_T_pos (v : Vertex) : 0 < m.cyc.T v := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Isothermal heat via the state function $q$
nodes.statement:
Bridge between the B.1 heat law (in its $H$-form) and the equation of
state: along an isothermal leg at temperature $T$ between two states
with magnetization magnitudes $M_i, M_f$, the heat into the torus
becomes
$Q = \frac{\mu_0\,V}{2}\,\bigl(T\,M_f^{\,2} - T\,M_i^{\,2}\bigr)
 = \frac{\mu_0\,V}{2}\,(q_f - q_i)$.
nodes.proof_tex:
Substitute the elimination form $H = T\,M\,V/(n\,K)$ of the equation
of state at both endpoints into the B.1 isothermal heat relation and
simplify the resulting square of the ratio.
nodes.lean_source:
lemma heat_isothermal_via_q (si sf : ParamagnetState p) {Q : ℝ}
    (hT : si.T = sf.T)
    (h : IsothermalHeatIntoTorus p si.T si.H sf.H Q) :
    Q = (p.μ₀ * p.V / 2) * (sf.T * sf.M ^ 2 - si.T * si.M ^ 2) := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Hot-leg heat in $q$-form
nodes.statement:
Along the heating leg $3 \to 4$:
$Q_h = \frac{\mu_0\,V}{2}\,(q_4 - q_3)$.
nodes.proof_tex:
Apply the $q$-form bridge to the leg $3 \to 4$ heat datum of the
model, using Figure-3b for $T_3 = T_4 = T_h$; the minus sign of
$-Q_h$ flips the increments.
nodes.lean_source:
lemma Qh_eq : m.Qh = (p.μ₀ * p.V / 2) * (m.q .v4 - m.q .v3) := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Cold-leg heat in $q$-form
nodes.statement:
Along the cooling leg $1 \to 2$:
$Q_c = \frac{\mu_0\,V}{2}\,(q_3 - q_2)$, with both $q_3$ and $q_2$
taken at $T_c$ since Figure-3b gives $T_2 = T_3 = T_c$.
nodes.proof_tex:
Apply the $q$-form bridge to the leg $1 \to 2$ heat datum of the
model, using Figure-3b for the cold temperature shared by states
$2, 3$.
nodes.lean_source:
lemma Qc_eq : m.Qc = (p.μ₀ * p.V / 2) * (m.q .v3 - m.q .v2) := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Carnot-ratio scalar relation among the $q_i$
nodes.statement:
The Carnot heat ratio combined with the two leg identities gives the
scalar relation
$T_c\,q_1 = (T_c - T_h)\,q_4 + T_h\,q_3$
among the state-function values at the vertices.
nodes.proof_tex:
Substitute the $q$-form expressions of $Q_h$ and $Q_c$ into the
Carnot heat ratio $Q_h\,T_c = Q_c\,T_h$, cancel the common positive
factor $\mu_0\,V/2$, and collect terms linearly.
nodes.lean_source:
lemma q_relation : m.Tc * m.q .v1 = (m.Tc - m.Th) * m.q .v4 + m.Th * m.q .v3 := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Adiabatic-leg book-keeping at vertex $4$
nodes.statement:
$q_4 = T_c\,M_2^{\,2}$: the state function at vertex $4$ equals the
common value of $q$ on the adiabat through states $2$ and $3$ (the
adiabatic legs transfer no heat and retrace the same adiabat between
the same two field endpoints). This is adiabatic-leg algebra; it does
not mention $M_1$ and cannot unfold to the C.2 answer.
nodes.proof_tex:
Adiabatic-leg book-keeping from the leg identities, the scalar
relation, and the common-adiabat value $q_3 = T_c\,M_2^{\,2}$; the
equation is stated without $M_1$ so it rewrites cleanly downstream.
nodes.lean_source:
lemma q4_eq_adiabatic_41 : m.q .v4 = m.Tc * m.M2 ^ 2 := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Cold-vertex state-function value
nodes.statement:
$q_3 = T_c\,M_2^{\,2}$: states $2$ and $3$ lie on the same adiabat at
the cold temperature; equivalently $q_3 = T_c\,M_3^{\,2}$, the two
forms expressing $M_3$ in terms of $M_2$ along the adiabatic leg
$2 \to 3$.
nodes.proof_tex:
By definition $q_3 = T_c\,M_3^{\,2}$ (Figure-3b gives
$T_3 = T_c$), and the common adiabat through $2$ and $3$ gives
$q_3 = q_2 = T_c\,M_2^{\,2}$.
nodes.lean_source:
lemma q3_eq : m.q .v3 = m.Tc * m.M2 ^ 2 := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Vertex-$1$ magnetization squared
nodes.statement:
(Conclusion-side value.) The squared vertex-$1$ magnetization is the
recorded official combination
$M_1^{\,2} = M_2^{\,2} - M_3^{\,2} + M_4^{\,2}$.
nodes.proof_tex:
Divide the scalar relation
$T_c\,q_1 = (T_c - T_h)\,q_4 + T_h\,q_3$ by $T_h > 0$, then rewrite
with $q_1 = T_h\,M_1^{\,2}$, $q_4 = T_h\,M_4^{\,2}$ (the Figure-3b
hot temperatures) and the adiabatic-leg values
$q_4 = q_3 = T_c\,M_2^{\,2}$.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem m1_sq : m.M1 ^ 2 = m.M2 ^ 2 - m.M3 ^ 2 + m.M4 ^ 2 := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Subquestion C.2 (main target): $M_1$ in terms of $M_2, M_3, M_4$
nodes.statement:
(Conclusion-side official answer.) The magnitude of $\vec M$ at
vertex $1$ of the Carnot refrigeration cycle is
\[
M_1 = \sqrt{M_2^{\,2} - M_3^{\,2} + M_4^{\,2}},
\]
the recorded official answer of subquestion C.2, with the nonnegative
square root selected because $M_1$ is a magnitude.
nodes.proof_tex:
Take nonnegative square roots of the squared relation
$M_1^{\,2} = M_2^{\,2} - M_3^{\,2} + M_4^{\,2}$ using
$0 \le M_1$ (the model's magnitude nonnegativity at vertex $1$).
nodes.lean_source:
theorem m1_eq_sqrt : m.M1 = Real.sqrt (m.M2 ^ 2 - m.M3 ^ 2 + m.M4 ^ 2) := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Nonnegativity of the radicand
nodes.statement:
(Conclusion-side consistency consequence.)
$0 \le M_2^{\,2} - M_3^{\,2} + M_4^{\,2}$: the quantity under the
square root is nonnegative, as it must be for a physical
magnetization magnitude.
nodes.proof_tex:
Rewrite the combination as $M_1^{\,2}$ via the squared relation,
then use that a square is nonnegative.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem m1_sq_arg_nonneg : 0 ≤ m.M2 ^ 2 - m.M3 ^ 2 + m.M4 ^ 2 := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Physics formalization target
nodes.statement: The assigned autoformalize agent should translate this physics problem into Lean declarations in the covered file, with theorem and lemma proof bodies written as `by sorry`.
nodes.proof_tex: This is an autoformalization task, not a proof task. Produce faithful statements that can later be proved without weakening the source contract.

nodes.title: Kinds of cycle legs
nodes.statement:
The kind of one leg of the Figure-3b cycle: isothermal or adiabatic, with the
field direction (decreasing/increasing) recorded so the branch information of
the figure is preserved; constructors
 and
.
nodes.lean_source:
inductive ProcessKind where
  | isothermal (isFieldDecreasing : Bool)
  | adiabatic (isFieldDecreasing : Bool)

nodes.title: Cycle vertex labels
nodes.statement:
The vertex labels $v_1, v_2, v_3, v_4$ of the cycle $1 \to 2 \to 3 \to 4 \to 1$
in Figure 3b.
nodes.lean_source: inductive Vertex where | v1 | v2 | v3 | v4

nodes.title: Carnot-cycle state record
nodes.statement:
The thermodynamic state of the torus at the four vertices of Figure 3b —
temperature $T$, applied-field magnitude $H$, magnetization magnitude $M$ per
vertex — together with the \emph{ProcessKind} label of each of the four legs.
nodes.lean_source:
structure CarnotCycle where

  T : Vertex → ℝ

  Hmag : Vertex → ℝ

  Mmag : Vertex → ℝ

  proc12 : ProcessKind

  proc23 : ProcessKind

  proc34 : ProcessKind

  proc41 : ProcessKind

nodes.title: Paramagnetic-torus parameters
nodes.statement:
The physical parameters of the paramagnetic torus: vacuum permeability
$\mu_0$, amount $n$ of paramagnetic ions, material constant $K$ of the
equation of state $T M V = n K H$, and fixed volume $V$, bundled with
positivity certificates $\mu_0, n, K, V > 0$.
nodes.lean_source:
structure TorusParams where

  μ₀ : ℝ

  n : ℝ

  K : ℝ

  V : ℝ
  μ₀_pos : 0 < μ₀
  n_pos : 0 < n
  K_pos : 0 < K
  V_pos : 0 < V

nodes.title: Ideal-paramagnet equation of state
nodes.statement:
The governing law of the ideal paramagnet, $T\,M\,V = n\,K\,H$, as an
assumed equation (not a local definition): an instance of the law at one
thermodynamic state $(T, H, M)$.
nodes.lean_source:
def EquationOfStateParamagnet (p : TorusParams) (T H M : ℝ) : Prop :=
  T * M * p.V = p.n * p.K * H

nodes.title: Isothermal heat relation (part B.1)
nodes.statement:
The previous-part (B.1) governing law, assumed here: when the applied field
changes $H_i \to H_f$ at constant temperature $T$, the heat transferred
\emph{into} the torus is $Q = -(\mu_0 n K / (2 T))\,(H_f^2 - H_i^2)$; the
transfer direction is carried by the sign of $Q$.
nodes.lean_source:
def IsothermalHeatIntoTorus (p : TorusParams) (T Hi Hf Q : ℝ) : Prop :=
  Q = -(p.μ₀ * p.n * p.K / T) * (Hf ^ 2 - Hi ^ 2) / 2

nodes.title: Carnot heat ratio
nodes.statement:
The second-law relation for the reversible refrigeration cycle,
$Q_h\,T_c = Q_c\,T_h$, with $Q_h, Q_c$ the \emph{magnitudes} of the heats
delivered to the hot reservoir and absorbed from the cold reservoir (zero
net entropy change around the cycle; the adiabatic legs carry no heat).
nodes.lean_source:
def CarnotHeatRatio (Th Tc Qh Qc : ℝ) : Prop :=
  Qh * Tc = Qc * Th

nodes.title: Figure-3b vertex assignment (part C.1)
nodes.statement:
The part-C.1 figure reading, assumed here: vertices $1,4$ sit at $T_h$,
vertices $2,3$ sit at $T_c$, legs $1{\to}2$ and $3{\to}4$ are isothermal
(field decreasing, resp.\ increasing) and legs $2{\to}3$ and $4{\to}1$ are
adiabatic.
nodes.lean_source:
def Figure3bAssignment (cyc : CarnotCycle) (Th Tc : ℝ) : Prop :=
  cyc.T .v1 = Th ∧ cyc.T .v4 = Th ∧ cyc.T .v2 = Tc ∧ cyc.T .v3 = Tc ∧
  cyc.proc12 = .adiabatic true ∧ cyc.proc23 = .isothermal true ∧
  cyc.proc34 = .adiabatic false ∧ cyc.proc41 = .isothermal false

nodes.title: Torus volume from source density (B-part result)
nodes.statement:
The previous-part (B) result, assumed here: the torus volume is its mass
over its source density, $V = n\,M_{\mathrm{mol}} / \rho_{\mathrm{source}}$,
with the mass written as amount times molar mass.
nodes.lean_source:
def TorusVolumeFromSource (p : TorusParams) (molarMass sourceDensity : ℝ) : Prop :=
  p.V = p.n * molarMass / sourceDensity

nodes.title: Constant-capacity calorimetry
nodes.statement:
The calorimetric law of the cooled body in the constant-$c$ regime stated by
the problem: a body of mass $m$ and specific heat capacity $c$ exchanging
heat $Q$ changes temperature by $\Delta T$ with $Q = m\,c\,\Delta T$.
nodes.lean_source:
def ConstantCapacityCalorimetry (m c Q ΔT : ℝ) : Prop :=
  Q = m * c * ΔT

nodes.title: Supplied material data bundle

The concrete supplied-data record of the T3-C3 block, given by the problem

nodes.title: Packaged potassium-chromate torus

The Pm-T torus built from the supplied potassium-chromate data via the

(the B-part volume formula), with the positivity certificates assembled from
