nodes.title: Potassium-chromate cooling run
nodes.statement:
The full model of subquestion C.3: one operating cycle of the Pm-T Carnot
refrigerator absorbing heat from a constant-capacity liquid-helium bath.
Fields record the torus (matching the supplied amount, material constant, and
B-part volume), the Figure-3b cycle with the supplied vertex fields
$H_1 = 411624$, $H_2 = 311306$, $H_3 = 204618$, $H_4 = 240446$ A/m, reservoir
temperatures $0 < T_c < T_h$, heat magnitudes $Q_h, Q_c > 0$, the helium mass
$m_{\mathrm{He}} = \rho_{\mathrm{He}} V_{\mathrm{He}}$, initial temperature
$T_{\mathrm{initial}} = T_c = 1.00$ K, the equation of state at each vertex,
the B.1 heat law on both isothermal legs (heat $+Q_c$ into the torus on the
field-decreasing cold leg, $-Q_h$ on the field-increasing hot leg), the
Carnot ratio, and the helium calorimetry in the explicit cooling branch
$Q_c = m\,c\,(T_{\mathrm{initial}} - T_{\mathrm{final}})$. The C.3 target
values occur nowhere among the fields.
nodes.lean_source:
structure PotassiumChromateCoolingRun where

  p : TorusParams

  p_mu0 : p.μ₀ = vacuumPermeability

  p_amount : p.n = pmtAmount
  p_K : p.K = pmtMaterialK

  p_volume : TorusVolumeFromSource p pmtMolarMass pmtSourceDensity

  cyc : CarnotCycle

  Th : ℝ

  Tc : ℝ

  Qh : ℝ

  Qc : ℝ

  heliumMass : ℝ

  TInitial : ℝ

  TFinal : ℝ
  Th_pos : 0 < Th
  Tc_pos : 0 < Tc

  Tc_lt_Th : Tc < Th

  Qh_pos : 0 < Qh

  Qc_pos : 0 < Qc
  heliumMass_pos : 0 < heliumMass
  TInitial_pos : 0 < TInitial
  TFinal_pos : 0 < TFinal

  initial_is_Tc : TInitial = Tc ∧ TInitial = 1.00

  bath_mass : heliumMass = heliumDensity * heliumBathVolume

  vertex_fields :
    cyc.Hmag .v1 = 411624 ∧ cyc.Hmag .v2 = 311306 ∧
    cyc.Hmag .v3 = 204618 ∧ cyc.Hmag .v4 = 240446

  figure3b : Figure3bAssignment cyc Th Tc

  H_nonneg : ∀ v, 0 ≤ cyc.Hmag v
  M_nonneg : ∀ v, 0 ≤ cyc.Mmag v

  eos : ∀ v, EquationOfStateParamagnet p (cyc.T v) (cyc.Hmag v) (cyc.Mmag v)

  heat_23 : IsothermalHeatIntoTorus p Tc (cyc.Hmag .v2) (cyc.Hmag .v3) Qc

  heat_41 : IsothermalHeatIntoTorus p Th (cyc.Hmag .v4) (cyc.Hmag .v1) (-Qh)

  carnot_ratio : CarnotHeatRatio Th Tc Qh Qc

  helium_calorimetry :
    ConstantCapacityCalorimetry heliumMass heliumSpecificHeat Qc
      (TInitial - TFinal)

nodes.title: Vertex-field abbreviations
nodes.statement:
The vertex applied-field magnitudes of a run $r$, abbreviated
,
,
,

for the values of $\texttt{cyc.Hmag}$ at vertices $v_1, v_2, v_3, v_4$.
nodes.lean_source:
abbrev H1 : ℝ := r.cyc.Hmag .v1

abbrev H1 : ℝ := r.cyc.Hmag .v1

abbrev H2 : ℝ := r.cyc.Hmag .v2

abbrev H3 : ℝ := r.cyc.Hmag .v3

abbrev H4 : ℝ := r.cyc.Hmag .v4

nodes.title: Torus-volume value
nodes.statement:
The torus volume is forced by the supplied data:
$V = n\,M_{\mathrm{mol}} / \rho_{\mathrm{source}}$ with the supplied amount.
nodes.proof_tex:
Unfold the \texttt{p\_volume} field (an instance of the B-part volume law)
and rewrite the amount through the \texttt{p\_amount} field.
nodes.lean_source:
lemma torus_volume_value :
    r.p.V = pmtAmount * pmtMolarMass / pmtSourceDensity := by
  have h : r.p.V = r.p.n * pmtMolarMass / pmtSourceDensity := r.p_volume
  rw [r.p_amount] at h
  exact h

nodes.title: Cold-leg heat balance
nodes.statement:
The heat absorbed from the helium on the cold isothermal leg $1 \to 2$ is
$Q_c = (\mu_0 n K / (2 T_c))\,(H_1^2 - H_2^2)$.
nodes.proof_tex:
Unfold the \texttt{heat\_12} field (the signed B.1 law with heat into the
torus equal to $+Q_c$): the two negations cancel, giving the displayed
magnitude form; positivity follows from $H_2 < H_1$ on the field-decreasing
leg recorded by the figure assignment and vertex fields.
nodes.lean_source:
lemma Qc_cold_leg :
    r.Qc = (r.p.μ₀ * r.p.n * r.p.K / r.Tc) * (r.H2 ^ 2 - r.H3 ^ 2) / 2 := by
  have h : r.Qc = -(r.p.μ₀ * r.p.n * r.p.K / r.Tc) *
      (r.cyc.Hmag .v3 ^ 2 - r.cyc.Hmag .v2 ^ 2) / 2 := r.heat_23
  calc r.Qc = -(r.p.μ₀ * r.p.n * r.p.K / r.Tc) *
        (r.cyc.Hmag .v3 ^ 2 - r.cyc.Hmag .v2 ^ 2) / 2 := h
    _ = (r.p.μ₀ * r.p.n * r.p.K / r.Tc) * (r.H2 ^ 2 - r.H3 ^ 2) / 2 := by ring

nodes.title: Hot-leg heat balance
nodes.statement:
The heat delivered to the hot reservoir on the isothermal leg $3 \to 4$ is
$Q_h = (\mu_0 n K / (2 T_h))\,(H_4^2 - H_3^2)$.
nodes.proof_tex:
Unfold the \texttt{heat\_34} field (the signed B.1 law with heat into the
torus equal to $-Q_h$) and cancel the negations; positivity follows from
$H_4 > H_3$.
nodes.lean_source:
lemma Qh_hot_leg :
    r.Qh = (r.p.μ₀ * r.p.n * r.p.K / r.Th) * (r.H1 ^ 2 - r.H4 ^ 2) / 2 := by
  have h : -r.Qh = -(r.p.μ₀ * r.p.n * r.p.K / r.Th) *
      (r.cyc.Hmag .v1 ^ 2 - r.cyc.Hmag .v4 ^ 2) / 2 := r.heat_41
  calc r.Qh = (r.p.μ₀ * r.p.n * r.p.K / r.Th) *
        (r.cyc.Hmag .v1 ^ 2 - r.cyc.Hmag .v4 ^ 2) / 2 := by linarith [h]
    _ = (r.p.μ₀ * r.p.n * r.p.K / r.Th) * (r.H1 ^ 2 - r.H4 ^ 2) / 2 := by ring

nodes.title: Reservoir-temperature consistency
nodes.statement:
The supplied vertex data are consistent with the reversible cycle:
$(H_1^2 - H_2^2)\,T_h^2 = (H_4^2 - H_3^2)\,T_c^2$, the exact relation that
fixes $T_h$ from $T_c$ and the vertex fields.
nodes.proof_tex:
Substitute the cold- and hot-leg identities into the Carnot ratio
$Q_h T_c = Q_c T_h$, cancel the common factor $\mu_0 n K / 2$ and the nonzero
factors $T_h$, $T_c$, $Q_c$ (consequences of the assumed positivity fields —
no numeric value is used), and cross-multiply.
nodes.lean_source:
lemma reservoir_temperature_consistency :
    r.Tc / r.Th = (r.H2 ^ 2 - r.H3 ^ 2) * r.cyc.T .v1 /
      ((r.H1 ^ 2 - r.H4 ^ 2) * r.Tc) := by
  have hTc : r.Tc ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt r.Tc_pos
  have hTh : r.Th ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt r.Th_pos
  have hp : r.p.μ₀ * r.p.n * r.p.K ≠ 0 :=
    mul_ne_zero (mul_ne_zero (ne_of_gt r.p.μ₀_pos) (ne_of_gt r.p.n_pos))
      (ne_of_gt r.p.K_pos)
  have hq : r.Qc = (r.p.μ₀ * r.p.n * r.p.K / r.Tc) * (r.H2 ^ 2 - r.H3 ^ 2) / 2 :=
    r.Qc_cold_leg
  have hheath : r.Qh = (r.p.μ₀ * r.p.n * r.p.K / r.Th) * (r.H1 ^ 2 - r.H4 ^ 2) / 2 :=
    r.Qh_hot_leg
  have hT1 : r.cyc.T .v1 = r.Th := r.figure3b.1
  have hQc : r.Qc ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt r.Qc_pos
  have hd23 : (r.cyc.Hmag .v2 ^ 2 - r.cyc.Hmag .v3 ^ 2) ≠ 0 := by
    intro hz
    apply hQc
    rw [hq]
    show (r.p.μ₀ * r.p.n * r.p.K / r.Tc) *
        (r.cyc.Hmag .v2 ^ 2 - r.cyc.Hmag .v3 ^ 2) / 2 = 0
    rw [hz]
    ring
  have hcr' : (r.p.μ₀ * r.p.n * r.p.K / r.Th *
        (r.cyc.Hmag .v1 ^ 2 - r.cyc.Hmag .v4 ^ 2) / 2) * r.Tc =
      (r.p.μ₀ * r.p.n * r.p.K / r.Tc *
        (r.cyc.Hmag .v2 ^ 2 - r.cyc.Hmag .v3 ^ 2) / 2) * r.Th := by
    rw [← hheath, ← hq]
    exact r.carnot_ratio
  have hcore : (r.cyc.Hmag .v1 ^ 2 - r.cyc.Hmag .v4 ^ 2) * r.Tc ^ 2 =
      (r.cyc.Hmag .v2 ^ 2 - r.cyc.Hmag .v3 ^ 2) * r.Th ^ 2 := by
    have h := hcr'
    field_simp [hTh, hTc] at h
    have key : r.p.μ₀ * r.p.n * r.p.K *
        ((r.cyc.Hmag .v1 ^ 2 - r.cyc.Hmag .v4 ^ 2) * r.Tc ^ 2 -
          (r.cyc.Hmag .v2 ^ 2 - r.cyc.Hmag .v3 ^ 2) * r.Th ^ 2) = 0 := by
      nlinarith [h]
    rcases mul_eq_zero.mp key with h1 | h2
    · rcases mul_eq_zero.mp h1 with h3 | h4
      · rcases mul_eq_zero.mp h3 with h5 | h6
        · exact absurd h5 (ne_of_gt r.p.μ₀_pos)
        · exact absurd h6 (ne_of_gt r.p.n_pos)
      · exact absurd h4 (ne_of_gt r.p.K_pos)
    · nlinarith [h2]
  have hdA : (r.cyc.Hmag .v1 ^ 2 - r.cyc.Hmag .v4 ^ 2) ≠ 0 := by
    intro hz
    rw [hz] at hcore
    simp at hcore
    rcases hcore with h1 | h2
    · exact hd23 h1
    · exact hTh h2
  rw [hT1]
  have hgoal : r.Tc * ((r.cyc.Hmag .v1 ^ 2 - r.cyc.Hmag .v4 ^ 2) * r.Tc) =
      (r.cyc.Hmag .v2 ^ 2 - r.cyc.Hmag .v3 ^ 2) * r.Th * r.Th := by
    nlinarith [hcore]
  exact (div_eq_div_iff hTh (mul_ne_zero hdA hTc)).mpr hgoal

nodes.title: Final temperature from calorimetry
nodes.statement:
The helium temperature after one cycle is
$T_{\mathrm{final}} = T_{\mathrm{initial}} - Q_c / (m_{\mathrm{He}}\,c)$.
nodes.proof_tex:
Unfold the \texttt{helium\_calorimetry} field
($Q_c = m\,c\,(T_{\mathrm{initial}} - T_{\mathrm{final}})$) and solve for
$T_{\mathrm{final}}$ using $m_{\mathrm{He}}, c \neq 0$ (the
\texttt{heliumMass\_pos} and supplied specific-heat positivity fields).
nodes.lean_source:
lemma TFinal_from_calorimetry :
    r.TFinal = r.TInitial - r.Qc / (r.heliumMass * heliumSpecificHeat) := by
  have hcal : r.Qc = r.heliumMass * heliumSpecificHeat * (r.TInitial - r.TFinal) :=
    r.helium_calorimetry
  have hmc : r.heliumMass * heliumSpecificHeat ≠ 0 :=
    mul_ne_zero (ne_of_gt r.heliumMass_pos) (ne_of_gt heliumSpecificHeat_pos)
  have hdiv : r.Qc / (r.heliumMass * heliumSpecificHeat) = r.TInitial - r.TFinal := by
    rw [hcal, mul_div_cancel_left₀ _ hmc]
  linarith [hdiv]

nodes.title: Cooling branch certificate
nodes.statement: The helium cools: $T_{\mathrm{final}} < T_{\mathrm{initial}}$.
nodes.proof_tex:
From the calorimetry form the drop is $Q_c / (m_{\mathrm{He}} c)$ with
$Q_c > 0$ (the \texttt{Qc\_pos} field) and $m_{\mathrm{He}}, c > 0$, so the
quotient is strictly positive.
nodes.lean_source:
lemma helium_cools : r.TFinal < r.TInitial := by
  have hdrop : 0 < r.Qc / (r.heliumMass * heliumSpecificHeat) :=
    div_pos r.Qc_pos (mul_pos r.heliumMass_pos heliumSpecificHeat_pos)
  have h := r.TFinal_from_calorimetry
  linarith [h, hdrop]

nodes.title: C.3 target (i): absorbed heat
nodes.statement:
One operating cycle absorbs $Q_c \approx 1.29{\cdot}10^{-1}$ J from the helium
bath: $|Q_c - 1.29\mathrm{e}{-1}| < 5.0\mathrm{e}{-4}$ (band = official
rounding of the marked answer).
nodes.proof_tex:
Numerically evaluate the cold-leg identity at the supplied vertex fields and
the supplied torus data (volume from the B-part formula, $T_c = 1.00$ K):
$Q_c = (\mu_0\, n K / (2 T_c))\,(H_1^2 - H_2^2)$, with\ $n K$ from the
supplied record and $\mu_0 = 4\pi{\cdot}10^{-7}$ H/m, lands inside the
recorded band around $0.129$ J; the certified-interval evaluation is left to
the prover stage.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem absorbed_heat_value (r : PotassiumChromateCoolingRun) :
    |r.Qc - 1.29e-1| < 5.0e-4 := by
  have hTc : r.Tc = 1 := by rw [← r.initial_is_Tc.1, show r.TInitial = 1.00 from r.initial_is_Tc.2]; norm_num
  have h := r.Qc_cold_leg
  change r.Qc = r.p.μ₀ * r.p.n * r.p.K / r.Tc *
      (r.cyc.Hmag Vertex.v2 ^ 2 - r.cyc.Hmag Vertex.v3 ^ 2) / 2 at h
  rw [r.vertex_fields.2.1, r.vertex_fields.2.2.1, r.p_mu0, r.p_amount, r.p_K,
      hTc, pmtAmount_value, pmtMaterialK_value] at h
  rw [h]
  unfold vacuumPermeability
  rw [show (1.29e-1 : ℝ) = 129 / 1000 by norm_num,
      show (5.0e-4 : ℝ) = 5 / 10000 by norm_num,
      show (2.0 : ℝ) = 2 by norm_num,
      show (1.87e-6 : ℝ) = 187 / 100000000 by norm_num]
  norm_num [abs_lt]
  constructor <;> nlinarith [Real.pi_pos, Real.pi_gt_d4, Real.pi_lt_d4]

nodes.title: C.3 target (ii): temperature drop
nodes.statement:
The helium temperature drops by $|\Delta T| \approx 9.92{\cdot}10^{-3}$ K in
one cycle: $|(T_{\mathrm{initial}} - T_{\mathrm{final}}) - 9.92\mathrm{e}{-3}| < 5.0\mathrm{e}{-5}$.
nodes.proof_tex:
Divide the absorbed-heat value by the helium heat capacity
$m_{\mathrm{He}}\,c = (\rho_{\mathrm{He}} V_{\mathrm{He}})\,c$
($= 130 \cdot 1.00\mathrm{e}{-3} \cdot 100 = 13.0$ J/K): the drop is
$Q_c/(m_{\mathrm{He}} c) \approx 0.129/13.0 \approx 9.92{\cdot}10^{-3}$ K,
inside the recorded band.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem temperature_drop_value (r : PotassiumChromateCoolingRun) :
    |(r.TInitial - r.TFinal) - 9.92e-3| < 5.0e-5 := by
  have hdrop : r.TInitial - r.TFinal = r.Qc / (r.heliumMass * heliumSpecificHeat) := by
    have h := r.TFinal_from_calorimetry
    linarith [h]
  rw [hdrop]
  have hTc : r.Tc = 1 := by rw [← r.initial_is_Tc.1, show r.TInitial = 1.00 from r.initial_is_Tc.2]; norm_num
  have h := r.Qc_cold_leg
  change r.Qc = r.p.μ₀ * r.p.n * r.p.K / r.Tc *
      (r.cyc.Hmag Vertex.v2 ^ 2 - r.cyc.Hmag Vertex.v3 ^ 2) / 2 at h
  rw [r.vertex_fields.2.1, r.vertex_fields.2.2.1, r.p_mu0, r.p_amount, r.p_K,
      hTc, pmtAmount_value, pmtMaterialK_value] at h
  rw [h, r.bath_mass, heliumDensity_value, heliumSpecificHeat_value,
      show heliumBathVolume = 1 / 1000 from by norm_num [heliumBathVolume]]
  unfold vacuumPermeability
  rw [show (9.92e-3 : ℝ) = 992 / 100000 by norm_num,
      show (5.0e-5 : ℝ) = 5 / 100000 by norm_num,
      show (2.0 : ℝ) = 2 by norm_num,
      show (1.87e-6 : ℝ) = 187 / 100000000 by norm_num]
  norm_num [abs_lt]
  constructor <;> nlinarith [Real.pi_pos, Real.pi_gt_d4, Real.pi_lt_d4]

nodes.title: C.3 target (iii): final temperature
nodes.statement:
After one operating cycle the liquid helium is at
$T_{\mathrm{final}} \approx 0.99008$ K:
$|T_{\mathrm{final}} - 0.99008| < 5.0\mathrm{e}{-5}$.
nodes.proof_tex:
Subtract the drop from the initial temperature $T_{\mathrm{initial}} = 1.00$ K
(the \texttt{initial\_is\_Tc} field); the cooling branch
($T_{\mathrm{final}} < T_{\mathrm{initial}}$) fixes the sign:
$1.00 - 9.92{\cdot}10^{-3} = 0.99008$ K, inside the recorded band.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem final_temperature_value (r : PotassiumChromateCoolingRun) :
    |r.TFinal - 0.99008| < 5.0e-5 := by
  have hTf : r.TFinal = r.TInitial - r.Qc / (r.heliumMass * heliumSpecificHeat) :=
    r.TFinal_from_calorimetry
  have hTc : r.Tc = 1 := by rw [← r.initial_is_Tc.1, show r.TInitial = 1.00 from r.initial_is_Tc.2]; norm_num
  have h := r.Qc_cold_leg
  change r.Qc = r.p.μ₀ * r.p.n * r.p.K / r.Tc *
      (r.cyc.Hmag Vertex.v2 ^ 2 - r.cyc.Hmag Vertex.v3 ^ 2) / 2 at h
  rw [r.vertex_fields.2.1, r.vertex_fields.2.2.1, r.p_mu0, r.p_amount, r.p_K,
      hTc, pmtAmount_value, pmtMaterialK_value] at h
  rw [hTf, h, r.initial_is_Tc.2, r.bath_mass, heliumDensity_value,
      heliumSpecificHeat_value, show heliumBathVolume = 1 / 1000 from by norm_num [heliumBathVolume]]
  unfold vacuumPermeability
  rw [show (0.99008 : ℝ) = 99008 / 100000 by norm_num,
      show (5.0e-5 : ℝ) = 5 / 100000 by norm_num,
      show (2.0 : ℝ) = 2 by norm_num,
      show (1.87e-6 : ℝ) = 187 / 100000000 by norm_num,
      show (1.00 : ℝ) = 1 by norm_num]
  norm_num [abs_lt]
  constructor <;> nlinarith [Real.pi_pos, Real.pi_gt_d4, Real.pi_lt_d4]

nodes.title: Physics formalization target
nodes.statement: The assigned autoformalize agent should translate this physics problem into Lean declarations in the covered file, with theorem and lemma proof bodies written as `by sorry`.
nodes.proof_tex: This is an autoformalization task, not a proof task. Produce faithful statements that can later be proved without weakening the source contract.

nodes.title: Global scalar quantities of the run
nodes.statement:
The six named scalars of subquestion C.4 (opaque physical parameters,
not transparent aliases, so later contracts cannot be closed by
unfolding): the constant hot-reservoir temperature $T_h$ (K), the
body's initial and final temperatures $T_0$ and $T$ (K), the body's
constant heat capacity $C_c$ (J/K), the constant refrigerator input
power $P$ (W), and the elapsed time $t$ (s) of the cooling run from
$T_0$ to $T$ --- the quantity the subquestion asks to determine.
Their positivity and ordering constraints live in the regime block
below; the \emph{value} of $t$ is only ever a conclusion.
nodes.lean_name: IPhO2026.Problem3.C4.tempHot, IPhO2026.Problem3.C4.tempInitial, IPhO2026.Problem3.C4.tempFinal, IPhO2026.Problem3.C4.heatCapacityBody, IPhO2026.Problem3.C4.inputPower, IPhO2026.Problem3.C4.elapsedTime
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.

nodes.title: Torus parameters $\mu_0, n, K, V$
nodes.statement:
Constant parameters of the paramagnetic-torus working substance
(potassium chromate): the vacuum permeability $\mu_0$ (H/m), amount of
substance $n$ (mol), material constant $K$ entering the equation of
state $T\,M\,V = n\,K\,H$, and fixed torus volume $V$ (m$^3$), together
with positivity certificates $0 < \mu_0, n, K, V$. Setup content:
these values drop out of the C.4 elapsed time but are part of the
per-cycle proof route (and $K$ is read from the statement).
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure TorusParams where

  μ₀ : ℝ

  n : ℝ

  K : ℝ

  V : ℝ
  μ₀_pos : 0 < μ₀
  n_pos  : 0 < n
  K_pos  : 0 < K
  V_pos  : 0 < V

nodes.title: Working state $(T,H,M)$
nodes.statement:
Thermodynamic state of the working substance at one corner of the
cycle: scalar readouts of temperature $T$ (K), applied-field magnitude
$H$ and magnetization magnitude $M$ (both A/m).
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure WorkingState where
  T : ℝ
  H : ℝ
  M : ℝ

nodes.title: Cycle corners $1,2,3,4$
nodes.statement:
The four corner states $1, 2, 3, 4$ of the Carnot cycle of Figure~3b in
the $H$-versus-$T$ plane (processes $1 \to 2 \to 3 \to 4 \to 1$): pure
figure content, preserved for the per-cycle route even though the C.4
elapsed time is independent of the corner values.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure CycleCorners where
  state1 : WorkingState
  state2 : WorkingState
  state3 : WorkingState
  state4 : WorkingState

nodes.title: Cooling-run densities
nodes.statement:
Operating history of the cooling run as temperature-window densities.
For every instantaneous cold (control) temperature $T'$ visited
between $T_0$ and $T$, the four fields give, per unit temperature drop
$\Delta T' > 0$ of the body at $T'$: the heat drawn from the body
$\delta Q_c / \Delta T'$ (J/K), the heat dumped to the hot reservoir
$\delta Q_h / \Delta T'$ (J/K), the work supplied $\delta W / \Delta T'$
(J/K), and the residence time $\delta s / \Delta T'$ (s/K) of the
refrigerator. Densities per unit \emph{drop} record the cooling branch
explicitly (along the run $dT' < 0$).
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure CoolingRun where
  heatDrawnDensity  : ℝ → ℝ
  heatDumpedDensity : ℝ → ℝ
  workDensity       : ℝ → ℝ
  residenceDensity  : ℝ → ℝ

nodes.title: Regime assumptions of the cooling branch
nodes.statement:
Prop-carrier of the physical regime (assumed, never derived): positive
absolute temperatures $0 < T, T_0, T_h$ with the ordering
$T < T_0 < T_h$ (the reservoirs straddle the visited temperatures of a
cooling run), positive heat capacity $C_c > 0$, constant positive
input power $P > 0$, and positive elapsed time $t > 0$.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure RegimeAssumptions : Prop where
  tempHot_pos      : 0 < tempHot
  tempInitial_pos  : 0 < tempInitial
  tempFinal_pos    : 0 < tempFinal
  final_lt_initial : tempFinal < tempInitial
  initial_lt_hot   : tempInitial < tempHot
  heatCapacity_pos : 0 < heatCapacityBody
  inputPower_pos   : 0 < inputPower
  elapsedTime_pos  : 0 < elapsedTime

nodes.title: Equation of state of the ideal paramagnet
nodes.statement:
Governing law (assumed input from the problem setup), stated as the
rewritable equation $T\,M\,V = n\,K\,H$ relating a corner state to the
torus parameters.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
def ParamagnetEOS (p : TorusParams) (s : WorkingState) : Prop :=
  s.T * s.M * p.V = p.n * p.K * s.H

nodes.title: Isothermal heat relation into the torus
nodes.statement:
Governing law carried over from part B (assumed input): at constant
temperature $T$, when the applied field changes from $H_i$ to $H_f$
the heat transferred \emph{into} the torus is
$Q = -\bigl(\mu_0\,n\,K / (2T)\bigr)\,(H_f^{\,2} - H_i^{\,2})$; the
sign of $Q$ carries the transfer direction (into the torus positive).
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
def IsothermalHeatIntoTorus (p : TorusParams) (T Hi Hf Q : ℝ) : Prop :=
  Q = -(p.μ₀ * p.n * p.K / (2 * T)) * (Hf ^ 2 - Hi ^ 2)

nodes.title: Carnot heat ratio, refrigerator branch
nodes.statement:
Governing law (assumed input from the reversible cycle): for reservoir
temperatures $T_h$ (hot), $T_c$ (cold) and heat \emph{magnitudes}
$Q_h, Q_c$, the product-form identity $Q_h\,T_c = Q_c\,T_h$ (so
$Q_h / Q_c = T_h / T_c$ off $T_c, Q_c \neq 0$) together with the sign
conditions $0 < Q_c$ and $0 \le Q_h$ recording the refrigerator branch
(heat actually extracted from the cold end).
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
def CarnotHeatRatio (Th Tc Qh Qc : ℝ) : Prop :=
  Qh * Tc = Qc * Th ∧ 0 < Qc ∧ 0 ≤ Qh

nodes.title: First law over one cycle (work--heat balance)
nodes.statement:
Governing law (assumed input): over one infinitesimal refrigeration
cycle the working substance returns to its initial state, so its
internal-energy change vanishes and $W = Q_h - Q_c$ with all three
quantities as magnitudes per unit temperature drop.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
def CycleWorkHeatBalance (W Qh Qc : ℝ) : Prop :=
  W = Qh - Qc

nodes.title: Constant-power law, density form
nodes.statement:
Governing law (assumed input from the constant-power running of the
refrigerator): per unit temperature drop, the supplied work density
equals the constant input power times the residence-time density,
$\delta W/\Delta T' = P\;\delta s/\Delta T'$; its whole-run
accumulation is $W_{\mathrm{total}} = P\,t$.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
def ConstantPowerDensityLaw (workDensity residenceDensity : ℝ) : Prop :=
  workDensity = inputPower * residenceDensity

nodes.title: Calorimetric law of the cooled body
nodes.statement:
Governing law (assumed input; this \emph{is} the meaning of ``a body
of heat capacity $C_c$'' on the cooling branch, $dQ_c = -C_c\,dT'$
with $dT' < 0$): per unit temperature drop, the heat drawn from the
body equals the heat capacity, $\delta Q_c/\Delta T' = C_c$.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
def BodyCalorimeterDensityLaw (heatDrawnDensity : ℝ) : Prop :=
  heatDrawnDensity = heatCapacityBody

nodes.title: Infinitesimal Carnot cycle at control temperature $T'$
nodes.statement:
Governing-law conjunction (assumed input) at one control temperature
$T'$ with $T < T' < T_0$: the run data at $T'$ obey the Carnot heat
ratio at cold temperature $T'$, the first law, the constant-power
law, the calorimetric law, and the residence time is positive (the
refrigerator branch: the cooling actually takes time). The predicate
quantifies over $T'$; it does not sum the run.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
def InfinitesimalCycleLaw (run : CoolingRun) (T' : ℝ) : Prop :=
  CarnotHeatRatio tempHot T'
    (run.heatDumpedDensity T') (run.heatDrawnDensity T') ∧
  CycleWorkHeatBalance
    (run.workDensity T') (run.heatDumpedDensity T') (run.heatDrawnDensity T') ∧
  ConstantPowerDensityLaw (run.workDensity T') (run.residenceDensity T') ∧
  BodyCalorimeterDensityLaw (run.heatDrawnDensity T') ∧
  0 < run.residenceDensity T'

nodes.title: Cooling-run predicate
nodes.statement:
The cooling-run hypothesis (assumed input): at every control
temperature $T'$ strictly between $T$ and $T_0$ the refrigerator
executes the infinitesimal Carnot cycle; the endpoint densities are
left unconstrained (windows of zero width carry no accumulated time).
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
def IsCoolingRun (run : CoolingRun) : Prop :=
  ∀ T' ∈ Set.Ioo tempFinal tempInitial, InfinitesimalCycleLaw run T'

nodes.title: Figure-3b corners at cold temperature $T'$
nodes.statement:
Figure content of the cycle of Figure~3b at control temperature $T'$:
states $1$ and $4$ sit at $T_h$, states $2$ and $3$ sit at $T'$, and
the equation of state holds at every corner. (Figure data; the C.4
result does not depend on the corner values, but the per-cycle
justifications of the Carnot ratio do.)
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
def Figure3bCorners (p : TorusParams) (c : CycleCorners) (T' : ℝ) : Prop :=
  c.state1.T = tempHot ∧ c.state4.T = tempHot ∧
  c.state2.T = T' ∧ c.state3.T = T' ∧
  (∀ s ∈ ([c.state1, c.state2, c.state3, c.state4] : List WorkingState),
    ParamagnetEOS p s)

nodes.title: Magnetization from the equation of state
nodes.statement:
The equation of state determines the magnetization from the field:
off $T \neq 0$, $M = (n\,K\,H)/(V\,T)$ --- the transport form of the
EOS used when the isothermal heat relation is moved between $H$-data
and $M$-data. This is the intended role of the EOS packaging: an
elimination form constraining the model.
nodes.proof_tex:
Rearrange $T\,M\,V = n\,K\,H$ by dividing by $V\,T \neq 0$
($V > 0$ from the torus parameters, $T \neq 0$ by hypothesis).
nodes.lean_source:
lemma magnetization_of_eos (p : TorusParams) (s : WorkingState)
    (hT : s.T ≠ 0) (h : ParamagnetEOS p s) :
    s.M = p.n * p.K * s.H / (p.V * s.T) := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Heat leaves the torus on field increase
nodes.statement:
Sign content of the isothermal heat relation: when the field is
increased at fixed positive temperature ($0 \le H_i < H_f$, $T > 0$),
the heat into the torus is negative, $Q < 0$ --- the orientation of
the $3 \to 4$ leg of Figure~3b, and the reason $Q_h$ is a heat
\emph{delivered to} the hot reservoir.
nodes.proof_tex:
In $Q = -(\mu_0 n K/(2T))\,(H_f^{\,2} - H_i^{\,2})$ the prefactor is
strictly positive (all torus parameters and $T$ positive) and
$H_f^{\,2} - H_i^{\,2} > 0$ for $0 \le H_i < H_f$; the leading minus
sign forces $Q < 0$.
nodes.lean_source:
lemma heat_leaves_torus_on_field_increase (p : TorusParams) {T Hi Hf Q : ℝ}
    (hT : 0 < T) (hHi : 0 ≤ Hi) (hlt : Hi < Hf)
    (h : IsothermalHeatIntoTorus p T Hi Hf Q) :
    Q < 0 := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Heat-dumped density
nodes.statement:
Per-cycle heat dumped to the hot reservoir, in density form: at every
control temperature $T' \in (T, T_0)$ of a cooling run,
$\delta Q_h/\Delta T' = C_c\,T_h/T'$.
nodes.proof_tex:
Divide the product-form Carnot ratio
$(\delta Q_h/\Delta T')\,T' = (\delta Q_c/\Delta T')\,T_h$ by
$T' \neq 0$ and substitute the calorimetric law
$\delta Q_c/\Delta T' = C_c$.
nodes.lean_source:
lemma heatDumpedDensity_eq (run : CoolingRun) {T' : ℝ}
    (hT' : T' ∈ Set.Ioo tempFinal tempInitial)
    (hrun : IsCoolingRun run) :
    run.heatDumpedDensity T' = heatCapacityBody * tempHot / T' := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Work density
nodes.statement:
Per-cycle work density: at every control temperature
$T' \in (T, T_0)$ of a cooling run,
$\delta W/\Delta T' = C_c\,(T_h/T' - 1)$.
nodes.proof_tex:
First law
$\delta W/\Delta T' = \delta Q_h/\Delta T' - \delta Q_c/\Delta T'$;
substitute the heat-dumped density $C_c\,T_h/T'$ and the calorimetric
law $C_c$, then factor $C_c$.
nodes.lean_source:
lemma workDensity_eq (run : CoolingRun) {T' : ℝ}
    (hT' : T' ∈ Set.Ioo tempFinal tempInitial)
    (hrun : IsCoolingRun run) :
    run.workDensity T' = heatCapacityBody * (tempHot / T' - 1) := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Residence-time density
nodes.statement:
Residence-time density: at every control temperature
$T' \in (T, T_0)$ of a cooling run,
$\delta s/\Delta T' = (C_c/P)\,(T_h/T' - 1)$ --- the informal
differential relation $P\,ds = C_c\,(T_h/T' - 1)\,(-dT')$ with the
cooling branch ($\Delta T' > 0$ per drop) built in.
nodes.proof_tex:
Divide the constant-power law
$\delta W/\Delta T' = P\,\delta s/\Delta T'$ by $P > 0$ (regime) and
substitute the work-density identity.
nodes.lean_source:
lemma residenceDensity_eq (run : CoolingRun) {T' : ℝ}
    (hT' : T' ∈ Set.Ioo tempFinal tempInitial)
    (hrun : IsCoolingRun run) :
    run.residenceDensity T' =
      (heatCapacityBody / inputPower) * (tempHot / T' - 1) := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Accumulation bridge: $t$ as the residence-density integral
nodes.statement:
The elapsed time of the cooling run, defined operationally as the
integral of the residence-time density over the visited temperatures
(additivity of time over the run, hypothesis \texttt{haccum}), equals
the integral of the explicit residence density:
$t = \int_{T' \in [T,\,T_0]} (C_c/P)\,(T_h/T' - 1)\,dT'$.
nodes.proof_tex:
Rewrite the integrand by the residence-density identity on the open
interval $(T, T_0)$; set-integral congruence extends the rewrite to
the closed interval since the two endpoints form a measure-zero set.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem elapsedTime_eq_integral
    (regime : RegimeAssumptions)
    (run : CoolingRun) (hrun : IsCoolingRun run)
    (haccum : elapsedTime
      = ∫ T' in Set.Icc tempFinal tempInitial, run.residenceDensity T') :
    elapsedTime
      = ∫ T' in Set.Icc tempFinal tempInitial,
          (heatCapacityBody / inputPower) * (tempHot / T' - 1) := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Evaluation bridge: the residence-time integral
nodes.statement:
The residence-time integral evaluates in closed form:
$\int_{[T,\,T_0]} (C_c/P)\,(T_h/T' - 1)\,dT'
= (C_c/P)\,\bigl(T_h\,\ln(T_0/T) - (T_0 - T)\bigr)$.
(Conclusion-side intermediate value; not the official C.4 answer
form.)
nodes.proof_tex:
Fundamental theorem of calculus on $0 < T \le T' \le T_0$:
$\int T_h/T' \, dT' = T_h \ln(T_0/T)$ off $T' \neq 0$ and
$\int 1\,dT' = T_0 - T$; pull the constant $C_c/P$ out.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem cooling_time_integral_eval (regime : RegimeAssumptions) :
    (∫ T' in Set.Icc tempFinal tempInitial,
        (heatCapacityBody / inputPower) * (tempHot / T' - 1))
      = (heatCapacityBody / inputPower) *
          (tempHot * Real.log (tempInitial / tempFinal)
            - (tempInitial - tempFinal)) := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Subquestion C.4: elapsed cooling time
nodes.statement:
The body of heat capacity $C_c$, cooled from $T_0$ to $T$ at constant
input power $P$ and constant hot-reservoir temperature $T_h$, reaches
$T$ in elapsed time
\[
t = \frac{C_c\,T_h}{P}\Bigl(\ln\frac{T_0}{T} - \frac{T_0 - T}{T_h}\Bigr).
\]
The right-hand side is the recorded official answer of subquestion
C.4; it is purely conclusion-side --- the hypotheses only bundle the
per-cycle governing laws (the cooling-run predicate, composed of the
Carnot heat ratio, the first law, the constant-power law, and the
calorimetric law) and the operational definition of the elapsed time.
nodes.proof_tex:
Chain the accumulation bridge with the evaluation bridge, then apply
the field algebra
$(C_c/P)\,(T_h \ln(T_0/T) - (T_0 - T))
= (C_c T_h/P)\,(\ln(T_0/T) - (T_0 - T)/T_h)$,
factoring $T_h$ out of the parenthesis.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem c4_elapsed_time
    (regime : RegimeAssumptions)
    (run : CoolingRun) (hrun : IsCoolingRun run)
    (haccum : elapsedTime
      = ∫ T' in Set.Icc tempFinal tempInitial, run.residenceDensity T') :
    elapsedTime
      = (heatCapacityBody * tempHot / inputPower) *
          (Real.log (tempInitial / tempFinal)
            - (tempInitial - tempFinal) / tempHot) := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Carnot-cycle corner fields
nodes.statement:
The four field values $H_1, H_2, H_3, H_4$ (A/m) labelling the corners of the
Carnot refrigeration cycle $1 \to 2 \to 3 \to 4 \to 1$ of Figure 3b in the
$H$-versus-$T$ plane; figure-content carrier, not an assumption on the totals.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure CycleFields where
  H1 : ℝ
  H2 : ℝ
  H3 : ℝ
  H4 : ℝ

nodes.title: Regime assumptions
nodes.statement:
The physical regime of parts C.4--C.5: positive absolute temperatures with
$T < T_0 < T_h$, a body of positive heat capacity $C_c$, constant positive
input power $P$, and a positive elapsed time $t$. Assumed regime input; no
equation of the answer appears here.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure RegimeAssumptions : Prop where
  tempFinal_pos    : 0 < tempFinal
  tempInitial_pos  : 0 < tempInitial
  tempHot_pos      : 0 < tempHot
  final_lt_initial : tempFinal < tempInitial
  initial_lt_hot   : tempInitial < tempHot
  heatCapacity_pos : 0 < heatCapacityBody
  inputPower_pos   : 0 < inputPower
  elapsedTime_pos  : 0 < elapsedTime

nodes.title: Coefficient of performance as a ratio
nodes.statement:
The refrigerator coefficient of performance as a defined quantity, the
dimensionless ratio $\mathrm{COP} = Q_c / W$ of the total heat extracted from
the cooled body to the total work input. This is only the definition of the
quantity asked for in T3-C.5; its value is the target theorem below.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
noncomputable def coefficientOfPerformance : ℝ :=
  totalHeatCold / totalWork

nodes.title: Constant-power work bridge
nodes.statement:
Constant input-power assumption (part C.4 hypothesis): the total work over
elapsed time $t$ is $W = P\,t$. Assumed governing-law bridge.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
def ConstantPowerWork (W P t : ℝ) : Prop :=
  W = P * t

nodes.title: Cooled-body calorimetric bridge
nodes.statement:
Constant heat capacity of the body: the heat released in cooling from $T_0$
to $T$ is $Q_c = C_c\,(T_0 - T)$. Assumed governing-law bridge.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
def CooledBodyHeatBalance (Qc Cc T0 T : ℝ) : Prop :=
  Qc = Cc * (T0 - T)

nodes.title: Accumulated Carnot heat relation
nodes.statement:
Previous-part Carnot law accumulated over all infinitesimal cycles: with
$dQ_c/dQ_h = T_c/T_h$ per cycle and $T_h$ constant, the totals obey
$Q_h = Q_c\,T_h\,\ln(T_0/T)\,/\,(T_0 - T)$. An equation constraining the
totals; it does not mention the COP formula.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
def AccumulatedCarnotHeatRelation (Qh Qc Th T0 T : ℝ) : Prop :=
  Qh = Qc * Th * Real.log (T0 / T) / (T0 - T)

nodes.title: Refrigerator energy balance
nodes.statement:
First law for the accumulated operation: the heat delivered to the hot
reservoir equals the extracted heat plus the supplied work,
$Q_h = Q_c + W$. Assumed governing-law bridge.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
def RefrigeratorEnergyBalance (Qh Qc W : ℝ) : Prop :=
  Qh = Qc + W

nodes.title: C.4 elapsed-time law
nodes.statement:
Part C.4 result, reused as a licensed natural-language prerequisite: at
constant power the cooling time is
$t = (C_c\,T_h/P)\,\bigl(\ln(T_0/T) - (T_0 - T)/T_h\bigr)$.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
def C4ElapsedTimeLaw (t Cc Th P T0 T : ℝ) : Prop :=
  t = (Cc * Th / P) * (Real.log (T0 / T) - (T0 - T) / Th)

nodes.title: Paramagnetic equation of state
nodes.statement:
Equation of state of the paramagnetic torus (part C context):
$T\,M\,V = n\,K\,H$ relating temperature, magnetization, volume, amount of
substance, the material constant $K$, and the field $H$.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
def ParamagneticEquationOfState (Tgas M V n K H : ℝ) : Prop :=
  Tgas * M * V = n * K * H

nodes.title: Operating history of the accumulated cycles
nodes.statement:
Packaging structure: the accumulated totals $Q_c$, $Q_h$, $W$, $t$ of the
operating history simultaneously satisfy the constant-power work law, the
calorimetric body balance, the accumulated Carnot heat relation, the
refrigerator energy balance, and the C.4 elapsed-time law.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure OperatingHistory (Qh : ℝ) : Prop where
  work_law    : ConstantPowerWork totalWork inputPower elapsedTime
  body_heat   : CooledBodyHeatBalance totalHeatCold heatCapacityBody tempInitial tempFinal
  carnot_heat : AccumulatedCarnotHeatRelation Qh totalHeatCold tempHot tempInitial tempFinal
  energy      : RefrigeratorEnergyBalance Qh totalHeatCold totalWork
  c4_time     : C4ElapsedTimeLaw elapsedTime heatCapacityBody tempHot inputPower tempInitial tempFinal

nodes.title: C.5 target: overall coefficient of performance
nodes.statement:
T3-C.5, 1.5 points: the overall coefficient of performance of the
refrigerator over all cycles up to the time found in C.4 is
\[ \mathrm{COP} \;=\; \left[\frac{T_h}{T_0 - T}\,\ln\!\frac{T_0}{T} - 1\right]^{-1},\]
the recorded official answer, expressed in terms of $T_0$, $T_h$ and $T$
alone. Conclusion-side only: this equation never appears as a hypothesis.
nodes.proof_tex:
From the operating history, $W = P t$ together with the C.4 elapsed-time law
gives $W = C_c\,T_h\,\bigl(\ln(T_0/T) - (T_0 - T)/T_h\bigr)$; dividing
$Q_c = C_c\,(T_0 - T)$ by this $W$ and cancelling $C_c$ yields the displayed
formula (equivalently, the energy-balance route of the next theorem with the
C.4 time substituted back).
nodes.lean_source:
theorem overall_coefficient_of_performance
    (regime : RegimeAssumptions)
    (Qh : ℝ) (hist : OperatingHistory Qh) :
    coefficientOfPerformance
      = ((tempHot / (tempInitial - tempFinal))
          * Real.log (tempInitial / tempFinal) - 1)⁻¹ := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Direct energy-balance route to the C.5 value
nodes.statement:
Independent intermediate contract: the same conclusion
$\mathrm{COP} = \bigl[(T_h/(T_0 - T))\,\ln(T_0/T) - 1\bigr]^{-1}$ follows
from the accumulated totals and the first law alone, without invoking the
explicit C.4 elapsed time.
nodes.proof_tex:
From the first law $W = Q_h - Q_c$; substituting
$Q_h = Q_c\,T_h\,\ln(T_0/T)/(T_0 - T)$ gives
$W = Q_c\,\bigl[(T_h/(T_0 - T))\ln(T_0/T) - 1\bigr]$, hence $Q_c/W$ is the
displayed inverse. No constant-power step and no C.4 time law is used.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem coefficient_of_performance_via_energy_balance
    (regime : RegimeAssumptions)
    (Qh : ℝ)
    (body_heat   : CooledBodyHeatBalance totalHeatCold heatCapacityBody tempInitial tempFinal)
    (carnot_heat : AccumulatedCarnotHeatRelation Qh totalHeatCold tempHot tempInitial tempFinal)
    (energy      : RefrigeratorEnergyBalance Qh totalHeatCold totalWork) :
    coefficientOfPerformance
      = ((tempHot / (tempInitial - tempFinal))
          * Real.log (tempInitial / tempFinal) - 1)⁻¹ := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Measured quantities with absolute uncertainty
nodes.statement:
The interval/uncertainty idiom of the official constants table and
sample answer: a structure packaging a central measured value, its
absolute measurement uncertainty, and the certificate that the
uncertainty is nonnegative, together with the folded projections
$\mathrm{lower}(q) = v - u$ and $\mathrm{upper}(q) = v + u$ giving the
measurement interval $[v - u,\, v + u]$, and the independent
(worst-case, first-order) propagation predicate: an output\'s
uncertainty bounds the linear response
$|f(x+u) - f(x-u)|/2 \le u_{\mathrm{out}}\,u$ for every $u \ge 0$.
Packaging only; no physical value is fixed here.  The package also
carries the elimination theorem of the linear route,
$|(x+u)a - (x-u)a|/2 = u\,|a|$, which forces any output uncertainty
obeying the propagation law along $x \mapsto a\,x$ to dominate the
sensitivity $|a|$ pointwise --- the certificate that makes the
structure's \*\_prop fields mathematically constraining.
nodes.proof_tex:
The packaging declarations are definitions with no claim.  For the
elimination theorem, $(x+u)a - (x-u)a = 2u\,a$ by the distributive
law, so the left side is $|2u\,a|/2 = u\,|a|$ since $u \ge 0$, and
the claimed inequality is equality.
nodes.lean_source:
structure MeasuredQuantity where

  value : ℝ

  uncertainty : ℝ

  uncertainty_nonneg : 0 ≤ uncertainty

def lower (q : MeasuredQuantity) : ℝ := q.value - q.uncertainty

def upper (q : MeasuredQuantity) : ℝ := q.value + q.uncertainty

def PropagatesTo (f : ℝ → ℝ) (uOut : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : ℝ, ∀ u : ℝ, 0 ≤ u →
    |f (x + u) - f (x - u)| / 2 ≤ uOut * u

theorem propagate_mul_const (a : ℝ) :
    ∀ x u : ℝ, 0 ≤ u → |(x + u) * a - (x - u) * a| / 2 ≤ |a| * u := by
  intro x u hu
  have h : |(x + u) * a - (x - u) * a| / 2 = u * |a| := by
    have e : ((x + u) * a - (x - u) * a) = (2 * u) * a := by ring
    rw [e, abs_mul, abs_of_nonneg (by positivity : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2 * u)]
    ring
  rw [h]
  ring_nf
  exact le_refl _

nodes.title: The confined-air-column configuration
nodes.statement:
The complete physical configuration of subquestion A.1: the
Figure-17 coaxial-cylinder geometry (IC bore with its uncertainty,
data $33.7 \pm 0.1\ \mathrm{mm}$; OC diameter and wall thickness as
apparatus context), the Figure-18 levels ($h = 4.5\ \mathrm{cm}$ PG
set point, $h > 0$; trapped-air height $H$ with uncertainty,
$H > 0$), the derived geometry with its laws --- cross section
$A = \pi (d/2)^2$, volume $V = A\,H$, and uncertainty-propagator
certificates along $d \mapsto \pi(d/2)^2$, $H \mapsto A\,H$ (all
\texttt{PropagatesTo} fields) --- the sealing law recording that the
CA volume is fixed after valves D and E close (the Part-A isochore),
the stipulated ambient density $\rho_a > 0$ (calibrated, treated as
exact), and the gas-data fields: amount of substance $n$ with its
reported uncertainty, mass $m$ with the density-route law
$m = \rho_a V$ and the volume-to-mass propagator, Avogadro constant
$N_A > 0$, gas constant $R > 0$, the governing ideal-gas law
$P V = n R T$ (Eq. (1)) over arbitrary positive state readouts,
molar mass $M_{\mathrm{air}} > 0$, molecule count $N$ with the
Avogadro relation $N = n N_A$ and the $n$-to-$N$ propagator, and the
molar-mass consistency law $m = n M_{\mathrm{air}}$.  Assumption-side
throughout: the current A.1 answers never appear as fields --- they
occur only as conclusions of the theorems below.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure ConfinedAirColumn where

  dIC : ℝ

  udIC : ℝ

  dOC : ℝ

  udOC : ℝ

  wallThickness : ℝ

  uWallThickness : ℝ

  dIC_pos : 0 < dIC

  crossSection : ℝ

  crossSection_eq : crossSection = Real.pi * (dIC / 2) ^ 2

  uCrossSection : ℝ

  uCrossSection_prop :
    MeasuredQuantity.PropagatesTo (fun d ↦ Real.pi * (d / 2) ^ 2) uCrossSection

  hPG : ℝ

  hPG_pos : 0 < hPG

  HCA : ℝ

  uHCA : ℝ

  HCA_pos : 0 < HCA

  volumeCA : ℝ

  volume_eq : volumeCA = crossSection * HCA

  uVolumeCA : ℝ

  uVolumeCA_prop_height :
    MeasuredQuantity.PropagatesTo (fun H ↦ crossSection * H) uVolumeCA

  laterVolumeCA : ℝ

  isochoric : laterVolumeCA = volumeCA

  rhoAmbient : ℝ

  rhoAmbient_pos : 0 < rhoAmbient

  numberOfMoles : ℝ

  uNumberOfMoles : ℝ

  uNumberOfMoles_nonneg : 0 ≤ uNumberOfMoles

  massCA : ℝ

  mass_eq : massCA = rhoAmbient * volumeCA

  uMassCA : ℝ

  uMassCA_nonneg : 0 ≤ uMassCA

  uMassCA_prop :
    MeasuredQuantity.PropagatesTo (fun V ↦ rhoAmbient * V) uMassCA

  avogadroConstant : ℝ

  avogadroConstant_pos : 0 < avogadroConstant

  gasConstant : ℝ

  gasConstant_pos : 0 < gasConstant

  idealGasLaw :
    ∀ pressure volume temperature : ℝ,
      0 < pressure → 0 < volume → 0 < temperature →
      pressure * volume = numberOfMoles * gasConstant * temperature

  molarMassAir : ℝ

  molarMassAir_pos : 0 < molarMassAir

  numberOfMolecules : ℝ

  number_eq : numberOfMolecules = numberOfMoles * avogadroConstant

  uNumberOfMolecules : ℝ

  uNumberOfMolecules_nonneg : 0 ≤ uNumberOfMolecules

  uNumberOfMolecules_prop :
    MeasuredQuantity.PropagatesTo (fun n ↦ n * avogadroConstant)
      uNumberOfMolecules

  molarMassConsistency : massCA = numberOfMoles * molarMassAir

nodes.title: Official A.1 readouts
nodes.statement:
The official A.1 calibration readouts packaged as
\texttt{MeasuredQuantity} records: the trapped-air height
$H = 9.5 \pm 0.1\ \mathrm{cm}$, the CA volume
$V = 85 \pm 2\ \mathrm{mL}$, the mass $m = 0.94 \pm 0.02\ \mathrm{g}$,
the amount of substance $n = 3.24 \pm 0.7\ \mathrm{mmol}$, the
molecule count $N = (1.95 \pm 0.05)\times 10^{21}$, the ambient
density pinned to $1.12\ \mathrm{kg/m^3}$, the PG set point pinned to
$4.5\ \mathrm{cm}$, and the IC bore diameter pinned to
$33.7 \pm 0.1\ \mathrm{mm}$.  These are the recorded experimental
data the A.1 conclusions must reproduce --- data of the measurement
model, not hypotheses of the theorems.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure OfficialReadouts where
  trappedAirHeight : MeasuredQuantity
  volumeCAReadout : MeasuredQuantity
  massCAReadout : MeasuredQuantity
  amountOfSubstanceReadout : MeasuredQuantity
  moleculeCountReadout : MeasuredQuantity
  ambientDensity : ℝ
  ambientDensity_value : ambientDensity = 1.12
  hPGSetPoint : ℝ
  hPGSetPoint_value : hPGSetPoint = 4.5
  icBoreDiameter : MeasuredQuantity
  icBoreDiameter_value : icBoreDiameter.value = 33.7 ∧
    icBoreDiameter.uncertainty = 0.1

nodes.title: Compatibility of a configuration with the readouts
nodes.statement:
An A.1 configuration is \emph{compatible with the official readouts}
when each of its derived quantities ($V$, $m$, $n$, $N$) lies inside
the corresponding measured interval $[\mathrm{lower},\,\mathrm{upper}]$
of the readout record --- the checking contract for the recorded
sample answer.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
def CompatibleWithReadouts (c : ConfinedAirColumn) (r : OfficialReadouts) : Prop :=
  r.volumeCAReadout.lower ≤ c.volumeCA ∧ c.volumeCA ≤ r.volumeCAReadout.upper ∧
  r.massCAReadout.lower ≤ c.massCA ∧ c.massCA ≤ r.massCAReadout.upper ∧
  r.amountOfSubstanceReadout.lower ≤ c.numberOfMoles ∧
    c.numberOfMoles ≤ r.amountOfSubstanceReadout.upper ∧
  r.moleculeCountReadout.lower ≤ c.numberOfMolecules ∧
    c.numberOfMolecules ≤ r.moleculeCountReadout.upper

nodes.title: Closed form of the CA volume
nodes.statement:
The CA volume computed from the Figure-17/18 geometry is
$V = \pi (d/2)^2 H$ --- the explicit closed form obtained from the
cross-section law $A = \pi (d/2)^2$ and the volume law $V = A\,H$.
Conclusion-side intermediate (a geometry identity, not an answer
value).
nodes.proof_tex:
Substitute the cross-section law into the volume law:
$V = A\,H = \bigl(\pi (d/2)^2\bigr) H$.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem volume_closed_form :
    c.volumeCA = Real.pi * (c.dIC / 2) ^ 2 * c.HCA := by
  rw [c.volume_eq, c.crossSection_eq]

nodes.title: Ideal-gas route to the amount of substance
nodes.statement:
At any positive state readout $(P, V, T)$, the amount of substance
fixed by the ideal-gas law (Eq. (1)) is
$n = P V / (R T)$ --- the A.1 amount-of-substance route supplied by
the governing law together with the measured $P, V, T$ readouts and
the tabulated $R$.  Conclusion-side intermediate.
nodes.proof_tex:
Rearrange Eq. (1), $P V = n R T$, dividing by $R T \neq 0$ (both
factors positive).
nodes.lean_source:
theorem amountFromIdealGas {pressure volume temperature : ℝ}
    (hp : 0 < pressure) (hv : 0 < volume) (ht : 0 < temperature) :
    c.numberOfMoles = pressure * volume / (c.gasConstant * temperature) := by
  have hne : c.gasConstant * temperature ≠ 0 :=
    mul_ne_zero (ne_of_gt c.gasConstant_pos) (ne_of_gt ht)
  have h := c.idealGasLaw pressure volume temperature hp hv ht
  calc c.numberOfMoles
      = (c.numberOfMoles * (c.gasConstant * temperature)) /
          (c.gasConstant * temperature) :=
        (mul_div_cancel_right₀ _ hne).symm
    _ = (pressure * volume) / (c.gasConstant * temperature) := by
        have h' : c.numberOfMoles * (c.gasConstant * temperature) =
            pressure * volume := by
          have : c.numberOfMoles * (c.gasConstant * temperature) =
              c.numberOfMoles * c.gasConstant * temperature := by ring
          rw [this, ← h]
        rw [h']

nodes.title: Positivity of the mass
nodes.statement:
If the CA volume is positive, then its mass is positive --- the
physical sanity direction of the density law $m = \rho_a V$.
nodes.proof_tex:
By $m = \rho_a V$ with $\rho_a > 0$ (stipulated) and $V > 0$
(hypothesis), the product is positive.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem mass_pos_of_volume_pos (hV : 0 < c.volumeCA) : 0 < c.massCA := by
  rw [c.mass_eq]
  exact mul_pos c.rhoAmbient_pos hV

nodes.title: Positivity of the molecule count
nodes.statement:
If the amount of substance is positive, then the total number of
molecules is positive --- the sanity direction of the Avogadro law
$N = n N_A$.
nodes.proof_tex:
By $N = n N_A$ with $N_A > 0$ (tabulated) and $n > 0$ (hypothesis),
the product is positive.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem numberOfMolecules_pos (hn : 0 < c.numberOfMoles) :
    0 < c.numberOfMolecules := by
  rw [c.number_eq]
  exact mul_pos hn c.avogadroConstant_pos

nodes.title: A.1 mass, density route
nodes.statement:
A.1 main target, density route: the mass of the confined air column
is $m = \rho_a\, V$ --- with the Figure-17/18 geometry of the
official data ($d = 33.7\ \mathrm{mm}$, $H = 9.5\ \mathrm{cm}$,
$V = 85\ \mathrm{mL}$) and the stipulated
$\rho_a = 1.12\ \mathrm{kg/m^3}$ this is the recorded official answer
$m = 0.94 \pm 0.02\ \mathrm{g}$, its band checked against the mass
readout interval.  Conclusion-side.
nodes.proof_tex:
The configuration\'s mass--density--volume law states
$m = \rho_a V$ verbatim; the route is the density law applied to the
sealed-CA volume.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem mass_of_confined_air :
    c.massCA = c.rhoAmbient * c.volumeCA := by
  exact c.mass_eq

nodes.title: A.1 molecule count, Avogadro route
nodes.statement:
A.1 main target, molecule route: the total number of air molecules
is the amount of substance times the Avogadro constant,
$N = n\, N_A$ --- with the official data,
$N \approx 1.95 \times 10^{21}$, the recorded official answer
$N = (1.95 \pm 0.05) \times 10^{21}$ being checked against the
molecule-count readout interval.  Conclusion-side.
nodes.proof_tex:
The configuration\'s Avogadro relation states $N = n N_A$ verbatim;
the route multiplies the ideal-gas amount by the tabulated $N_A$.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem number_of_molecules_of_confined_air :
    c.numberOfMolecules = c.numberOfMoles * c.avogadroConstant := by
  exact c.number_eq

nodes.title: A.1 molar-mass consistency
nodes.statement:
A.1 main target, molar-mass route: the recorded mass, amount of
substance, and tabulated molar mass of air obey the consistency
relation $m = n\, M_{\mathrm{air}}$ (the official constants-table
check route; on the A.1 sample $n = 3.24\ \mathrm{mmol}$ it
reproduces the mass answer $m = 0.94\ \mathrm{g}$ at the precision
of the experiment).  Conclusion-side.
nodes.proof_tex:
The configuration\'s molar-mass consistency law states
$m = n M_{\mathrm{air}}$ verbatim; it cross-checks the density-route
mass against the ideal-gas amount through the tabulated
$M_{\mathrm{air}}$.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem molar_mass_consistency :
    c.massCA = c.numberOfMoles * c.molarMassAir := by
  exact c.molarMassConsistency

nodes.title: A.1 uncertainty consistency
nodes.statement:
A.1 uncertainty target: the reported uncertainties of the three
answers propagate compatibly --- the mass and amount-of-substance
uncertainties are nonnegative, and the molecule-count deviation from
the exact Avogadro relation is bounded by the propagation budget,
$|N - N_A\, n| \le u_N + u_n\, N_A$ (the band-side reading of the
official sample $n = 3.24 \pm 0.7\ \mathrm{mmol}$,
$N = (1.95 \pm 0.05) \times 10^{21}$).  Conclusion-side.
nodes.proof_tex:
The two nonnegativity conjuncts are the measurement model\'s
nonnegativity certificates; the deviation conjunct follows from the
$n \mapsto n N_A$ propagation law, which bounds the residual by the
sum of the output uncertainty and the sensitivity times the input
uncertainty.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem uncertainty_consistency :
    0 ≤ c.uMassCA ∧
    0 ≤ c.uNumberOfMoles ∧
    |c.numberOfMolecules - c.avogadroConstant * c.numberOfMoles| ≤
      c.uNumberOfMolecules + c.uNumberOfMoles * c.avogadroConstant := by
  refine ⟨c.uMassCA_nonneg, c.uNumberOfMoles_nonneg, ?_⟩
  rw [c.number_eq]
  have hcomm : c.avogadroConstant * c.numberOfMoles =
      c.numberOfMoles * c.avogadroConstant := mul_comm _ _
  rw [hcomm, sub_self, abs_zero]
  exact add_nonneg c.uNumberOfMolecules_nonneg
    (mul_nonneg c.uNumberOfMoles_nonneg (le_of_lt c.avogadroConstant_pos))

nodes.title: Time-averaged ambient air density (Bucaramanga)
nodes.statement:
The figure readout $\rho_a = 1.12\ \mathrm{kg/m^3}$: the source notes the
ambient air density varies with local temperature and pressure and
prescribes this time-averaged value throughout Part A.  Recorded as data,
keeping its measured value.
nodes.lean_source: def ambientAirDensity : ℝ := 1.12

nodes.title: Propylene-glycol seal height
nodes.statement:
The height $h = 0.045\ \mathrm{m}$ ($4.5$ cm, Figure 18) of propylene
glycol introduced into the inner cylinder; introducing PG to this height
and closing valves D and E seals the air column CA at fixed volume,
enabling the isochoric process.
nodes.lean_source: def pgHeight : ℝ := 0.045

nodes.title: Reference absolute temperature
nodes.statement:
The reference absolute temperature $T_0 = 273.15\ \mathrm{K}$ of the
reference-constants table --- the temperature at which the reference
pressure $P_0$ of Eq. (2) is recorded.  Assumption-side equipment data;
the reciprocal $1/T_0$ enters only in conclusions.
nodes.lean_source: def referenceAbsTemperature : ℝ := 273.15

nodes.title: Real-valued absolute-temperature projection
nodes.statement:
The projection of PhysLean's typed absolute-temperature type
\texttt{Temperature} (an arbitrary-unit absolute temperature wrapping
nonnegative reals) to its real-number value; zero is absolute zero in any
such unit system.
nodes.lean_source: def absTemp : Temperature → ℝ := Temperature.toReal

nodes.title: \texttt{absTemp} agrees with the real coercion
nodes.statement:
For every absolute temperature $\mathrm{temp}$,
$\mathrm{absTemp}\ \mathrm{temp} = (\mathrm{temp} : \mathbb{R})$.
nodes.proof_tex:
Unfold the projection; both sides are the PhysLean real value of the
wrapped temperature.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem absTemp_eq_toReal (temp : Temperature) : absTemp temp = (temp : ℝ) := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Absolute temperatures are nonnegative
nodes.statement:
For every absolute temperature $\mathrm{temp}$,
$0 \le \mathrm{absTemp}\ \mathrm{temp}$.
nodes.proof_tex:
The wrapped real of a PhysLean absolute temperature is nonnegative by
construction.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem absTemp_nonneg (temp : Temperature) : 0 ≤ absTemp temp := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Ideal-gas reference coefficient
nodes.statement:
The constant-volume thermal pressure coefficient predicted by the ideal
gas law at the reference temperature: exactly $1/T_0$ (Eq. (1) makes $P$
proportional to the absolute temperature at fixed $V$ and $n$).  A named
definition only; its numeric evaluation is a separate proof obligation.
nodes.lean_source:
def idealThermalPressureCoefficient : ℝ :=
  1 / referenceAbsTemperature

nodes.title: Numerical value of the ideal coefficient
nodes.statement:
The ideal-gas reference coefficient evaluates to
$1/273.15\ \mathrm{K^{-1}}$ ($\approx 0.0037\ \mathrm{K^{-1}}$, the
recorded ideal-gas reference value).
nodes.proof_tex:
Unfold the coefficient and the recorded reference temperature
$T_0 = 273.15\ \mathrm{K}$; the equality is definitionally the identity
$1/273.15 = 1/273.15$.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem idealThermalPressureCoefficient_value :
    idealThermalPressureCoefficient = 1 / 273.15 := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Isochoric process record
nodes.statement:
An isochoric (constant-volume) process of a fixed amount of gas: an
inhabited process-time index type, the measured absolute-temperature
history $T : \mathrm{ProcessTime} \to \mathrm{Temperature}$ (the A.2
table), and the recorded absolute pressure
$P : \mathrm{ProcessTime} \to \mathbb{R}$ of the sealed column CA at each
instant.  Plain data; the physics is assigned by the law predicates below.
nodes.lean_source:
structure IsochoricProcess where
  ProcessTime : Type
  [Inhabited : Inhabited ProcessTime]
  T : ProcessTime → Temperature
  P : ProcessTime → ℝ

nodes.title: Ideal-gas law on the sealed column (Eq. (1))
nodes.statement:
The governing equation of state (Eq. (1) of the source): there are amount
$n > 0$ (mol), fixed volume $V > 0$ ($\mathrm{m^3}$, constant because PG
seals CA) and universal gas constant $R > 0$ with
$P(t)\,V = n\,R\,\mathrm{absTemp}(T(t))$ at every recorded instant.  The
constant $R$ is a free positive parameter because Part A.4 notes the
sensors may be intentionally decalibrated, shifting the expected value of
$R$ from its reference value --- no numeric $R$ is assumed anywhere.
nodes.lean_source:
structure IsIdealGasLaw (proc : IsochoricProcess) where
  n : ℝ
  V : ℝ
  R : ℝ
  hn : 0 < n
  hV : 0 < V
  hR : 0 < R
  state_eq :
    ∀ t : proc.ProcessTime,
      proc.P t * V = n * R * absTemp (proc.T t)

nodes.title: Positive pressure at positive temperature
nodes.statement:
In any ideal-gas isochoric process the recorded pressure is strictly
positive wherever the absolute temperature is strictly positive:
$0 < \mathrm{absTemp}(T(t)) \Rightarrow 0 < P(t)$.
nodes.proof_tex:
From the state equation $P(t) = n R\, \mathrm{absTemp}(T(t))/V$; the
right-hand side is a quotient of positive quantities since
$n, R, V > 0$.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem IsIdealGasLaw.pressure_pos_of_temp_pos (proc : IsochoricProcess)
    (law : IsIdealGasLaw proc) (t : proc.ProcessTime)
    (ht : 0 < absTemp (proc.T t)) :
    0 < proc.P t := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Isochoric pressure ratio equals temperature ratio
nodes.statement:
The bridge between Eq. (1) and the target coefficient: at fixed $V$ and
$n$, for any two instants with strictly positive absolute temperatures,
$P_2/P_1 = T_2/T_1$ --- Eq. (1) divided state-to-state.
nodes.proof_tex:
Write both state equations $P_i V = n R T_i$, divide, and cancel the
common positive factor $nR/V$.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem IsIdealGasLaw.pressure_ratio_eq_temp_ratio (proc : IsochoricProcess)
    (law : IsIdealGasLaw proc) (t₁ t₂ : proc.ProcessTime)
    (ht₁ : 0 < absTemp (proc.T t₁)) (ht₂ : 0 < absTemp (proc.T t₂)) :
    proc.P t₂ / proc.P t₁ = absTemp (proc.T t₂) / absTemp (proc.T t₁) := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Linear isochore (A.3 result, affine law)
nodes.statement:
The A.3 graphical result as a hypothesis interface: the recorded pressure
is affine in the absolute temperature,
$P(t) = \mathrm{offset} + \mathrm{slope}\cdot\mathrm{absTemp}(T(t))$,
with $\mathrm{slope} = \Delta P/\Delta T > 0$.  For an ideal gas at fixed
$V$ the offset vanishes; it is kept general since experimental data need
not pass exactly through the origin.  This is assumption-side
(previous-part natural-language prerequisite), not a conclusion.
nodes.lean_source:
structure IsIsochoricLinear (proc : IsochoricProcess) where
  slope : ℝ
  offset : ℝ
  slope_pos : 0 < slope
  affine :
    ∀ t : proc.ProcessTime,
      proc.P t = offset + slope * absTemp (proc.T t)

nodes.title: Slope equals the finite-difference quotient
nodes.statement:
Between any two readout instants with distinct absolute temperatures, the
isochore slope is exactly the finite-difference quotient
$\mathrm{slope} = (P(t_1) - P(t_2))/(\mathrm{absTemp}(T(t_1)) -
\mathrm{absTemp}(T(t_2)))$.
nodes.proof_tex:
Subtract the affine law at $t_2$ from the affine law at $t_1$; the offsets
cancel and division by the nonzero temperature difference isolates the
slope.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem IsIsochoricLinear.slope_eq_div (proc : IsochoricProcess)
    (lin : IsIsochoricLinear proc) (t₁ t₂ : proc.ProcessTime)
    (hT : absTemp (proc.T t₁) ≠ absTemp (proc.T t₂)) :
    lin.slope =
      (proc.P t₁ - proc.P t₂) /
        (absTemp (proc.T t₁) - absTemp (proc.T t₂)) := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Reference state $(T_0, P_0)$ with positivity certificate
nodes.statement:
The reference configuration of Eq. (2): a chosen reference instant $t_0$
whose temperature is the reference temperature $T_0$ of the reference
configuration, with the positivity certificate $hP_0 : 0 < P(t_0)$.  The
folded projections give the reference temperature
$T_0 = \mathrm{absTemp}(T(t_0))$ as a real number and the reference
pressure $P_0 = P(t_0)$ --- the pressure of the system at $T_0$.
Everything here is apparatus data; the value $1/T_0$ appears only in
later conclusions.
nodes.lean_source:
structure IsReferenceState (proc : IsochoricProcess) where
  t₀ : proc.ProcessTime
  hP₀ : 0 < proc.P t₀

def IsReferenceState.referenceTemperature (proc : IsochoricProcess)
    (ref : IsReferenceState proc) : ℝ :=
  absTemp (proc.T ref.t₀)

def IsReferenceState.referencePressure (proc : IsochoricProcess)
    (ref : IsReferenceState proc) : ℝ :=
  proc.P ref.t₀

nodes.title: Thermal pressure coefficient on the isochore (Eq. (2))
nodes.statement:
The constant-volume thermal pressure coefficient of Eq. (2),
$\beta_0 = (1/P_0)\,(\Delta P/\Delta T)$, instantiated on the A.3
isochoric line: the finite-difference quotient $\Delta P/\Delta T$ is the
slope of the isochore, so $\beta_0 = \mathrm{slope}/P_0$.  Only the
Eq.-(2) definition is recorded here; the ideal-gas value $1/T_0$ is a
conclusion-side theorem, not this definition.

nodes.title: Two-readout dataset around the reference state
nodes.statement:
The sparse A.2 dataset, parametrized by the reference pressure $P_0$, the
reference temperature $T_0$ and the coefficient $\beta_0$: temperatures
$T_1, T_2$ sampled around the reference temperature, the measured
pressures at those temperatures, the measured reference pressure, and the
readout equalities
$\mathrm{measuredPressure}\ T_1 = P_0 + \beta_0\,P_0\,(T_1 - T_0)$ and
$\mathrm{measuredPressure}\ T_2 = P_0 + \beta_0\,P_0\,(T_2 - T_0)$
recording that the readouts follow the isochoric finite-difference law, so
that $\Delta P/\Delta T = \beta_0 P_0$ on the recorded data; the measured
reference pressure is identified with $P_0$.  The non-degeneracy field
$hT12 : T_1 \ne T_2$ (added iter-007, source-warranted by the A.2
finite-difference protocol) guarantees the slope carrier is
degenerate-free: without it the instance $T_1 = T_2$ satisfies every
hypothesis of the uncertainty theorem while its conclusion fails --- see
the NOTE at the file end.
nodes.lean_source:
structure IsochoricReadout (P₀ T₀ β₀ : ℝ) where
  T₁ : ℝ
  T₂ : ℝ
  hT12 : T₁ ≠ T₂
  measuredPressure : (t : ℝ) → t = T₁ ∨ t = T₂ → ℝ
  measuredP₀ : ℝ
  measured_hP₁ : measuredPressure T₁ (Or.inl rfl) = P₀ + β₀ * P₀ * (T₁ - T₀)
  measured_hP₂ : measuredPressure T₂ (Or.inr rfl) = P₀ + β₀ * P₀ * (T₂ - T₀)
  measured_hP₀ : measuredP₀ = P₀

nodes.title: A.5 ideal value: $\beta_0 = 1/T_0$
nodes.statement:
Under the ideal-gas law (Eq. (1)) and a linear isochore, the measured
Eq.-(2) coefficient equals the ideal value $\beta_0 = 1/T_0$
(numerically $1/273.15\ \mathrm{K} = 0.0037\ \mathrm{K^{-1}}$ at
$T_0 = 273.15\ \mathrm{K}$) --- the value the official sample compares
against.  Conclusion-side.
nodes.proof_tex:
By the isochoric ratio bridge, between any two recorded states
$P_2/P_1 = T_2/T_1$; eliminating via
$\beta_0 = (1/P_0)(\Delta P/\Delta T)$ and the Eq.-(1) proportionality of
$P$ to $T$ at fixed $n, V$ collapses the finite-difference quotient to
$P_0/T_0$, hence $\beta_0 = 1/T_0$.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem beta0_close_to_ideal
    (proc : IsochoricProcess)
    (law : IsIdealGasLaw proc)
    (linear : IsIsochoricLinear proc)
    (ref : IsReferenceState proc)
    (T₀ β₀ : ℝ)
    (hT₀ : T₀ = IsReferenceState.referenceTemperature proc ref)
    (hT₀pos : 0 < T₀)
    (hβ₀ : β₀ = IsIsochoricLinear.thermalPressureCoefficient proc linear ref) :
    β₀ = 1 / T₀ := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Finite-difference consistency (Eq. (2) on A.2 data)
nodes.statement:
Between any two recorded temperatures the isochoric pressure increment
satisfies $\mathrm{slope}\cdot\Delta T = \beta_0\,P_0\,\Delta T$; with
$\beta_0 = 1/T_0$ the measured increment matches the ideal-gas increment
$P_0\,\Delta T/T_0$.  This is Eq. (2) evaluated on the A.2 data table.
Conclusion-side.
nodes.proof_tex:
Subtract the ideal increment: the measured increment equals
$\beta_0\,P_0\,\Delta T$ by the two readout equalities; divide by
$P_0\,\Delta T \neq 0$.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem beta0_eq_ideal_of_linear
    (proc : IsochoricProcess)
    (law : IsIdealGasLaw proc)
    (linear : IsIsochoricLinear proc)
    (ref : IsReferenceState proc)
    (T₀ β₀ : ℝ)
    (hT₀ : T₀ = IsReferenceState.referenceTemperature proc ref)
    (hT₀pos : 0 < T₀)
    (hβ₀ : β₀ = IsIsochoricLinear.thermalPressureCoefficient proc linear ref) :
    ∀ T₁ T₂ : ℝ,
      linear.slope * (T₂ - T₁) =
        β₀ * IsReferenceState.referencePressure proc ref * (T₂ - T₁) := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Uncertainty propagation: $|\beta_0 - 1/T_0| \le \sigma$
nodes.statement:
If the two-readout pressure increment deviates from the ideal-gas
increment $P_0\,\Delta T/T_0$ by at most $P_0\,|\Delta T|\,\sigma$
(with $\sigma > 0$), then the measured coefficient obeys the propagated
bound $|\beta_0 - 1/T_0| \le \sigma$.  This is the formal content of the
official sample $\beta_0 = 0.0034 \pm 0.0007\ \mathrm{K^{-1}}$ covering
the ideal-gas reference $0.0037\ \mathrm{K^{-1}}$:
$|0.0034 - 0.0037| = 0.0003 \le 0.0007$.  Conclusion-side.
nodes.proof_tex:
By the two readout equalities the deviation equals
$P_0\,|T_2 - T_1|\cdot|\beta_0 - 1/T_0|$ (the measured increment is
$\beta_0\,P_0\,\Delta T$, and the ideal increment is $P_0\,\Delta T/T_0$
via the finite-difference consistency).  The factor
$P_0\,|T_2 - T_1|$ is strictly positive by the reference-state
certificate $hP_0$ and the readout non-degeneracy $hT12 : T_1 \ne T_2$,
so it cancels the matching factor on the right-hand side of the deviation
bound, leaving $|\beta_0 - 1/T_0| \le \sigma$.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem beta0_uncertainty_bound
    (proc : IsochoricProcess)
    (law : IsIdealGasLaw proc)
    (linear : IsIsochoricLinear proc)
    (ref : IsReferenceState proc)
    (T₀ β₀ : ℝ)
    (hT₀ : T₀ = IsReferenceState.referenceTemperature proc ref)
    (hT₀pos : 0 < T₀)
    (hβ₀ : β₀ = IsIsochoricLinear.thermalPressureCoefficient proc linear ref)
    (readouts : IsochoricReadout
      (IsReferenceState.referencePressure proc ref) T₀ β₀)
    (σ : ℝ) (hσ : 0 < σ)
    (hdev :
      |(readouts.measuredPressure readouts.T₂ (Or.inr rfl)) -
          (readouts.measuredPressure readouts.T₁ (Or.inl rfl)) -
        IsReferenceState.referencePressure proc ref *
          (readouts.T₂ - readouts.T₁) / T₀|
        ≤ IsReferenceState.referencePressure proc ref *
            |readouts.T₂ - readouts.T₁| * σ) :
    |β₀ - 1 / T₀| ≤ σ := by
  sorry

nodes.title: A.5 main target: value, consistency, and uncertainty
nodes.statement:
The A.5 target conjunction for a process with reference state
$(T_0, P_0)$, $T_0 > 0$, a non-degenerate temperature history, and a
two-readout dataset: (1) $\beta_0 = 1/T_0$, the ideal-gas prediction,
numerically $1/273.15\ \mathrm{K} = 0.0037\ \mathrm{K^{-1}}$ at
$T_0 = 273.15\ \mathrm{K}$; (2) the finite-difference bridge
$\mathrm{slope}\cdot\Delta T = \beta_0\,P_0\,\Delta T$ between any two
recorded temperatures; (3) the uncertainty bound
$|\beta_0 - 1/T_0| \le \sigma$ whenever the readout deviation is
$\le P_0\,|\Delta T|\,\sigma$.  The official sample band
$0.0034 \pm 0.0007\ \mathrm{K^{-1}}$ is the A.5-band-side reading of (3):
the reported band covers the ideal reference since
$|0.0034 - 0.0037| = 0.0003 \le 0.0007$.  All numeric answer values
appear only here, in conclusions.
nodes.proof_tex:
Conjoin the three component theorems:
\cref{thm:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_4_A_5:beta0_close_to_ideal},
\cref{thm:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_4_A_5:beta0_eq_ideal_of_linear},
and
\cref{thm:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_4_A_5:beta0_uncertainty_bound}
--- each is available under the packaged hypotheses by verbatim
transcription (the formal proof is the prover stage's remaining
obligation).
nodes.lean_source:
theorem main
    (proc : IsochoricProcess)
    (law : IsIdealGasLaw proc)
    (linear : IsIsochoricLinear proc)
    (ref : IsReferenceState proc)
    (T₀ β₀ : ℝ)
    (hT₀ : T₀ = IsReferenceState.referenceTemperature proc ref)
    (hT₀pos : 0 < T₀)
    (hvar : ∃ t₁ t₂ : proc.ProcessTime,
      absTemp (proc.T t₁) ≠ absTemp (proc.T t₂))
    (hβ₀ : β₀ = IsIsochoricLinear.thermalPressureCoefficient proc linear ref)
    (readouts : IsochoricReadout
      (IsReferenceState.referencePressure proc ref) T₀ β₀) :
    (β₀ = 1 / T₀)
      ∧ (∀ T₁ T₂ : ℝ,
          linear.slope * (T₂ - T₁) =
            β₀ * IsReferenceState.referencePressure proc ref * (T₂ - T₁))
      ∧ (∀ σ : ℝ, 0 < σ →
          |(readouts.measuredPressure readouts.T₂ (Or.inr rfl)) -
              (readouts.measuredPressure readouts.T₁ (Or.inl rfl)) -
            IsReferenceState.referencePressure proc ref *
              (readouts.T₂ - readouts.T₁) / T₀|
            ≤ IsReferenceState.referencePressure proc ref *
                |readouts.T₂ - readouts.T₁| * σ →
          |β₀ - 1 / T₀| ≤ σ) := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Physics formalization target
nodes.statement: The assigned autoformalize agent should translate this physics problem into Lean declarations in the covered file, with theorem and lemma proof bodies written as `by sorry`.
nodes.proof_tex: This is an autoformalization task, not a proof task. Produce faithful statements that can later be proved without weakening the source contract.

nodes.title: Gas column geometry
nodes.statement:
The geometry of the gas column trapped in the inner cylinder (Figure 19):
a uniform cross-sectional area $A$ (in $\mathrm{m}^2$) together with a
positivity certificate $0 < A$, so that the recorded water-level height
$H$ determines the headspace volume.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure GasColumnGeometry where
  crossSectionalArea : ℝ
  area_pos : 0 < crossSectionalArea

nodes.title: Trapped gas volume
nodes.statement:
The headspace volume of the trapped gas at recorded water-level height
$H$: $\mathit{gasVolume}\,H = A \cdot H$.  Defined for arbitrary real
$H$; the physical law fields restrict it to positive heights, so $H$
plays the role of volume per unit cross-sectional area in the gas laws.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
def gasVolume (G : GasColumnGeometry) (H : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  G.crossSectionalArea * H

nodes.title: B.4 physical data
nodes.statement:
The full physical data package of subquestion B.4: the gas-column
geometry; the constant total pressure $P_{atm} > 0$ held fixed by the
syringe; the gas constant $R > 0$; the fixed dry-air content
$n_{\mathrm{air}} > 0$ of the sealed headspace; the reference temperature
$T_0$ fixed at the $0\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ reference of the exam and the
extrapolated height $H_0 > 0$ at $T_0$ (B.3 result); the dry-air partial
pressure $p_{\mathrm{air}}(T',H')$, vapor pressure $P_v(T',H')$, and
vapor molar content $n_{\mathrm{vap}}(T',H')$ at each admitted state,
with $n_{\mathrm{vap}} \ge 0$.  Its law fields are Dalton's law with the
syringe arrangement, $p_{\mathrm{air}}(T',H') + P_v(T',H') = P_{atm}$ at
every admitted state; the B.4 hypothesis $P_v(T_0, H_0) = 0$; and the
ideal-gas law for each trapped component,
$p_{\mathrm{air}}\,(A H') = n_{\mathrm{air}} R T'$ and
$P_v\,(A H') = n_{\mathrm{vap}} R T'$.  Assumption side: the B.4 answer
appears nowhere among its fields.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure VaporPressureB4Data where

  geometry : GasColumnGeometry

  P_atm : ℝ
  P_atm_pos : 0 < P_atm

  R : ℝ
  R_pos : 0 < R

  dryAirMoles : ℝ
  dryAirMoles_pos : 0 < dryAirMoles

  T₀ : ℝ
  T₀_val : T₀ = 273.15

  H₀ : ℝ
  H₀_pos : 0 < H₀

  dryAirPartialPressure : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ

  vaporMoles : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ

  vaporPressure : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ

  vaporMoles_nonneg :
    ∀ {T' H' : ℝ}, 0 < T' → 0 < H' → 0 ≤ vaporMoles T' H'

  total_pressure_eq_atm :
    ∀ {T' H' : ℝ}, 0 < T' → 0 < H' →
      dryAirPartialPressure T' H' + vaporPressure T' H' = P_atm

  vaporPressure_zero_at_T₀ : vaporPressure T₀ H₀ = 0

  idealGas :
    ∀ {T' H' : ℝ}, 0 < T' → 0 < H' →
      dryAirPartialPressure T' H' * gasVolume geometry H' = dryAirMoles * R * T' ∧
      vaporPressure T' H' * gasVolume geometry H' = vaporMoles T' H' * R * T'

nodes.title: Admissible measured state and reference state
nodes.statement:
An admissible measured state of the B.4 data table: a pair $(T, H)$ of an
absolute-temperature readout and the recorded water-level height at that
temperature, both carrying positivity certificates $0 < T$ and $0 < H$.
The reference state $(T_0, H_0)$ is admitted: its positivity facts come
from the fixed reference-temperature value and the certificate
$0 < H_0$.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure MeasuredState (D : VaporPressureB4Data) where
  T : ℝ
  T_pos : 0 < T
  H : ℝ
  H_pos : 0 < H

def referenceState (D : VaporPressureB4Data) : D.MeasuredState where
  T := D.T₀
  T_pos := D.T₀_val ▸ (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) < 273.15)
  H := D.H₀
  H_pos := D.H₀_pos

nodes.title: Clausius--Clapeyron vapor-pressure relation
nodes.statement:
The Clausius--Clapeyron relation, Eq.\ (3) of the exam, as a predicate on
a vapor-pressure curve $P_v$: at every absolute temperature $T > 0$,
$P_v(T) = P_{v0}\,\exp\bigl(-(Q_v/R)\,(1/T - 1/T_0)\bigr)$, with $Q_v$
the molar latent heat of vaporization and $P_{v0}$ the vapor pressure at
the reference temperature $T_0$.  Context for B.4 (it drives parts
B.5/B.6); it is \emph{not} a hypothesis of the B.4 target, which needs
only the vanishing of the vapor pressure at $T_0$.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.

nodes.title: Dry air carries the whole pressure at the reference state
nodes.statement:
At the reference state $(T_0, H_0)$, with $0 < T_0$, the dry-air partial
pressure equals the full total pressure:
$p_{\mathrm{air}}(T_0, H_0) = P_{atm}$.
nodes.proof_tex:
Dalton's law at $(T_0, H_0)$ gives
$p_{\mathrm{air}}(T_0, H_0) + P_v(T_0, H_0) = P_{atm}$, and the B.4
hypothesis $P_v(T_0, H_0) = 0$ collapses the sum.
nodes.lean_source:
lemma dryAirPartialPressure_at_T₀ (D : VaporPressureB4Data) (hT₀ : 0 < D.T₀) :
    D.dryAirPartialPressure D.T₀ D.H₀ = D.P_atm := by
  have h := D.total_pressure_eq_atm hT₀ D.H₀_pos
  rw [D.vaporPressure_zero_at_T₀, add_zero] at h
  exact h

nodes.title: Combined gas-law form at an admitted state
nodes.statement:
At every admitted state $(T', H')$ with $0 < T'$ and $0 < H'$, the total
pressure times the headspace volume equals the total trapped molar
content times $R T'$:
$P_{atm}\,(A H') = \bigl(n_{\mathrm{air}} + n_{\mathrm{vap}}(T',H')\bigr)\, R\, T'$.
nodes.proof_tex:
Rewrite $P_{atm}$ via Dalton's law, distribute the volume over the two
component pressures, replace each component term by its ideal-gas-law
right-hand side, and regroup.
nodes.lean_source:
lemma total_pressure_mul_volume (D : VaporPressureB4Data)
    {T' H' : ℝ} (hT : 0 < T') (hH : 0 < H') :
    D.P_atm * gasVolume D.geometry H' =
      (D.dryAirMoles + D.vaporMoles T' H') * D.R * T' := by
  have htot := D.total_pressure_eq_atm hT hH
  have hgas := D.idealGas hT hH
  calc D.P_atm * gasVolume D.geometry H'
      = (D.dryAirPartialPressure T' H' + D.vaporPressure T' H') *
          gasVolume D.geometry H' := by rw [htot]
    _ = D.dryAirPartialPressure T' H' * gasVolume D.geometry H' +
          D.vaporPressure T' H' * gasVolume D.geometry H' := by ring
    _ = D.dryAirMoles * D.R * T' + D.vaporMoles T' H' * D.R * T' := by
        rw [hgas.1, hgas.2]
    _ = (D.dryAirMoles + D.vaporMoles T' H') * D.R * T' := by ring

nodes.title: Zero reference value forces identically zero vapor pressure
nodes.statement:
Consistency checkpoint between Eq.\ (3) and the B.4 zero hypothesis:
under the Clausius--Clapeyron context at reference value $P_{v0}$ for the
curve $T \mapsto P_v(T, H_0)$, if $P_{v0} = 0$ then the vapor pressure
vanishes at every temperature $T > 0$.  Context lemma for B.5/B.6; not
used by the B.4 target.
nodes.proof_tex:
Instantiate the Clausius--Clapeyron relation at $T$ and substitute
$P_{v0} = 0$, making the right-hand side zero.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem eq_zero_of_clausiusClapeyron_zero (D : VaporPressureB4Data)
    (Q_v P_v0 : ℝ)
    (hCC : ClausiusClapeyron D.R Q_v D.T₀ P_v0 (fun T => D.vaporPressure T D.H₀))
    (hP_v0 : P_v0 = 0)
    {T : ℝ} (hT : 0 < T) :
    D.vaporPressure T D.H₀ = 0 := by
  have h := hCC T hT
  rw [hP_v0, zero_mul] at h
  exact h

nodes.title: B.4 vapor-pressure readout formula
nodes.statement:
At every admissible measured state $(T, H)$ of the trapped dry air plus
water vapor mixture, the vapor pressure is the recorded B.4 answer
\[ P_v \;=\; P_{atm}\Bigl(1 - \frac{H_0\,T}{H\,T_0}\Bigr). \]
The Clausius--Clapeyron relation is \emph{not} assumed: B.4 uses only
Dalton's law at constant total pressure, the ideal-gas law for the fixed
dry-air content, and the vanishing of the vapor pressure at $T_0$.  The
official formula lives only here and in
\cref{thm:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_4_B_4:target}, on the
conclusion side.
nodes.proof_tex:
Apply the combined gas law at $(T, H)$ and at the reference state
$(T_0, H_0)$, where the dry air alone carries $P_{atm}$
(\cref{lem:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_4_B_4:dryAirPartialPressure_at_T0}),
so the dry-air ideal-gas law gives
$P_{atm} A H_0 = n_{\mathrm{air}} R T_0$.  Eliminating the fixed dry-air
content $n_{\mathrm{air}}$ between this reference balance and the state
balance yields $p_{\mathrm{air}}(T,H)\,H T_0 = P_{atm} H_0 T$, and
subtracting from $P_{atm}$ via Dalton's law gives the claimed closed
form; the contracted sorried proof body is left to the prover stage.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem vaporPressure_eq (D : VaporPressureB4Data) (s : D.MeasuredState) :
    D.vaporPressure s.T s.H =
      D.P_atm * (1 - (D.H₀ * s.T) / (s.H * D.T₀)) := by
  sorry

nodes.title: B.4 target relation
nodes.statement:
The B.4 target relation at an arbitrary admissible measured state
$(T, H)$, matching the recorded official answer:
$P_v = P_{atm}\,\bigl(1 - (H_0 T)/(H T_0)\bigr)$.
This is the exact statement the umbrella autoformalization entry
\cref{thm:physics:IPhO_2026_4_B_4:target} points at.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem target (D : VaporPressureB4Data) (s : D.MeasuredState) :
    D.vaporPressure s.T s.H =
      D.P_atm * (1 - (D.H₀ * s.T) / (s.H * D.T₀)) := by
  sorry
