nodes.title: Dimensional length and pressure aliases
nodes.statement:
The water-level heights $H_0, H$ carry PhysLean's dimensional length type
(dimension $L$), and the pressures $P_{\mathrm{atm}}, P_v$ carry PhysLean's
dimensional pressure type (dimension $M L^{-1} T^{-2}$); the
\texttt{InnerCylinderExperiment} structure packages the apparatus readouts of
the B-parts ($P_{\mathrm{atm}}$, the vapor-pressure function $P_v(T)$, the
reference temperature $T_0 = 273.15$ K with its real-valued readout, the
extrapolated height $H_0$, and the vanishing-extrapolation anchor) on these
typed habitats.
nodes.lean_source:
abbrev DimLength : Type := Dimensionful (WithDim L𝓭 ℝ)

abbrev Pressure : Type := DimPressure

structure InnerCylinderExperiment where

  P_atm : Pressure

  P_v : Temperature → Pressure

  T₀ : Temperature

  H₀ : DimLength

  T₀_value_K : ℝ

  vapor_pressure_taken_zero_at_T₀ : Prop

  T₀_value_K_eq : T₀_value_K = 273.15

nodes.title: Abstract molar and specific wrappers
nodes.statement:
PhysLean has no amount-of-substance dimension, so the molar latent heat
$Q_v$ (J/mol), the gas constant $R$ (J/(mol$\cdot$K)), the molar mass of
water $M_0$ (kg/mol) and the specific latent heat $L_v$ (J/kg) are carried
by smallest faithful local wrappers, deliberately opaque (no field
projection) so that conversion and uncertainty relations cannot be
discharged by unfolding.
nodes.lean_source:
structure MolarEnergy where
  deriving Nonempty

opaque catalogMolarLatentHeatQv : MolarEnergy

opaque catalogGasConstantR : MolarEnergy

structure MolarHeatCapacity where
  deriving Nonempty

structure MolarMass where
  deriving Nonempty

structure SpecificLatentHeat where
  deriving Nonempty

opaque catalogMolarMassWaterM0 : MolarMass

opaque catalogGasConstantRMolarHeatCapacity : MolarHeatCapacity

nodes.title: Catalog opaque constants
nodes.statement:
Catalog-level named inhabitants of the abstract wrappers: the B.5 central
molar latent heat $Q_v = 39 \pm 2$ kJ/mol, the gas constant in both
molar-energy and molar-heat-capacity form
($R = 8.314$ J/(mol$\cdot$K)), and the molar mass of water
$M_0 = 18.0 \times 10^{-3}$ kg/mol.

nodes.title: Integrated Clausius--Clapeyron law
nodes.statement:
The physical law itself: for every pair of absolute temperatures,
$\ln(P_v(T)/P_v(T_0)) = -(Q_v/R)\,(1/T - 1/T_0)$, expressed between the
scalar readouts $\mathrm{lnRatio}$ and $\mathrm{invTdiff}$ with slope carrier
$Q_v/R > 0$; \texttt{IsClausiusClapeyronSlope} records the B.5 extraction
that the slope $s$ of the $\ln(P_v/P_{\mathrm{atm}})$ vs $1/T$ graph equals
$-Q_v/R$.
nodes.lean_source:
def SatisfiesClausiusClapeyron
    (lnRatio invTdiff : Temperature → Temperature → ℝ)
    (QvOverR_K : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ T T₀ : Temperature, lnRatio T T₀ = -QvOverR_K * invTdiff T T₀

def IsClausiusClapeyronSlope
    (lnRatio invTdiff : Temperature → Temperature → ℝ)
    (QvOverR_K slope_K : ℝ) : Prop :=
  SatisfiesClausiusClapeyron lnRatio invTdiff QvOverR_K ∧
    slope_K = -QvOverR_K

nodes.title: Part-B.5 measurements and B.6 input package
nodes.statement:
The natural-language previous-part prerequisite in Lean form: the measured
slope $-4700 \pm 200$ K of the Clausius--Clapeyron graph, the resulting
$Q_v = 39 \pm 2$ kJ/mol, and the problem-stated $R = 8.31$ J/(mol$\cdot$K),
with official sample values recorded as field equations;
\texttt{PartB6Input} is the conjunction of the apparatus record and the
B.5 measurements, containing no field committal to the B.6 formula
$L_v = Q_v/M_0$.
nodes.lean_source:
structure PartB5Measurements where

  slope_K : ℝ

  slope_uncertainty_K : ℝ

  Qv_kJ_per_mol : ℝ

  Qv_uncertainty_kJ_per_mol : ℝ

  R_J_per_mol_K : ℝ

  slope_K_eq : slope_K = -4700

  slope_uncertainty_K_eq : slope_uncertainty_K = 200

  Qv_kJ_per_mol_eq : Qv_kJ_per_mol = 39

  Qv_uncertainty_kJ_per_mol_eq : Qv_uncertainty_kJ_per_mol = 2

  R_J_per_mol_K_eq : R_J_per_mol_K = 8.31

structure PartB6Input extends InnerCylinderExperiment, PartB5Measurements

nodes.title: Molar-to-specific conversion relation
nodes.statement:
The unit-carrying conversion at the heart of B.6: a witness carrying the
magnitudes of $Q_v$ (kJ/mol), $M_0$ (kg/mol) and $L_v$ (kJ/kg) together
with the physical conversion equation
$L_v = Q_{v\mathrm{mag}} / M_{0\mathrm{mag}}$ and the positivity of
$M_0$; \texttt{ConvertsMolarLatentHeatToSpecific} names its nonemptiness as
a proposition. The relation is hypothesis material for the prover, never a
definition making the target true by unfolding.
nodes.lean_source:
structure IsSpecificLatentHeatOf
    (Lv : SpecificLatentHeat) (Qv : MolarEnergy) (M0 : MolarMass) where

  Qv_magnitude_kJ_per_mol : ℝ

  M0_magnitude_kg_per_mol : ℝ

  Lv_magnitude_kJ_per_kg : ℝ

  conversion_eq :
    Lv_magnitude_kJ_per_kg =
      Qv_magnitude_kJ_per_mol / M0_magnitude_kg_per_mol

  M0_pos : 0 < M0_magnitude_kg_per_mol

def ConvertsMolarLatentHeatToSpecific
    (Lv : SpecificLatentHeat) (Qv : MolarEnergy) (M0 : MolarMass) : Prop :=
  Nonempty (IsSpecificLatentHeatOf Lv Qv M0)

nodes.title: Official-answer value record
nodes.statement:
The scalar, unit-tagged record of the official result
$L_v = 2190 \pm 110$ kJ/kg (central value and absolute uncertainty), the
uncertainty-band relation $|measured - 2190| \le 110$ (kJ/kg), and the
catalog scalars $Q_v = 39$ kJ/mol, $M_0 = 18.0 \times 10^{-3}$ kg/mol,
$\Delta Q_v = 2$ kJ/mol.
nodes.lean_source:
structure SpecificLatentHeatValue where

  central_kJ_per_kg : ℝ

  uncertainty_kJ_per_kg : ℝ

def SpecificLatentHeatValue.withinUncertainty
    (measured official : SpecificLatentHeatValue) : Prop :=
  |measured.central_kJ_per_kg - official.central_kJ_per_kg| ≤
    official.uncertainty_kJ_per_kg

def officialSpecificLatentHeatValue : SpecificLatentHeatValue where
  central_kJ_per_kg := 2190
  uncertainty_kJ_per_kg := 110

def catalogQvValue : ℝ := 39

def catalogMolarMassWaterValue : ℝ := 18.0e-3

def catalogQvUncertainty : ℝ := 2

nodes.title: B.6 main target: conversion with official consistency
nodes.statement:
Under the B.6 input package there exists a conversion witness
$L_v = Q_v/M_0$ whose magnitudes match the catalog central values
($39$ kJ/mol, $18.0 \times 10^{-3}$ kg/mol), and the reported specific
latent heat lies within the official uncertainty interval
$2190 \pm 110$ kJ/kg.
nodes.proof_tex:
Take the catalog magnitudes as the witness components; the conversion
equation holds by the scalar division $39/(18.0\mathrm{e}{-3})$ and the
band membership follows from
$|39/(18.0\mathrm{e}{-3}) - 2190| \approx 23.3 \le 110$; the existential
packaging is left to the prover stage.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem latent_heat_per_unit_mass_target
    (input : PartB6Input)
    (Qv : MolarEnergy) (M0 : MolarMass) (Lv : SpecificLatentHeat)
    (Lv_reported : SpecificLatentHeatValue) :
    ∃ witness : IsSpecificLatentHeatOf Lv Qv M0,
      witness.Qv_magnitude_kJ_per_mol = catalogQvValue ∧
      witness.M0_magnitude_kg_per_mol = catalogMolarMassWaterValue ∧
      Lv_reported.withinUncertainty officialSpecificLatentHeatValue := by
  sorry

nodes.title: B.6 formula, explicit scalar form
nodes.statement:
For the catalog central values,
$L_v = Q_v/M_0 = 39/(18.0 \times 10^{-3}) \approx 2190$ kJ/kg, within the
official $\pm 110$ kJ/kg.
nodes.proof_tex:
Pure scalar arithmetic: $39/(18.0\mathrm{e}{-3}) = 2166.\overline{6}$ and
$|2166.\overline{6} - 2190| = 23.\overline{3} \le 110$.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem latent_heat_per_unit_mass_formula :
    ∃ Lv Qv M0 : ℝ,
      Qv = catalogQvValue ∧
      M0 = catalogMolarMassWaterValue ∧
      Lv = Qv / M0 ∧
      |Lv - officialSpecificLatentHeatValue.central_kJ_per_kg| ≤
        officialSpecificLatentHeatValue.uncertainty_kJ_per_kg := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Computed value within official uncertainty
nodes.statement:
The computed central value $L_v = 39/(18.0 \times 10^{-3}) \approx 2167$
kJ/kg lies within the official interval $2190 \pm 110$ kJ/kg.
nodes.proof_tex:
Same scalar evaluation:
$|2166.\overline{6} - 2190| = 23.\overline{3} \le 110$.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem computed_value_within_official_uncertainty :
    |(catalogQvValue / catalogMolarMassWaterValue) -
        officialSpecificLatentHeatValue.central_kJ_per_kg| ≤
      officialSpecificLatentHeatValue.uncertainty_kJ_per_kg := by
  sorry

nodes.title: B.5 bridge: $Q_v$ from the Clausius--Clapeyron slope
nodes.statement:
The B.5 slope $s = -4700 \pm 200$ K with $R = 8.31$ J/(mol$\cdot$K) fixes
the molar latent heat at $Q_v = -s \cdot R \approx 39.1$ kJ/mol, consistent
with the official $Q_v = 39 \pm 2$ kJ/mol:
$Q_v = -\mathtt{slope\_K}\cdot\mathtt{R}/1000$ and
$|Q_v^{\mathrm{computed}} - Q_v^{\mathrm{input}}| \le \Delta Q_v$.
nodes.proof_tex:
Substitute the recorded field equations: $-(-4700)\cdot 8.31/1000 = 39.057$
kJ/mol and $|39.057 - 39| = 0.057 \le 2$.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem qv_from_clausius_clapeyron_slope
    (input : PartB6Input) :
    ∃ Qv_computed_kJ_per_mol : ℝ,
      Qv_computed_kJ_per_mol = -input.slope_K * input.R_J_per_mol_K / 1000 ∧
      |Qv_computed_kJ_per_mol - input.Qv_kJ_per_mol| ≤
        input.Qv_uncertainty_kJ_per_mol := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Reference-temperature calibration
nodes.statement:
The reference temperature readout of the setup is
$T_0 = 273.15$ K, captured for the formalization even though B.6 does not
use it directly.
nodes.proof_tex:
Immediate from the recorded field equation
\texttt{T\_0\_value\_K\_eq}.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem reference_temperature_calibration
    (input : PartB6Input) :
    input.T₀_value_K = 273.15 := by
  sorry

nodes.title: SI-valued quantity
nodes.statement:
A physical quantity carrying PhysLean dimension $d$, accessed through its
SI-unit representative (metre, second, kilogram, coulomb, kelvin): a record
whose single field \texttt{valSI} is the \texttt{WithDim d $\mathbb{R}$}
value of the quantity in SI units.
nodes.lean_source:
structure SIQuantity (d : Dimension) where

  valSI : WithDim d ℝ

nodes.title: Coherence of the SI liftings
nodes.statement:
Multiplication and division of dimension-carrying quantities lift to
\texttt{SIQuantity} (instances
,
),
and the SI value of a product/quotient is the product/quotient of the SI
values (,
); the dimension cast
 along $d_1 = d_2$ preserves the
SI value ().
nodes.lean_name: IPhO2026_4_C_6.SIQuantity.valSI_mul, IPhO2026_4_C_6.SIQuantity.valSI_div, IPhO2026_4_C_6.SIQuantity.castTo_valSI, IPhO2026_4_C_6.instHMul, IPhO2026_4_C_6.instHDiv, IPhO2026_4_C_6.SIQuantity.valSI_mul, IPhO2026_4_C_6.SIQuantity.valSI_div, IPhO2026_4_C_6.SIQuantity.castTo, IPhO2026_4_C_6.SIQuantity.castTo_valSI
nodes.proof_tex:
Each is a definitional equality (\texttt{rfl}): SI is coherent, and
\texttt{castTo} is PhysLean \texttt{WithDim.cast} lifted to the record.
nodes.lean_source:
@[simp]
lemma valSI_mul (q1 : SIQuantity d1) (q2 : SIQuantity d2) :
    (q1 * q2).valSI = q1.valSI * q2.valSI := rfl

@[simp]
lemma valSI_div (q1 : SIQuantity d1) (q2 : SIQuantity d2) :
    (q1 / q2).valSI = q1.valSI / q2.valSI := rfl

@[simp]
lemma castTo_valSI {d₁ d₂ : Dimension} (q : SIQuantity d₁) (h : d₁ = d₂) :
    (q.castTo h).valSI.val = q.valSI.val := rfl

@[simp]
lemma valSI_mul (q1 : SIQuantity d1) (q2 : SIQuantity d2) :
    (q1 * q2).valSI = q1.valSI * q2.valSI := rfl

@[simp]
lemma valSI_div (q1 : SIQuantity d1) (q2 : SIQuantity d2) :
    (q1 / q2).valSI = q1.valSI / q2.valSI := rfl

def castTo {d₁ d₂ : Dimension} (q : SIQuantity d₁) (h : d₁ = d₂) : SIQuantity d₂ :=
  ⟨WithDim.cast q.valSI h⟩

@[simp]
lemma castTo_valSI {d₁ d₂ : Dimension} (q : SIQuantity d₁) (h : d₁ = d₂) :
    (q.castTo h).valSI.val = q.valSI.val := rfl

nodes.title: Named dimension aliases
nodes.statement:
The dimension families of the problem, as \texttt{SIQuantity} aliases:
water mass  ($\mathsf{M}$),
specific heat 
($\mathsf{L}^2\mathsf{T}^{-2}\Theta^{-1}$, i.e.\ J/(kg\cdot K)),
wall thermal resistance 
($\Theta\,\mathsf{T}^3\mathsf{L}^{-2}\mathsf{M}^{-1}$, i.e.\ K/W),
C.5-graph slope  ($\mathsf{T}^{-1}$),
temperature difference  ($\Theta$),
heat current 
($\mathsf{M}\mathsf{L}^2\mathsf{T}^{-3}$, i.e.\ watt).
nodes.lean_name: IPhO2026_4_C_6.DimMassQ, IPhO2026_4_C_6.DimMassQ, IPhO2026_4_C_6.DimSpecificHeat, IPhO2026_4_C_6.DimThermalResistance, IPhO2026_4_C_6.DimC5Slope, IPhO2026_4_C_6.DimTempDiffQ, IPhO2026_4_C_6.DimWattQ
nodes.lean_source:
abbrev DimMassQ : Type := SIQuantity M𝓭

abbrev DimMassQ : Type := SIQuantity M𝓭

abbrev DimSpecificHeat : Type := SIQuantity (L𝓭 * L𝓭 * T𝓭⁻¹ * T𝓭⁻¹ * Θ𝓭⁻¹)

abbrev DimThermalResistance : Type := SIQuantity (Θ𝓭 * T𝓭 ^ 3 * L𝓭⁻¹ * L𝓭⁻¹ * M𝓭⁻¹)

abbrev DimC5Slope : Type := SIQuantity T𝓭⁻¹

abbrev DimTempDiffQ : Type := SIQuantity Θ𝓭

abbrev DimWattQ : Type := SIQuantity (M𝓭 * L𝓭 * L𝓭 * T𝓭⁻¹ * T𝓭⁻¹ * T𝓭⁻¹)

nodes.title: Strict band and measured value
nodes.statement:
\texttt{StrictBand lo hi v} locates a value $v$ in the band
$lo < v \le hi$ (one-sided at the upper edge);
 $\;v$ certifies that the physical value
lies in the open band $(v - \delta, v + \delta)$ around the central readout
$v$, with the propagated uncertainty half-width $\delta > 0$ part of the
contract.
nodes.lean_source:
structure StrictBand (lo hi : ℝ) (v : ℝ) : Prop where

  lower : lo < v

  upper : v ≤ hi

structure MeasuredValue (v : ℝ) where

  uncertainty : ℝ

  uncertainty_pos : 0 < uncertainty

  in_band : StrictBand (v - uncertainty) (v + uncertainty) v

nodes.title: Temperature-difference and rate quantities
nodes.statement:
The dimension-carrying constructs on the temperature record:
 (a temperature difference in kelvin, on the
real readouts of PhysLean \texttt{Temperature}),
 (the time derivative of the
inner-cylinder temperature, K/s),
 (the finite-difference rate
$(T_{IC}(t_1) - T_{IC}(t_0))/(t_1 - t_0)$ of Equation 5, K/s).
nodes.lean_source:
noncomputable def tempDiffSI (T₁ T₂ : Temperature) : WithDim Θ𝓭 ℝ :=
  ⟨(T₁.toReal - T₂.toReal)⟩

noncomputable def tempDiffSI (T₁ T₂ : Temperature) : WithDim Θ𝓭 ℝ :=
  ⟨(T₁.toReal - T₂.toReal)⟩

noncomputable def coolingRateSI (TIC : Time → Temperature) (t : Time) :
    WithDim (Θ𝓭 * T𝓭⁻¹) ℝ :=
  ⟨deriv (fun s : ℝ => (TIC (⟨s⟩ : Time)).toReal) t.val⟩

noncomputable def finiteDiffRateSI (TIC : Time → Temperature) (t₀ t₁ : Time) :
    WithDim (Θ𝓭 * T𝓭⁻¹) ℝ :=
  (⟨(TIC t₁).toReal - (TIC t₀).toReal⟩ : WithDim Θ𝓭 ℝ) / (⟨t₁.val - t₀.val⟩ : WithDim T𝓭 ℝ)

nodes.title: Inner heat capacity and wall drive
nodes.statement:
is the heat capacity $c_0\,m$ of
the inner-cylinder water in J/K (dimension
$\mathsf{M}\mathsf{L}^2\mathsf{T}^{-2}\Theta^{-1}$, via a dimension cast
proved by the file-local \texttt{dim\_component} macro);
 is the thermal drive $\Delta T / R_{Th}$ of
the wall as a heat current in watts (the formal identification
$\Theta\cdot(\Theta\mathsf{T}^3\mathsf{L}^{-2}\mathsf{M}^{-1})^{-1} = \mathsf{M}\mathsf{L}^2\mathsf{T}^{-3}$).
nodes.lean_source:
noncomputable def innerHeatCapacitySI (c₀ : DimSpecificHeat) (m : DimMassQ) :
    SIQuantity (M𝓭 * L𝓭 * L𝓭 * T𝓭⁻¹ * T𝓭⁻¹ * Θ𝓭⁻¹) :=
  (c₀ * m).castTo (by ext <;> dim_component)

noncomputable def innerHeatCapacitySI (c₀ : DimSpecificHeat) (m : DimMassQ) :
    SIQuantity (M𝓭 * L𝓭 * L𝓭 * T𝓭⁻¹ * T𝓭⁻¹ * Θ𝓭⁻¹) :=
  (c₀ * m).castTo (by ext <;> dim_component)

noncomputable def driveSI (R : WithDim Θ𝓭 ℝ) (RTh : DimThermalResistance) : DimWattQ :=
  (({ valSI := R } : DimTempDiffQ) / RTh).castTo (by ext <;> dim_component)

nodes.title: Cooling model (Eq.\ 4 + energy conservation)
nodes.statement:
With the apparatus heat capacity ignored, the heat flowing through the wall
per unit time is absorbed by the inner water:
$c_0\,m\,\mathrm{d}T_{IC}/\mathrm{d}t = (T_{OC} - T_{IC})/R_{Th}$ for all
$t$, stated on SI values. A governing law of the problem (assumption side);
the C.6 target is not part of it.
nodes.lean_source:
def CoolingModel (c₀ : DimSpecificHeat) (m : DimMassQ) (RTh : DimThermalResistance)
    (TOC TIC : Time → Temperature) : Prop :=
  ∀ t : Time,
    (innerHeatCapacitySI c₀ m * (SIQuantity.mk (coolingRateSI TIC t))).valSI.val =
      (driveSI (tempDiffSI (TOC t) (TIC t)) RTh).valSI.val

nodes.title: Finite-difference model (Eq.\ 5)
nodes.statement:
On every measurement interval $[t_0, t_1]$ with $t_0 \ne t_1$, the
finite-difference rate $(T_{IC}(t_1) - T_{IC}(t_0))/(t_1 - t_0)$ tracks the
model rate $\overline{\Delta T}/(R_{Th}\,c_0\,m)$, where
$\overline{\Delta T} = \bar T_{OC} - \bar T_{IC}$ is the interval-averaged
temperature difference (Equation 5 of the source).
nodes.lean_source:
def FiniteDifferenceModel (c₀ : DimSpecificHeat) (m : DimMassQ)
    (RTh : DimThermalResistance) (TIC : Time → Temperature)
    (ΔTavg : Time → Time → WithDim Θ𝓭 ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ t₀ t₁ : Time, t₀ ≠ t₁ →
    (innerHeatCapacitySI c₀ m * (SIQuantity.mk (finiteDiffRateSI TIC t₀ t₁))).valSI.val =
      (driveSI (ΔTavg t₀ t₁) RTh).valSI.val

nodes.title: Fourier radial-conduction law (Eq.\ 6)
nodes.statement:
The conductive heat current through the wall satisfies
$\mathrm{d}Q/\mathrm{d}t = -\lambda\,A\,\mathrm{d}T/\mathrm{d}r$ AND equals
the lumped wall drive $(T_{OC} - T_{IC})/R_{Th}$ — the conjunction that
makes $R_{Th}$ the \emph{effective} wall resistance determined by the wall
material ($\lambda$, acrylic) and geometry (Figure 17 dimensions).
nodes.lean_source:
def FourierRadialConductionLaw
    (heatCurrent : ℝ) (lambda : SIQuantity (M𝓭 * L𝓭 * T𝓭⁻¹ * T𝓭⁻¹ * T𝓭⁻¹ * Θ𝓭⁻¹))
    (wallArea : SIQuantity (L𝓭 * L𝓭)) (radialTempGradient : SIQuantity (Θ𝓭 * L𝓭⁻¹))
    (ΔT : WithDim Θ𝓭 ℝ) (RTh : DimThermalResistance) : Prop :=
  heatCurrent = -(lambda.valSI.val * wallArea.valSI.val * radialTempGradient.valSI.val) ∧
    heatCurrent = (driveSI ΔT RTh).valSI.val

nodes.title: Least-squares line under an exactly linear law
nodes.statement:
The C.5 graphing step: the fitted slope $s$ and intercept $b$ reproduce
every data point ($y_j = s\,x_j + b$ for each of the $n$ samples) and $s$
equals the least-squares estimator
$\Sigma(x - \bar x)(y - \bar y) / \Sigma(x - \bar x)^2$ — the physical
content of ``the C.5 graph is linear with slope $s$'' without making the
C.6 conclusion an assumption.
nodes.lean_source:
def IsLeastSquaresLine (x y : ℕ → ℝ) (n : ℕ) (s b : ℝ) : Prop :=
  (∀ j : ℕ, j < n → y j = s * x j + b) ∧
    s = (∑ j ∈ Finset.range n,
            (x j - (∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, x k) / n) *
            (y j - (∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, y k) / n)) /
        (∑ j ∈ Finset.range n, (x j - (∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, x k) / n) ^ 2)

nodes.title: Experiment record (E1 Part C)
nodes.statement:
The IPhO 2026 E1 Part-C apparatus and measurement record: the calibrations
$c_0$, $m$, the effective wall resistance $R_{Th} > 0$ (the quantity C.6
determines — its value unconstrained), the temperature records
$T_{IC}, T_{OC}$, the interval-average $\overline{\Delta T}$, the C.4
equilibrium temperature (natural-language prerequisite), the two cooling
models (Eq.\ 4/conservation and Eq.\ 5), the wall material/geometric data
with Fourier's law (Eq.\ 6), the C.5 sample record with $\ge 2$ samples, the
fitted slope $s > 0$ and intercept, positivity of $c_0\,m$, the
non-degeneracy certificate $x_{\mathrm{varies}}$ (the abscissae are not all
equal), the least-squares fit (C.5 prerequisite), and the slope's
\texttt{MeasuredValue} uncertainty readout. The C.6 conclusion appears
nowhere among the fields.
nodes.lean_source:
structure ExperimentC where

  c₀ : DimSpecificHeat

  m : DimMassQ

  RTh : DimThermalResistance

  RTh_pos : 0 < RTh.valSI.val

  TIC : Time → Temperature

  TOC : Time → Temperature

  ΔTavg : Time → Time → WithDim Θ𝓭 ℝ

  T_eq : Temperature

  cooling_model : CoolingModel c₀ m RTh TOC TIC

  finite_difference_model : FiniteDifferenceModel c₀ m RTh TIC ΔTavg

  thermalConductivity : SIQuantity (M𝓭 * L𝓭 * T𝓭⁻¹ * T𝓭⁻¹ * T𝓭⁻¹ * Θ𝓭⁻¹)

  wallArea : SIQuantity (L𝓭 * L𝓭)

  radialTempGradient : SIQuantity (Θ𝓭 * L𝓭⁻¹)

  wallTempDiff : WithDim Θ𝓭 ℝ

  heatCurrent : ℝ

  fourier_law : FourierRadialConductionLaw heatCurrent thermalConductivity
    wallArea radialTempGradient wallTempDiff RTh

  samples : ℕ

  samples_ge : 2 ≤ samples

  xSample : ℕ → ℝ

  ySample : ℕ → ℝ

  slopeC5 : DimC5Slope

  slopeC5_pos : 0 < slopeC5.valSI.val

  heatCapacity_pos : 0 < (innerHeatCapacitySI c₀ m).valSI.val

  interceptC5 : ℝ

  x_varies : ∑ j ∈ Finset.range samples,
      (xSample j - (∑ k ∈ Finset.range samples, xSample k) / samples) ^ 2 ≠ 0

  c5_linear_fit : IsLeastSquaresLine xSample ySample samples slopeC5.valSI.val interceptC5

  slope_readout : MeasuredValue slopeC5.valSI.val

nodes.title: Positive sample count
nodes.statement:
Structural bookkeeping: the record carries a positive sample count, since at
least two measurements are needed for the C.5 graph.
nodes.proof_tex: $0 < 2 \le \texttt{samples}$ by the \texttt{samples\_ge} field.
nodes.lean_source: theorem samples_pos : 0 < E.samples := lt_of_lt_of_le (by norm_num) E.samples_ge

nodes.title: First-point reproduction
nodes.statement:
Data readout: the least-squares line reproduces the first recorded ordinate,
$y_0 = s\,x_0 + b$.
nodes.proof_tex:
Pure unfolding of the C.5 fit hypothesis at index $0$ (valid since
$0 < \texttt{samples}$); a helper expansion, not the C.6 answer.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem c5_first_point : E.ySample 0 = E.slopeC5.valSI.val * E.xSample 0 + E.interceptC5 :=
  E.c5_linear_fit.1 0 E.samples_pos

nodes.title: Dimensional correctness of the slope--resistance inversion
nodes.statement:
Physical bridge on the dimensional side: the product
$(c_0\,m)\,R_{Th}$ has the action dimension $\mathrm{J\,s} =
\mathsf{M}\mathsf{L}^2\mathsf{T}^{-2}\Theta^{-1}\cdot
\Theta\mathsf{T}^3\mathsf{L}^{-2}\mathsf{M}^{-1}$
which reduces to $\mathsf{T}$ — so the graphed slope
$s = 1/(c_0\,m\,R_{Th})$ carries $\mathsf{T}^{-1}$, certifying the
dimensional arithmetic of the C.6 inversion.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem slope_inversion_is_dimensionally_correct :
    (M𝓭 * L𝓭 * L𝓭 * T𝓭⁻¹ * T𝓭⁻¹ * Θ𝓭⁻¹ * (Θ𝓭 * T𝓭 ^ 3 * L𝓭⁻¹ * L𝓭⁻¹ * M𝓭⁻¹) :
        Dimension) =
      T𝓭 := by
  ext <;> dim_component

nodes.title: C.6 main target: wall resistance from the C.5 graph
nodes.statement:
From the governing cooling model, its finite-difference form on the
measurement intervals, and the calibrated linear C.5 graph readout, the
effective wall thermal resistance is determined by the C.5 slope as
$R_{Th} = 1/(c_0\,m\,s)$ (equality of real SI values, kelvin per watt);
multiplied through, this is the source form $c_0\,m\,s\,R_{Th} = 1$.
nodes.proof_tex:
Differentiate/average the \texttt{CoolingModel} and read it against the
\texttt{FiniteDifferenceModel}: the graph's ordinate per unit abscissa is
$1/(c_0\,m\,R_{Th})$, which the least-squares fit identifies with the
fitted slope $s$ (the \texttt{x\_varies} field rules out a degenerate fit);
invert using $R_{Th} > 0$, $s > 0$, $c_0 m > 0$. Conclusion side only.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem wall_thermal_resistance_from_C5 (E : ExperimentC) :
    E.RTh.valSI.val =
      1 / ((innerHeatCapacitySI E.c₀ E.m).valSI.val * E.slopeC5.valSI.val) := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Exact inversion key
nodes.statement:
The central model value $R_0 = 1/(c_0\,m\,s)$ obeys the recorded identity
$(c_0\,m)\,s\,R_0 = 1$ exactly, for any nonzero $c_0 m$ and $s$; this
separates the exact algebraic content of the C.6 conclusion from the
uncertainty band of the actual measurement.
nodes.proof_tex:
One division: $x \cdot (1/x) = 1$ for $x = (c_0 m)\,s \ne 0$ (product of
nonzero reals), via Mathlib \texttt{mul\_inv\_cancel₀}.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem cooling_model_inversion_key {cms s : ℝ} (hcms : cms ≠ 0) (hs : s ≠ 0) :
    cms * s * (1 / (cms * s)) = 1 := by
  rw [one_div, mul_inv_cancel₀ (mul_ne_zero hcms hs)]

nodes.title: Uncertainty propagation to C.6
nodes.statement:
For $R_{Th} = 1/(c_0\,m\,s)$ the relative uncertainties add in worst-case
(single-sided) form, $|\delta R/R| = |\delta s/s| + |\delta(c_0 m)/(c_0 m)|$:
a measurand $q$ known within strict relative half-width $u_q < 1/2$, inverted
jointly with the slope $s$ known within $u_s < 1/2$, determines the model
value $1/(q\,s)$ within the relative band $u_s + u_q$ of the central
resistance.
nodes.proof_tex:
Write $|1/(q s) - 1/(c\,m\,s)| = |(c m - q)/(q\,c m\,s)|$; the strict
bands bound the denominator away from zero (each budget $< 1/2$), and the
worst-case addition of the budgets closes the estimate. Certified interval
arithmetic is left to the prover stage.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem uncertainty_propagates_to_resistance
    {q c mval s R uq us δq : ℝ}
    (hq : 0 < q) (hs : 0 < s) (hc : 0 < c) (hm : 0 < mval) (hR : 0 < R)
    (hkey : R = 1 / (c * mval * s))
    (hband : δq = q * uq)
    (hbudget : uq < 1 / 2) (hslope : us < 1 / 2)
    (huq_nn : 0 ≤ uq) (hus_nn : 0 ≤ us) :
    |1 / (q * s) - R| ≤ R * (us + uq) := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Official sample value
nodes.statement:
The recorded official answer $R_{Th} = 1.17 \pm 0.03$ K/W is consistent with
the official sample run's microdata (C.5 rate-slope
$a = (2.28 \pm 0.06){\cdot}10^{-3}$ 1/s, water mass $m = (89 \pm 1)$ g,
$c_0 = 4186$ J/(kg\cdot K) exact): the model value
$1/(4186 \cdot 0.089 \cdot 2.28{\cdot}10^{-3}) \approx 1.177$ K/W lies
inside the recorded band (deviation $\approx 0.007 \le 0.03$).
nodes.proof_tex:
Numerical evaluation of the inversion at the sample microdata against the
recorded band; certified interval arithmetic is left to the prover stage.
(Provenance caveat: the microdata citation rests on the official-solution
material quoted by the iter-004 lane; the source PDF is absent from this
checkout — arithmetic independently re-verified by the iter-004 review.)
nodes.lean_source:
theorem official_sample_value :
    ∃ (R : DimThermalResistance) (δ : ℝ),
      R.valSI.val = 1.17 ∧ δ = 0.03 ∧
        |R.valSI.val - 1 / ((4186 : ℝ) * (0.089 : ℝ) * (2.28e-3 : ℝ))| ≤ δ := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Official sample uncertainty budget
nodes.statement:
The recorded half-width $0.03$ K/W dominates the official sample's mean-error
budget $1.17 \cdot (\Delta a/a + \Delta m/m)/2$
($= 1.17 \cdot (0.06/2.28 + 1/89)/2 \approx 0.022$; the $/2$ combining
convention is the official practice for the independent graphical and scale
readouts and is documented load-bearing: the worst-case full sum
$\approx 0.044$ would exceed the band).
nodes.proof_tex:
Direct numerical comparison of the budget against $0.03$; certified interval
arithmetic is left to the prover stage.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem official_sample_uncertainty :
    1.17 * ((0.06 / 2.28 : ℝ) + (1 / 89 : ℝ)) / 2 ≤ (0.03 : ℝ) := by
  sorry

nodes.title: Physics formalization target
nodes.statement: The assigned autoformalize agent should translate this physics problem into Lean declarations in the covered file, with theorem and lemma proof bodies written as `by sorry`.
nodes.proof_tex: This is an autoformalization task, not a proof task. Produce faithful statements that can later be proved without weakening the source contract.

nodes.title: Thermal experiment readout data
nodes.statement:
The scalar experiment readout package in SI units: the effective wall
thermal resistance $R_{Th}$ (K/W) measured in part C.6 as
$1.17 \pm 0.03\ \mathrm{K/W}$ (of which only the interval is used here),
together with the recorded water temperatures $T_{IC}$ and $T_{OC}$ (K) of
the inner and outer cylinders. This is readout content: it carries no
governing law --- Equation (4) lives instead in
\cref{def:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_4_C_7:LumpedHeatFlowLaw}.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure ThermalExperimentData where

  R_Th : ℝ

  T_IC : ℝ

  T_OC : ℝ

nodes.title: Cylindrical wall geometry and lateral area
nodes.statement:
The Figure-17 geometry of the acrylic wall separating the two cylinders:
inner radius $r_1 = 33.7/2\ \mathrm{mm} = 16.85\ \mathrm{mm}$ (the IC
bore radius), outer radius $r_2 = r_1 + 6.4\ \mathrm{mm} = 23.25$
mm (wall thickness $6.4 \pm 0.1\ \mathrm{mm}$), and wetted
wall height $h = 10\ \mathrm{cm}$, the IC water level of Procedure
step 3; lengths are stored in metres with certificates $0 < r_1$,
$r_1 < r_2$, $0 < h$. The folded projection \texttt{lateralArea} is the
lateral cylinder area $A(r) = 2\pi r h$ at radius $r$ --- the area $A$
appearing in Fourier's law (6) for radial conduction through a slim wall.
All geometry entries are figure/procedure readouts (assumption side).
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure CylindricalWallGeometry where

  r₁ : ℝ

  r₂ : ℝ

  h : ℝ
  r₁_pos : 0 < r₁
  r₁_lt_r₂ : r₁ < r₂
  h_pos : 0 < h

noncomputable def lateralArea (G : CylindricalWallGeometry) (r : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  2 * π * r * G.h

nodes.title: Lumped heat-flow law, Eq.\ (4)
nodes.statement:
Equation (4) of the problem, the lumped heat-flow model: the heat received
by the IC water through the wall per unit time is
$P = (T_{OC} - T_{IC})/R_{Th}$. Taken as a modeling hypothesis (governing
law) on an already-given current $P$; it is not the definition of
$R_{Th}$ nor of $P$.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
def LumpedHeatFlowLaw (D : ThermalExperimentData) (P : ℝ) : Prop :=
  P = (D.T_OC - D.T_IC) / D.R_Th

nodes.title: Radial Fourier conduction, Eq.\ (6)
nodes.statement:
Steady 1-D radial Fourier conduction through the slim cylindrical wall:
the \texttt{steady} field (the pump homogenizes the water temperatures, so
the profile is stationary) asserts constancy of the outward heat current
$P(r)$ across the whole wall $r \in [r_1, r_2]$, and the
\texttt{fourier} field is Fourier's law (6) at every radius,
$P(r) = -\lambda\,A(r)\,\mathrm{d}T/\mathrm{d}r$ with
$A(r) = 2\pi r h$. An assumed governing-law structure; the C.7 answer
never appears among its fields.
nodes.proof_tex: Definition; no claim.
nodes.lean_source:
structure RadialFourierConduction
    (G : CylindricalWallGeometry) (lam : ℝ)
    (T : ℝ → ℝ) (P : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop where

  steady : ∀ r ∈ Set.Icc G.r₁ G.r₂, ∀ r' ∈ Set.Icc G.r₁ G.r₂, P r = P r'

  fourier : ∀ r ∈ Set.Icc G.r₁ G.r₂,
    P r = -lam * G.lateralArea r * deriv T r

nodes.title: Constancy of the wall heat current
nodes.statement:
The constant wall heat current delivered by the steady state: for any two
radii $r, r' \in [r_1, r_2]$ inside the wall, $P(r) = P(r')$. This is the
eliminable content that the C.7 derivation integrates against.
nodes.proof_tex:
Direct application of the \texttt{steady} field of the
radial-Fourier-conduction witness at the two radii --- an intentional
projection extracting the constant-current value.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem wall_current {G : CylindricalWallGeometry} {lam : ℝ}
    {T P : ℝ → ℝ} (hF : RadialFourierConduction G lam T P)
    {r r' : ℝ} (hr : r ∈ Set.Icc G.r₁ G.r₂)
    (hr' : r' ∈ Set.Icc G.r₁ G.r₂) : P r = P r' :=
  hF.steady r hr r' hr'

nodes.title: C.7 derivation formula: acrylic conductivity from the data
nodes.statement:
Combining the lumped heat-flow law (4) with steady radial Fourier
conduction (6) through the wall $[r_1, r_2]$, imposing the boundary
temperatures $T(r_1) = T_{IC}$, $T(r_2) = T_{OC}$ and the drive
$T_{IC} < T_{OC}$ (with $R_{Th} \ne 0$, $\lambda \ne 0$), the acrylic
conductivity is
\[ \lambda \;=\; \frac{\ln(r_2/r_1)}{2\pi h\,R_{Th}}. \]
This is the recorded C.7 answer formula --- the conclusion of the
derivation, never a hypothesis.
nodes.proof_tex:
Constancy and positivity of $P = (T_{OC}-T_{IC})/R_{Th} > 0$ give
$\mathrm{d}T/\mathrm{d}r < 0$ (outward-decreasing profile, so the
derivative exists almost everywhere on $(r_1, r_2)$); integrating
$P/(2\pi\lambda h r) = -\mathrm{d}T/\mathrm{d}r$ over $[r_1, r_2]$ yields
$P\ln(r_2/r_1)/(2\pi\lambda h) = T_{IC} - T_{OC}$ via
$\int r^{-1} = \ln$; substituting Eq.\ (4) for $P$ and solving for
$\lambda$ gives the claimed formula. The certified integration is the
sorried proof body left to the prover stage.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem acrylicConductivity_formula
    (G : CylindricalWallGeometry) (D : ThermalExperimentData)
    (lam : ℝ) (T : ℝ → ℝ) (P : ℝ → ℝ)
    (hflow : LumpedHeatFlowLaw D (P G.r₁))
    (hfourier : RadialFourierConduction G lam T P)
    (hR : D.R_Th ≠ 0) (hlam : lam ≠ 0)
    (hT_inner : T G.r₁ = D.T_IC) (hT_outer : T G.r₂ = D.T_OC)
    (hΔT : D.T_IC < D.T_OC) :
    lam = Real.log (G.r₂ / G.r₁) / (2 * π * G.h * D.R_Th) := by
  sorry

nodes.title: C.7 official sample value with propagated uncertainty
nodes.statement:
For $\lambda$ given by the C.7 formula at the official sample inputs ---
the C.6 central measurement $R_{Th} = 1.17\ \mathrm{K/W}$, the Figure-17
geometry $r_2/r_1 = 23.25/16.85$ and wetted height $h = 0.10$
m --- the official sample report
$\lambda = 0.25 \pm 0.01\ \mathrm{W/(m\cdot K)}$ holds:
$\lvert \lambda - 0.25 \rvert \le 0.01$. The official band lives only
here, on the conclusion side; the formula itself is taken as the
hypothesis \texttt{hformula} because
\cref{thm:IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_4_C_7:acrylicConductivity_formula}
is proved independently.
nodes.proof_tex:
Direct numerical evaluation of the formula at $R_{Th} = 1.17$:
$\ln(23.25/16.85)/(2\pi \cdot 0.10 \cdot 1.17) \approx 0.25$
W/(m$\cdot$K), inside the recorded $\pm 0.01$ window; certified
interval/refinement arithmetic is the sorried proof body left to the
prover stage.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem acrylicConductivity_officialSample
    (lam R_Th : ℝ)
    (hformula : lam = Real.log ((23.25e-3 : ℝ) / 16.85e-3) /
      (2 * π * (0.10 : ℝ) * R_Th))
    (hR_central : R_Th = 1.17) (hR_uncert : |R_Th - 1.17| ≤ 0.03) :
    |lam - 0.25| ≤ 0.01 := by
  sorry

nodes.title: IPhO2026.Problem1.B1.CoulombPairData
nodes.lean_source:
structure CoulombPairData (hR : ScalingRegime) where

  reduced_mass : ℝ

  total_angular_momentum : ℝ

  total_energy : ℝ

  initial_separation : ℝ

  initial_speed : ℝ

  reduced_mass_eq : reduced_mass = particleMass / 2

  initial_separation_value :
    initial_separation = initialSeparationInBohrRadii * bohrRadius

  angular_momentum_per_particle :
    particleMass * initial_speed * (initial_separation / 2) = boundMu * hbar

  total_angular_momentum_eq :
    total_angular_momentum =
      2 * (particleMass * initial_speed * (initial_separation / 2))

  relative_kinetic :
    2 * ((1 / 2) * particleMass * initial_speed ^ 2) =
      (1 / 2) * reduced_mass * (2 * initial_speed) ^ 2

  coulomb_law :
    total_energy =
      2 * ((1 / 2) * particleMass * initial_speed ^ 2) -
        coulombK * elementaryCharge ^ 2 / initial_separation

  orbit_support :
    ∃ O : Set ℝ,
      O.Nonempty ∧
        (∀ r ∈ O,
          0 < r ∧
            total_energy * r ^ 2 + coulombK * elementaryCharge ^ 2 * r -
                total_angular_momentum ^ 2 / (2 * reduced_mass) ≤ 0)

  turning_100 :
    total_energy * initial_separation ^ 2 +
        coulombK * elementaryCharge ^ 2 * initial_separation -
          total_angular_momentum ^ 2 / (2 * reduced_mass) = 0

  bound_branch : total_energy < 0

nodes.title: IPhO2026.Problem1.B1.CoulombPairData.AnchoredValues
nodes.lean_source:
structure AnchoredValues {hR : ScalingRegime} (D : CoulombPairData hR) :
    Prop where

  total_angular_momentum_value :
    D.total_angular_momentum = 2 * boundMu * hbar

  speed_value :
    particleMass * D.initial_speed * (D.initial_separation / 2) =
      boundMu * hbar

  reduced_mass_pos : 0 < D.reduced_mass

  initial_separation_pos : 0 < D.initial_separation

nodes.title: IPhO2026.Problem1.B1.CoulombPairData.attainedSeparations
nodes.lean_source:
def attainedSeparations : Set ℝ :=
  { r : ℝ | 0 < r ∧ D.turningQuadratic r ≤ 0 }

nodes.title: IPhO2026.Problem1.B1.CoulombPairData.attainedSeparations_lt_energy_threshold
nodes.lean_source:
theorem attainedSeparations_lt_energy_threshold {hR : ScalingRegime}
    (D : CoulombPairData hR) (hm : 0 < D.reduced_mass) {r : ℝ}
    (hr : r ∈ D.attainedSeparations) :
    r < coulombK * elementaryCharge ^ 2 / (-D.total_energy) := by
  rcases hr with ⟨hr_pos, hrQ⟩
  by_contra hcontra
  push_neg at hcontra
  have hpos := D.quadratic_pos_of_large hm hcontra
  linarith [hrQ, hpos]

nodes.title: IPhO2026.Problem1.B1.CoulombPairData.attainedSeparations_nonempty
nodes.lean_source:
theorem attainedSeparations_nonempty : D.attainedSeparations.Nonempty :=
  (Classical.choose_spec D.orbit_support).1.mono D.orbit_subset_attainedSeparations

nodes.title: IPhO2026.Problem1.B1.CoulombPairData.initial_separation_attained
nodes.lean_source:
theorem initial_separation_attained :
    D.initial_separation ∈ D.attainedSeparations := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [D.initial_separation_value]
    have : 0 < initialSeparationInBohrRadii * bohrRadius :=
      mul_pos (by norm_num [initialSeparationInBohrRadii]) hR.bohrRadius_pos
    exact this
  · rw [turningQuadratic]
    rw [D.turning_100]

nodes.title: IPhO2026.Problem1.B1.CoulombPairData.mem_attainedSeparations_iff
nodes.lean_source:
theorem mem_attainedSeparations_iff (r : ℝ) :
    r ∈ D.attainedSeparations ↔ 0 < r ∧ D.turningQuadratic r ≤ 0 :=
  Iff.rfl

nodes.title: IPhO2026.Problem1.B1.CoulombPairData.orbit_subset_attainedSeparations
nodes.lean_source:
theorem orbit_subset_attainedSeparations :
    Classical.choose D.orbit_support ⊆ D.attainedSeparations :=
  fun _ hr =>
    ⟨(Classical.choose_spec D.orbit_support).2 _ hr |>.1,
      D.quadratic_nonpos_of_orbit hr⟩

nodes.title: IPhO2026.Problem1.B1.CoulombPairData.quadratic_nonpos_of_orbit
nodes.lean_source:
theorem quadratic_nonpos_of_orbit {r : ℝ}
    (hr : r ∈ Classical.choose D.orbit_support) :
    D.turningQuadratic r ≤ 0 :=
  ((Classical.choose_spec D.orbit_support).2 r hr).2

nodes.title: IPhO2026.Problem1.B1.CoulombPairData.quadratic_pos_of_large
nodes.lean_source:
theorem quadratic_pos_of_large {hR : ScalingRegime} (D : CoulombPairData hR)
    (hm : 0 < D.reduced_mass) {r : ℝ}
    (hr : coulombK * elementaryCharge ^ 2 / (-D.total_energy) ≤ r) :
    0 < D.turningQuadratic r := by
  have hE : D.total_energy < 0 := D.bound_branch
  have hneg : 0 < -D.total_energy := neg_pos.mpr hE
  have he : elementaryCharge ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt hR.elementaryCharge_pos
  have hnum_pos : 0 < coulombK * elementaryCharge ^ 2 :=
    mul_pos hR.coulombK_pos (sq_pos_of_ne_zero he)
  have hr_pos : 0 < r := lt_of_lt_of_le (div_pos hnum_pos hneg) hr
  have hnn : 0 ≤ coulombK * elementaryCharge ^ 2 := le_of_lt hnum_pos
  have hkey : 0 ≤ D.total_energy * r + coulombK * elementaryCharge ^ 2 := by
    have hmul : coulombK * elementaryCharge ^ 2 ≤ r * (-D.total_energy) := by
      have h := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hr (le_of_lt hneg)
      rwa [div_mul_cancel₀ _ (ne_of_gt hneg)] at h
    have hcast : D.total_energy * r = -(r * (-D.total_energy)) := by ring
    rw [hcast]
    nlinarith [hmul]
  have hL : 0 < D.total_angular_momentum ^ 2 / (2 * D.reduced_mass) := by
    by_contra hnotpos
    push_neg at hnotpos
    have hinit_pos : 0 < D.initial_separation := by
      rw [D.initial_separation_value]
      exact mul_pos (by norm_num [initialSeparationInBohrRadii]) hR.bohrRadius_pos
    have hterm : D.total_energy * D.initial_separation ^ 2 < 0 :=
      mul_neg_of_neg_of_pos hE (sq_pos_of_pos hinit_pos)
    have hcoul : 0 < coulombK * elementaryCharge ^ 2 * D.initial_separation :=
      mul_pos hnum_pos hinit_pos
    have hnonneg_L : 0 ≤ D.total_angular_momentum ^ 2 / (2 * D.reduced_mass) :=
      div_nonneg (sq_nonneg _) (by linarith [hm])
    have hL0 : D.total_angular_momentum ^ 2 / (2 * D.reduced_mass) = 0 :=
      le_antisymm hnotpos hnonneg_L
    have hturn := D.turning_100
    rw [hL0] at hturn
    simp only [sub_zero] at hturn
    linarith [hturn, hterm, hcoul]
  have hexpand : D.turningQuadratic r =
      r * (D.total_energy * r + coulombK * elementaryCharge ^ 2)
        - D.total_angular_momentum ^ 2 / (2 * D.reduced_mass) := by
    rw [turningQuadratic]; ring
  rw [hexpand]
  have hnonneg : 0 ≤ r * (D.total_energy * r + coulombK * elementaryCharge ^ 2) :=
    mul_nonneg (le_of_lt hr_pos) hkey
  linarith [hL, hnonneg]

theorem attainedSeparations_subset_Icc_abstract {hR : ScalingRegime}
    (D : CoulombPairData hR) {r : ℝ} (hr : r ∈ D.attainedSeparations)
    {x₁ x₂ : ℝ} (_hx₁₂ : x₁ < x₂)
    (hfact : ∀ x : ℝ, 0 < x →
      D.turningQuadratic (x * bohrRadius) ≤ 0 → x₁ ≤ x ∧ x ≤ x₂) :
    x₁ * bohrRadius ≤ r ∧ r ≤ x₂ * bohrRadius := by
  rcases hr with ⟨hr_pos, hrQ⟩
  have ha := hR.bohrRadius_pos
  obtain ⟨x, rfl : r = x * bohrRadius, hx⟩ : ∃ x : ℝ, r = x * bohrRadius ∧ 0 < x :=
    ⟨r / bohrRadius, by field_simp, by positivity⟩
  rcases hfact x hx hrQ with ⟨h1, h2⟩
  constructor
  · nlinarith [ha]
  · nlinarith [ha]

    (100 / x) ^ 2 - (100 / 100 + 100 / (1600 / 9)) * (100 / x) +
        (100 / 100) * (100 / (1600 / 9)) =
      (100 / x - 1) * (100 / x - 9 / 16) := by
  have hx' : (100 : ℝ) / x ≠ 0 := by positivity
  field_simp
  ring

      IsMaxSeparationAlongOrbit D r_max ∧ r_max = (1600 / 9) * bohrRadius := by
  refine ⟨(1600 / 9) * bohrRadius, ⟨⟨?_, ?_⟩, rfl⟩⟩

nodes.title: IPhO2026.Problem1.B1.turning_root_cases
nodes.lean_source:
theorem turning_root_cases {hR : ScalingRegime} (D : CoulombPairData hR)
    {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 < x)
    (hroot :
      (100 / x) ^ 2 - (100 / 100 + 100 / (1600 / 9)) * (100 / x) +
          (100 / 100) * (100 / (1600 / 9)) = 0) :
    x = 100 ∨ x = 1600 / 9 := by
  rw [certified_factorization (hR := hR) (_D := D) x hx] at hroot
  rcases mul_eq_zero.mp hroot with h | h
  · have : (100 : ℝ) / x = 1 := by linarith
    have hx0 : x ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt hx
    field_simp at this
    left
    linarith [this]
  · have : (100 : ℝ) / x = 9 / 16 := by linarith
    have hx0 : x ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt hx
    field_simp at this
    right
    nlinarith [this]
